articles.title: Carrick hurt by Old Trafford boos as Manchester United’s poor start continues
articles.summary: Fans were less than impressed by Man Utd's display
articles.content:
Carrick hurt by Old Trafford boos as Manchester United’s poor start continues

Fans were less than impressed by Man Utd's display

Last Update:

Michael Carrick admitted he was hurt by boos from sections of the Manchester United supporters after slipping to a late 1-1 draw at home to winless Tottenham.

Dominic Solanke’s late header cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo’s finish at Old Trafford in a game where the visitors enjoyed many of the better chances, with some supporters making their feelings known at half-time and full-time with audible boos.

“It’s not nice,” Carrick told Sky Sports.

“It hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

Carrick admitted United were poor in the first half but felt they grew into the game and acknowledged that late goals are affecting them significantly.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through.

“We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.

“I don’t think it is lack of confidence, but a game can get away from you very quickly. We found a way right back into the game, and got ourselves in a great position – that is one of the most disappointing things.”

Match Statistics

Mbeumo: First half wasn’t us

Goalscorer Mbeumo said United’s first half was not up to scratch but was keen to take the positives from the draw.

He added: “We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

articles.title: De Zerbi ‘happy’ after seeing ‘right spirit’ as Spurs climb off bottom but winless start continues
articles.summary: Spurs climbed off the bottom of the table but are still winless
articles.content:
De Zerbi ‘happy’ after seeing ‘right spirit’ as Spurs climb off bottom but winless start continues

Spurs climbed off the bottom of the table but are still winless

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi was pleased with Tottenham’s display at Manchester United after fighting back with 10 men to earn a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford.

Dominic Solanke scored a header in the second minute of added time to earn a point they were good value for after seeing a host of excellent chances missed against the Red Devils, who went ahead through Bryan Mbeumo.

Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card meant Spurs had to show even more spirit to get back into the game, and De Zerbi was pleased to take the positives despite their winless start to the season ultimately stretch to six games.

De Zerbi told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four.

“The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat.

“We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

De Zerbi: ‘There aren’t too many strikers better than Solanke’

De Zerbi was full of praise for goalscorer Solanke, who was selected as captain for the game at Old Trafford, and insisted there are few better No9s in the league after opening his account for the season.

The Italian added: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke.

“Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Ipswich pile more misery on Fulham as Brighton charge on with win over Sunderland

Catch up with the best of the action from the Premier League's afternoon games.

Last Update:

Sunderland 0-2 Brighton

Brighton overcame a second-half red card to beat Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light, with Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scoring for the visitors.

The Seagulls played more than 30 minutes with 10 men after Pascal Struijk was sent off, but Sunderland failed to capitalise on their numerical advantage.

Both sides struck the woodwork during an entertaining first half. Wilson Isidor turned Enzo Le Fee’s cross against the post before Struijk headed Pascal Gross’ free-kick onto the upright shortly before the interval.

Brighton broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute when Gross collected a quick throw-in and found De Cuyper, who took a touch before finishing past Robin Roefs.

However, the visitors suffered a setback four minutes later when Struijk was dismissed following a VAR review for denying Isidor a goalscoring opportunity.

Sunderland pushed forward in search of an equaliser, with Granit Xhaka testing Bart Verbruggen from a free-kick before Malick Fofana saw an effort comfortably saved.

Brighton defended well despite their numerical disadvantage and sealed the win in stoppage time.

Substitute Georginio Rutter released Hadjam down the left, and the defender marked his Premier League debut with a composed finish across Roefs to secure all three points.

Ipswich 2-1 Fulham

Ipswich scored twice in the closing minutes to secure a 2-1 win over Fulham at Portman Road, with Dara O’Shea heading home the winner in stoppage time.

Fulham had looked set for their first Premier League win under Alvaro Arbeloa after Ryan Sessegnon’s superb strike, but Gary O’Neil’s side produced a remarkable comeback.

The visitors enjoyed the better chances before half-time, with Christian Walton denying Sander Berge before Gonzalo Garcia dragged an effort wide.

Fulham eventually broke the deadlock in the 55th minute when Sessegnon collected a half-clearance from Issa Diop and fired a brilliant left-footed effort into the bottom corner.

Ipswich responded strongly, with Emersonn heading against the post before Bernd Leno produced an excellent save to deny Sindre Walle Egeli.

The hosts finally equalised in the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara controlled Calvin Bassey’s clearance and hammered a stunning long-range strike past Leno.

Three minutes later, Jack Clarke delivered a dangerous free-kick and O’Shea headed home at the near post to complete the turnaround.

Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal response against Leeds – ‘We had to restore our identity’

Mikel Arteta has spoken after Arsenal's win over Leeds.

Last Update:

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta praised his side for restoring their identity after coming from behind to beat Leeds United in the Premier League on Saturday.

The Gunners fell behind in the early kick-off at the Emirates Stadium but recovered to secure an important victory against a Leeds side who had arrived in North London unbeaten in the league this season.

Arteta admitted he had been unhappy with Arsenal’s previous performance against Brighton and challenged his players to produce a response.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, the Spaniard insisted his squad had delivered exactly the reaction he wanted, reserving particular praise for the substitutes who helped turn the game around.

“Before the game we talked about two things,” he said.

“One, the challenge ahead because Leeds had not lost in the Premier League and it was going to be really tough.

“And second one, to restore our identity and be ourselves again, regardless of the context of the match.

“We weren’t pleased against Brighton and today was an opportunity to put that right. We certainly reacted in the manner we expected.”

Arsenal substitutes praised for changing Leeds clash

Arteta highlighted Arsenal’s equaliser as the moment that shifted the momentum of the match.

With Leeds having taken the lead in the lunchtime kick-off, the home crowd needed a response from their team.

“When you play 12:30 at home and you go 1-0 down, you have to restore a lot of things,” Arteta explained.

“The energy is one of them. We had a incredible response, you could sense the crowd, the energy changed immediately.

“The finishers come in and made a huge difference to help us win the game.

“We bring a lot of leadership on in those three players,” he said.

“Goal threat, players that can win duels, can play forward and penetrate against this high press.”

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended by Portugal after Jorge Jesus fallout as federation opens investigation
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended by Portugal.
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo suspended by Portugal after Jorge Jesus fallout as federation opens investigation

Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended by Portugal.

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened following his controversial departure from the national team.

The 41-year-old left Portugal’s squad during the recent international break after a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus over his playing time.

Ronaldo subsequently apologised to his team-mates and supporters, admitting he had been wrong to leave the camp and insisting he would accept any punishment imposed by the federation.

However, the FPF has now confirmed that an investigation is underway, with the Portugal captain facing an uncertain international future while the disciplinary process continues.

“Disciplinary proceedings have been initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro, following a decision by the Non-Professional Section on October 9, 2026,” the federation said in a statement.

The governing body explained that Ronaldo had initially been placed under an automatic provisional suspension before a further suspension was imposed.

The case has also been classified as “urgent”, although no timeframe has been provided for a final ruling.

Ronaldo scores 980th career goal on Al-Nassr return

While his international future remains uncertain, Ronaldo has already returned to action for Al-Nassr.

The Portuguese forward scored on Friday as Postecoglou’s side secured a 3-0 victory over Diriyah in the Saudi Pro League.

Ronaldo opened the scoring after Kingsley Coman’s effort from outside the penalty area was saved by goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah.

The 41-year-old reacted quickest to the rebound and finished from close range to register the 980th goal of his professional career.

The victory moved defending champions Al-Nassr level on points with league leaders Al-Qadsiah after eight rounds of fixtures, although they remain behind on goal difference.

Postecoglou had previously insisted Ronaldo was in good spirits following his return from international duty and declined to comment on the disagreement with Jesus.

“Ronaldo played for us with full commitment and his morale is very high,” the Australian said earlier this week.

“I’m his coach now at Al Nassr, and he is a great addition to our team.

“I don’t like to talk about what happened with his national team.”

BREAKING: Cole Palmer signs new Chelsea contract

Cole Palmer has signed a new contract at Chelsea.

Last Update:

Cole Palmer has signed a new Chelsea contract until 2034, with the England international rewarded with improved terms following his impressive performances at Stamford Bridge.

The 24-year-old was already tied to the club until 2033 but has agreed another extension.

Palmer has established himself as a key figure in Chelsea’s attack since arriving from Manchester City for £42.5million in 2023.

The new agreement means Palmer now holds one of the longest contracts in the Premier League, with Manchester City’s Erling Haaland and Chelsea teammates Joao Pedro and Geovany Quenda also contracted until 2034.

Chelsea have made a habit of handing lengthy contracts to their players, allowing the club to protect their value while maintaining a structured approach to wages.

Joao Pedro signed a new deal until 2034 in August, while Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month.

Alonso provides Palmer fitness update after England absence

Despite his impressive start to the season, Palmer continues to be managed carefully following the groin injury that troubled him throughout the previous campaign.

The midfielder previously admitted that he had continued playing through the problem when he “probably shouldn’t have done”.

His fitness issues eventually contributed to his omission from England’s World Cup squad during the summer, having previously sought specialist advice over whether surgery would be necessary.

Palmer has played more minutes than any other Chelsea player this season but missed England’s latest international fixtures.

articles.content:
European football results today: La Liga, Bundesliga, and Ligue 1 scores, highlights

The latest results from Spain, Germany and France

Last Update:

There were matches across Spain, Germany and France on Friday as players returned from the September and October international break.

Five of the nine goals across the leagues came after the 84th minute, including two to change the outcome of games during second-half added time.

Borussia Dortmund failed to win for the first time this season, while Malaga are no longer adrift at the foot of the table in Spain.

Lyon missed out on the win Paulo Fonseca’s side required to displace Monaco at the top in France and have now played a game more than their rivals.

Bundesliga results: Borussia Dortmund vs Werder Bremen

Bremen goalkeeper Karl Hein made a string of outstanding saves before Daniel Svensson slid in to put Bundesliga leaders Dortmund in front in the 80th minute, with Nico Schlotterbeck’s header doubling their advantage five minutes later.

Just when Bremen looked beaten, Ludovit Reis struck via a post from long range to give them hope with two minutes remaining. West Ham loanee Niclas Fullkrug then equalised with a 92nd-minute header as the visitors moved fourth.

Dortmund are three points clear of second-placed Bayern Munich, who visit fifth-placed Augsburg on Saturday (14:30 BST). Take a look at the full Bundesliga table.

La Liga results: Malaga vs Espanyol

On-loan Bayern winger Bryan Zaragoza ended a mazy run by giving Espanyol an early lead at Malaga, putting his side on course to move eighth in La Liga at the expense of opponents without a win in their first seven league games.

Pablo Martinez sent a free-kick from an outlandish distance against the crossbar on the hour mark as Malaga pursued an equaliser they found through Adrian Nino’s clever volley inside the box in the 93rd minute.

Malaga are level on points with second-bottom Valencia and a point from safety. Espanyol are 11th, an equidistant three points between sixth and 18th. The full table is on La Liga’s website.

Ligue 1 results: Lens vs Lyon

Veteran forward Florian Sotoca’s volley from inside the penalty area gave Lens a half-time lead under new manager Yannick Cahuzac in Ligue 1.

Matthieu Udol headed in Florian Thauvin’s delivery for the second-half equaliser but was then sent off for a mistimed challenge on Khalis Merah, whose finish pulled one back shortly afterwards.

Lens are seventh, while Lyon suffered their first defeat of the season and could be overtaken this weekend by four teams, including Paris Saint-Germain. You can find the Ligue 1 standings here.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany opens up on painful Musiala situation after Bayern Munich star suffers another injury
articles.summary: Jamal Musiala is set for my time on the injury table.
articles.content:
Vincent Kompany opens up on painful Musiala situation after Bayern Munich star suffers another injury

Jamal Musiala is set for my time on the injury table.

Last Update:

Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has backed Jamal Musiala to overcome his latest injury setback after the Germany international suffered a muscle tear while on international duty.

The 23-year-old sustained what Bayern have described as a “minor” muscle tear while warming up for Germany’s Nations League clash against the Netherlands on September 24.

It represents another frustrating setback for Musiala, who has already missed three of Bayern’s opening seven matches this season following a difficult pre-season.

Speaking ahead of Bayern’s Bundesliga clash with Augsburg on Saturday, Kompany expressed his sympathy for Musiala and drew comparisons with his own experiences as a player.

“I can relate to his story of setbacks,” Kompany said.

“I’ve experienced that often in my own career. Coming back from that is a great strength.

“I hope he can enjoy playing football again in the coming years, and I believe he will. Once you learn how to come back from moments like these, you carry that ability with you for the rest of your life.

“In every situation, he knows how to fight his way back and he always comes back.

“We’ve seen how happy the team and fans are when he scores a goal. We’ll experience those moments again.”

Bayern looking to maintain unbeaten Bundesliga start

Bayern return from the international break aiming to extend their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season.

Kompany’s side have won six of their opening seven league matches, with a goalless draw against Schalke last month preventing them from maintaining a perfect record.

Their next opponents, Augsburg, have endured a more difficult spell after beginning the campaign strongly.

They have conceded six goals across their last three matches, but Kompany is refusing to underestimate a side that caused Bayern problems last season.

Augsburg were the only team to defeat Bayern in the Bundesliga during the previous campaign, securing a 2-1 victory at the Allianz Arena in January.

“It’s a very important game,” Kompany said.

“We lost a Bundesliga match last year, against Augsburg. It’s still a derby and it’s an away game.

“Augsburg are known for their compact formation and their ability to be very dangerous on the ball.

“They have a lot of individual quality. They have more than people sometimes realise.

“They’ve started the season with momentum. It’s still a derby, the fans are looking forward to it, and so are we.”

articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi delivers Dejan Kulusevski injury update as Tottenham star finally prepares for return
articles.summary: Dejan Kulusevski is closing in on a return to Tottenham after a year-and-a-half with injury.
articles.content:
Roberto De Zerbi delivers Dejan Kulusevski injury update as Tottenham star finally prepares for return

Dejan Kulusevski is closing in on a return to Tottenham after a year-and-a-half with injury.

Last Update:

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi has praised Dejan Kulusevski’s attitude during his injury recovery, describing the Sweden international as an example to the rest of his squad.

Kulusevski has been working towards a return to action after nearly 18 months on the sidelines, with De Zerbi impressed by the midfielder’s commitment throughout his rehabilitation.

The Tottenham boss confirmed that Kulusevski will travel with the squad for Saturday’s Premier League clash against Manchester United, although his involvement will be in a supporting capacity rather than as a player.

De Zerbi also provided updates on James Maddison, Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke ahead of the trip to Old Trafford.

De Zerbi praises Kulusevski’s injury recovery

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, De Zerbi singled out Kulusevski for the professionalism and character he has demonstrated while recovering from injury.

“He is working well. Tomorrow he comes with us for support,” De Zerbi said.

“He is working very well and I think he is an example for everyone.

“Forget the player but the example of how he reacted to the injury, the character he showed this time was an example and reference to everyone.”

Kulusevski’s continued absence has deprived Tottenham of one of their most creative attacking players, with the Sweden international capable of operating both centrally and on the right flank.

Maddison available as Van de Ven and Van Hecke return

Tottenham have received positive news elsewhere, with De Zerbi confirming that both Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke are available for selection.

Van de Ven had suffered a hand injury while representing the Netherlands during the international break, raising concerns about his availability for the trip to Manchester.

However, the defender has been cleared to play.

“They are available to play,” De Zerbi confirmed. “Micky played four games, 90 minutes and JP just three games. The difference is this.

“JP yesterday, wife had twins and emotional aspect we have to consider but he’s available.”

James Maddison is also available despite experiencing another minor fitness setback.

“He’s available but he lost three, four days at the end of last week and start of this,” De Zerbi explained.

“James is a special player for us. Gallagher, as a 10, also he’s playing well.

“We’re both frustrated because he wants to be on the pitch. Not a big injury and tomorrow he can play but the Premier League is tough and you need to be fit and in the right condition to run and fight.

“He is working well and this is the way.

“The way is to complete three, four, five weeks in a row without feeling pain and problems and then he’s a normal player.”

De Zerbi backs Mateus Fernandes to succeed at Spurs

De Zerbi also discussed summer signing Mateus Fernandes, insisting the midfielder remains an important part of his plans despite needing time to settle at Tottenham.

Fernandes was among the club’s major arrivals during the summer transfer window, with Spurs investing heavily in their squad.

The Italian believes the midfielder has the ability to become a key player but acknowledged that adapting to his new surroundings will take time.

“He’s a great player, he’s one of the best in our team and he needs time to understand the club and come inside the environment of Spurs,” De Zerbi said.

“I have confidence in him.”

articles.title: Chelsea boss Alonso dislikes elongated international break and says it means coaches ‘disconnect’
articles.summary: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is relishing the return of Premier League action with his side facing Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge on Saturday
articles.content:
Chelsea boss Alonso dislikes elongated international break and says it means coaches ‘disconnect’

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is relishing the return of Premier League action with his side facing Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge on Saturday

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso says the international break is “too long” after having three weeks to digest Chelsea’s 3-0 hammering at Brentford.

Alonso’s early promise at Stamford Bridge has dissipated somewhat after a run of three league games without a win, culminating in their horror show at the Gtech Community Stadium on September 18, has left them 10th in the Premier League table.

The Blues boss would have preferred to have had a swifter chance to right the wrongs of that performance but will finally get the chance when Bournemouth visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

He said: “If you ask me which way I prefer, with three weeks or two breaks or one be so long, I prefer the other way. This one you disconnect too much. It’s too long. For the dynamic of a club coach, I prefer the other way.

“We have had time to analyse the game, recover some players and get ready for tomorrow. We need to keep learning, to be in the process, to be able to read the moment, adapt to the situation. From each game, we are learning things. We need to make sure we don’t make the same mistakes again.”

Bournemouth will arrive in West London without a win after five games but Alonso is not expecting an easy afternoon.

“A tough test. So intense, high tempo game, so demanding,” he said. “They know what they’re doing with Marco [Rose] and previously with Andoni [Iraola]. The core of the team is the same. We need to have a good game and we need a win.”

Chelsea midfielder Caicedo to make welcome return

Alonso is likely to be boosted by the return of several key players, including Moises Caicedo, who has managed just 14 minutes this season due to injury.

Alonso said: ”Yes, he is ready to go. Finally. Anyone would miss a player of his quality and importance. We have missed him for sure and we are happy he is back and he feels better. We didn’t want to take risks for Brentford for example but he feels much better.”

Reece James and Joao Pedro are also available while Cole Palmer has shrugged off the knock that led to him withdrawing from the England squad for the recent Nations League games.

“Yes, they have been training. Some earlier than others. Marco Palestra as well. They have trained well and ready to go. For sure, we know they are key players and important,” said Alonso.

On Palmer, he added: “He has trained this week and feels better. The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit and enjoying his game. For the next part we have a good feeling with him and he is feeling better.”

Winger Jamie Gittens is facing a few weeks on the sidelines, though, after sustaining an ankle injury.

articles.title: Michael Carrick admits Manchester City charges have ‘affected me personally’ as United boss demands resolution
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has had his say on Manchester City's guilty charges.
articles.content:
Michael Carrick admits Manchester City charges have ‘affected me personally’ as United boss demands resolution

Michael Carrick has had his say on Manchester City's guilty charges.

Last Update:

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has admitted Manchester City’s financial charges have affected him personally and called for the ongoing case to be resolved as quickly as possible.

City are appealing after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations, with the outcome of that process still to be decided.

Carrick, who spent 12 years playing for Manchester United during City’s rise to prominence, acknowledged that he has questions about the case but was reluctant to discuss potential consequences while the appeal remains ongoing.

Speaking at his latest press conference, Carrick admitted the situation had raised questions that have yet to be fully answered.

“Very difficult to say in many ways,” the United boss said.

“It’s thrown up a lot of questions, some have had answers, some haven’t. As it’s still ongoing, and we don’t how long it’s going to go, there’s only so much I can say.

“Certainly I’ve got my own questions about it, it’s affected me personally in different ways over a period of time.

“But as the case is going now I don’t know where that stands and how it’s going to end up, so we’ll just have to wait and see.”

Carrick was part of the Manchester United side that finished second to City in the 2011-12 Premier League title race, when Sergio Aguero’s stoppage-time winner against Queens Park Rangers secured the championship on goal difference.

He also experienced City’s growing influence in English football throughout the latter stages of his playing career.

“What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone’s benefit is essential.”

Manchester United suffer Patrick Dorgu injury blow

Carrick also provided an update on Manchester United’s injury situation following the international break, confirming that Patrick Dorgu faces several weeks on the sidelines.

The Denmark international was forced off while representing his country and now looks set for an extended absence.

“It’s a bit mixed really through the internationals,” Carrick said.

“Patrick [Dorgu] came off and it looks like he’ll be out probably for a number of weeks.”

United are also monitoring Noussair Mazraoui after the defender suffered a knock while away on international duty.

“Noussair Mazraoui came off and took a knock. He’s not quite right yet, we’ll have to see how he is.”

Carrick provides updates on Rashford, Mainoo and Sesko

There was more encouraging news concerning several other members of the United squad, with Carlos Baleba making progress towards full fitness.

“Carlos Beleba is improving. He’s trained a lot,” Carrick said.

“Amad Diallo has done a little bit of training. Marcus [Rashford] has done a little bit of training. Kobbie [Mainoo] has done a little bit of training.”

However, Benjamin Sesko remains further away from returning to action.

“Benjamin [Sesko] is a little further a way with the issue he’s got. He’ll be a little bit further away.”

articles.title: Arsenal boss Arteta addresses Manchester City’s guilty verdict
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has been talking to the media ahead of Arsenal's return to Premier League action.
articles.content:
Arsenal boss Arteta addresses Manchester City’s guilty verdict

Mikel Arteta has been talking to the media ahead of Arsenal's return to Premier League action.

Last Update:

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has “complete trust” in Manchester City and echoed Enzo Maresca’s view that the club’s previous achievements should not be not tainted despite the fact they have been found guilty of financial doping.

Arteta worked under Pep Guardiola between 2016 and 2019 before landing the top job at the Emirates Stadium.

During their time together, and in the period in which the cheating was committed between 2009 and 2018, City won two Premier League titles, the FA Cup and two EFL Cups.

City have appealed the Independent Commission’s verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing and Arteta was giving little away when asked about the issue prior to Saturday’s home game with Leeds.

He said: “I trust the club now, in the future, always. I completely trust the club.

“Fully understand the question, but I will respect the process. It is still an ongoing process that is not resolved because it has been appealed.

“My position and the club’s position is not to make any further comment until it is resolved.”

Rice, Konsa and Havertz doubts for Arsenal’s game with Leeds

Of more pressing concern to Arteta is an injury list that threatens to deprive him of several key players for the lunchtime clash with Daniel Farke’s men.

Winger Christos Tzolis is definitely out and Arteta said he would have to wait and see whether Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Kai Havertz would be available.

“We have to manage him [Rice] because he’s had a few issues since he came back from the World Cup,” he added. “Hopefully tomorrow he’s available and some others also are in doubt.

“With Kai he had a muscular injury. I spoke to Germany and they sent the player back as normal, Ezri we had good communication with the England camp.

“Tzolis has a muscle injury as he’s going to be out for a few weeks.”

Arteta delighted with new Arsenal deal

Although Arteta must have stewed on Arsenal’s last result during the international break, a 3-0 hammering at Brighton, he did reveal some good news this week with the signing of a new, four-year deal that will make him the highest-paid manager in the Premier League.

He said: “My family are very grateful to be able to enjoy this unbelievable right to continue. I said from the beginning that me and the club wanted the same thing, but I loved the way it was handled.

“I think it is really important. I always said that when you’re negotiating and trying to figure out the future, the most important thing is at the end when you’re about to sign the deal and looking at everyone in the room and seeing so many smiley faces and excitement in their eyes.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Liverpool suffer double injury blow as Iraola confirms two key absences against Manchester City
articles.summary: Liverpool are set to include Lewis Koumas against Manchester City with two of their more senior forwards absent
articles.content:
BREAKING: Liverpool suffer double injury blow as Iraola confirms two key absences against Manchester City

Liverpool are set to include Lewis Koumas against Manchester City with two of their more senior forwards absent

Last Update:

Neither Alexander Isak nor Cody Gakpo will be available when Liverpool host Manchester City on Sunday, Reds boss Andoni Iraola has confirmed.

Although the news is not unexpected after both players pulled out of their respective squads during the international break, it had been hoped at least one would be available to face the Premier League leaders.

Instead, Iraola is likely to turn to Lewis Koumas to lead the line.

The Spaniard said: “Alex Isak and Gakpo won’t play, not ready unfortunately for us. Injuries in the break. You always hope the doctor doesn’t call you but we have been unlucky. They are not going to be involved.

“Timeframe…Gakpo has an ankle injury, a matter of him dealing with the pain. A bad tackle I think. He is working but not for Sunday. Isak has a thigh injury. They don’t look like long-term injuries but they are not ready for Sunday.

“Koumas has our trust. The player has shown he is ready to go. We also have other players who can cover the positions, so we will take a decision.”

Liverpool boss Iraola expects big atmosphere at Anfield

The wider context around the game surrounds the guilty verdict handed out to City by the Independent Commission investigating systematic financial doping.

City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed but Anfield should be a hostile place for the visitors to tread on Sunday afternoon.

Iraola added: “I think always when you play and lead these kind of games the atmosphere is going to be big, especially at Anfield. I think we want to give our supporters reasons to be [excited] – they will be with us – but when they see the team they want to see on the pitch, we can create a bigger atmosphere and we will work for this.”

Asked about the verdict, Iraola gave little away but did admit it would be better for the league if the appeal ruling was dished out quickly.

“I think uncertainty is not good for anyone and anyone involved, but the process is ongoing and we have to be patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end,” he said.

We want to show our level against City, says Liverpool boss Iraola

Liverpool remain unbeaten but have struggled for consistency.

“I think it’s still very early,” said the former Bournemouth boss. “Whatever happens, we’ve just played five games but it’s true that we would like to face a team like City and show our level and get the win and have a good day. It’s massive for everyone involved in these types of games. It’s an exciting moment.

“We are playing at home at Anfield against City who is top of the league right now. They have won all of their games and I think we will go for it. I think it will be quite an open game and we have to be ready and also use the help from our supporters.

“Every time you face a team that is around you [in the table] you always want to win but in the end it’s still very early in the season.”

Jeremy Jacquet will be tasked with keeping Erling Haaland quiet and Iraola has been impressed with the young Frenchman’s start to life in the Premier League.

Iraola said: “He’s done really well. Firstly because he is a very good player, obviously you know Jacquet and you see clips of him but until you have him in everyday training you can’t really appreciate what he has.

“I am very happy for him personally because to make a debut in the national team, in a team like France who is difficult to have a chance [in], and I think he played really well and he should be happy. But still he has a long way to go.”

articles.title: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick claims Lamine Yamal ‘will be the best player in the world’
articles.summary: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has been speaking about Lamine Yamal ahead of La Liga's return.
articles.content:
Barcelona boss Hansi Flick claims Lamine Yamal ‘will be the best player in the world’

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has been speaking about Lamine Yamal ahead of La Liga's return.

Last Update:

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has backed Lamine Yamal to become the best footballer in the world, praising the teenager’s mentality and attitude ahead of the Ballon d’Or this month.

Yamal has continued to attract attention with his displays for Spain during the international break, adding to his strong start to the season with Barcelona.

Flick believes the winger already possesses the qualities required to reach the very top of the game and suggested he may have achieved that status already.

“What I see in the games with Spain and with us in the first eight games is incredible,” Flick said.

“I saw it in London against England live. It depends on each player, they are young and recover quickly.

“Lamine is young and enjoys playing soccer. If you don’t train much, it’s good that you’ve stayed at that level.

“He enjoys playing soccer and has confidence and his attitude is incredible. What we see here in training is very good.”

“He will be the best player in the world if he is not already,” the Barcelona boss added.

“With his attitude, his mentality, his willingness to improve every day… that is the right mentality and at the moment he is on that path and I am very happy with it.”

Flick questions Raphinha’s international schedule

Flick was also asked about Raphinha and the demands placed on players during international breaks.

The Barcelona manager acknowledged the importance of representing their country but questioned whether Brazil needed to travel to Australia and India for friendly matches.

“The national team is the national team and for anyone it is the main objective, to defend their country, and it is Raphinha’s mentality and attitude,” Flick said.

“Always give 100%. We must reflect on whether it was necessary for him to play in Australia, to travel so many thousands of kilometers. It’s incredible.”

“They have to choose friendly matches and in Europe it is not possible because of the Nations League.

“When I was in the German team we had the option of going to Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, but because you had two or three friendlies. Now it’s impossible.”

articles.title: Manchester City’s success is not ‘tainted’ by guilty verdict, insists Enzo Maresca
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca is adamant Manchester City’s achievements have not been tainted by the club being found guilty of breaching 114 financial regulations. The verdict of the Independent Commission a fortnight ago – that City cheated the system to the tune of over £900, enabling them to bolster their squad with players that went on to […]
articles.content:
Manchester City’s success is not ‘tainted’ by guilty verdict, insists Enzo Maresca

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca is adamant Manchester City’s achievements have not been tainted by the club being found guilty of breaching 114 financial regulations.

The verdict of the Independent Commission a fortnight ago – that City cheated the system to the tune of over £900, enabling them to bolster their squad with players that went on to enjoy huge on-field success – has inevitably led to claims the period between 2009 and 2018 should be viewed differently.

But Maresca, who worked for the club as part of Pep Guardiola’s coaching staff across two separate spells between 2020 and 2023 before replacing the Spaniard in the top job over the summer, insisted the players’ achievements should still be recognised.

Asked if their success was tainted, he replied: “Absolutely not. The last time I was here was the treble season, I know the effort from the players, the club, the manager that was Pep. I know exactly the effort the club put in to achieve that kind of target. I don’t have any doubts about that.”

City will win the appeal – Maresca

City have appealed the verdict, and continue to deny any wrongdoing, and Maresca is confident the club will be cleared.

He added: “I understand the reason why most of you [the media] are here, but the only thing I can say is what I’ve said already. The reason why I joined this club is because I completely trust 100% the owners, the CEO, the sporting director – all the organisation.

“I would like to speak about this situation when we’re going to win the appeal. Now it makes no sense to speak about anything, because I don’t have any information.”

Maresca said he would have “100%” joined City if the findings of the Independent Commission had already been revealed and hinted he would remain in post if the sanction saw the club thrown out of the Premier League.

“I won the Championship with Leicester, so in case we’re in League One, we’ll see!” he said. “But again, we are thinking about something that we don’t know.”

City will face a tough test at Liverpool – Maresca

With the appeal process ongoing, Maresca’s immediate concern is Sunday’s challenging trip to Liverpool with a white-hot atmosphere expected at Anfield.

“It will be a tough game [against Liverpool], a tough test,” he added. “But we need to be ready. The focus has to be about the game. The environment in Anfield is nice, [it will] probably be worse because of the situation. Again, it will be our duty to try and do our best and try and win the game.”

Maresca revealed the issue has not led to any negativity within the dressing room with the players focusing on trying to extend their 100% record to six games this weekend.

He said: “I understand that probably you want to hear or listen to different words from me. But the real words is that the players, yes the noise is there, but they are 20- to 25-years-old. They come, they enjoy, they train, they go home happy, they are top of the league. So the players are relaxed. They are just thinking how we can beat Liverpool. And hopefully, we’re going to try.

“We understand the seriousness of the situation, we understand the noise completely, 100%. It’s something serious. But at the same time, we just need to manage that and focus on what we can control. Try to prepare the game the best way, go to Anfield, and win the game.”

Haaland fit for City

City will have Erling Haaland available despite fears the striker sustained an injury on international duty with Norway.

“He’s good! He’s good!” said Maresca. “He went to Marbella, two or three days off, played golf, recovery, and ready for Anfield. He’s good, thank you.

“It was good [to see him again]. Also because, again, the players are thinking about international teams, some days off, and then go again. It was good.”

articles.content:
He was not doing the Tour of Switzerland! Real Madrid boss Mourinho defends under-fire Mbappe after cycling pictures

Kylian Mbappe would not play for Real Madrid if Jose Mourinho felt he was not fulfilling his responsibilities towards the club, the Portuguese insisted on Friday

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has lashed out at claims he was unhappy with Kylian Mbappe amid suggestions the Real Madrid striker was not taking his rehabilitation from a knee injury seriously.

Mbappe sustained a recurrence of a long-standing problem when playing for France against Turkey in the opening game of the international break. He pulled out of Les Bleus’ squad but was then spotted in a Parisian nightclub while further accusations were thrown his way when he filmed himself riding a bike in the Swiss Alps.

Asked about his star man ahead of Saturday’s game with Villarreal, Mourinho said: “For me, [being] a player is [living that for] 24 hours. Something important or negative that he does on a private level, always has some impact. I always say a player will always be a human being. A man who can be wrong, but has a sense of responsibility.

“In the case of Mbappé. He has been here, he has had a diagnosis. He has gone to an outpatient clinic because his knee has a history that cannot be forgotten. He has a recovery plan that you don’t have to know in detail.

“And then, it’s the issue of problem-seeking [by the media]. The real problems that football has had these last couple of weeks have not been enough and there is a search for more. First, the disco that was not a disco. It was a place for a private event at Paris fashion week. Then, the bicycle in Switzerland where it was a hotel of small houses. There were bicycles to move to other areas. And it looks like he was doing the Tour of Switzerland.”

Mourinho criticises media for Real Madrid whispers

Mbappe could still face a hostile reception from the Santiago Bernabeu crowd this weekend and if he does Mourinho believes the local press will be to blame.

“If this happens, it will be a great victory for you [the media],” he said. “Not even giant stories like the Manchester City one or the difficult situation in my country with Cristiano [Ronaldo] and his coach. So many stories that could feed your work, but it has not been enough.

“Madrid is Madrid and you always have to get something out.”

Asked if he understood the fans’ frustration with a player who has scored 94 goals in 111 games in all competitions since joining from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024, Mourinho replied: “This is one of your goals. It is not necessary to be Einstein to understand that this is the goal.

“My hope is that the Bernabéu will be fair. To be fair is to be intelligent. Read between the lines and understand the dynamics. Understand the objectives. I promise that if a Real Madrid player does not fulfill his obligations as a player or as a citizen, they will not see that player. They won’t be able to whistle him, he’s going to be at home. I don’t give him the opportunity to sit on the bench.

“Mbappé is going to play. He won’t be on the bench. I’m sure he hasn’t failed in his obligations with Real Madrid.”

Pressure on Real Madrid to remain on coat tails of leaders Barcelona

Madrid head into the clash with Villarreal in fourth place in La Liga, five places and seven points ahead of their opponents. But with Barcelona winning all seven of their opening games, the pressure is on Mourinho’s men to win tomorrow or risk falling even further behind their arch-rivals in the title race.

articles.summary: Everton's American owners are seeking investment - or a complete sale - of the Merseyside club
articles.content:
TFG put Everton up for sale

Everton's American owners are seeking investment - or a complete sale - of the Merseyside club

Last Update:

The Friedkin Group has confirmed Everton are up for sale.

The club’s majority owners released a statement this morning announcing they were seeking external investment and would countenance a complete sale if they found the “right stewards to take the club forward”.

Everton were purchased by the Friedkin Group in December 2024, ending an unhappy period under Farhad Moshiri. They helped stabilise the cub financially, refinancing much of the debt and arranging lower-interest loans secured against Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But fans have been less impressed with on-field trading with Everton recording a rare profit in the summer transfer window after selling the likes of Iliman Ndiaye and Beto to Manchester City and Fiorentina respectively.

TFG released a statement on Friday that read: “The Friedkin Group is exploring new investment options for Everton Football Club, including the potential sale of a controlling interest.

“When TFG became custodians of Everton, the club faced significant financial uncertainty and challenges both on and off the pitch. The immediate priority was to provide the stability, investment and support needed to secure the club’s future, including helping to bring the long-promised stadium to completion for its deserving supporters.

“With that foundation now safely in place, the time is right to consider the next chapter for Everton. We will only entertain interest from parties who we strongly believe will be the right stewards to take the club forward and build on the momentum that has been established.

“Throughout this process, TFG’s focus will remain unchanged. We will support the club in all ways necessary to achieve success on the pitch and will continue efforts to make a positive difference in the communities the club serves.”

David Moyes’ side have made a solid start on the field and will take their unbeaten record to Hull on Sunday.

articles.title: Mourinho jokes he’ll be lucky to see final Man City verdict
articles.summary: Mourinho's Man United finished second to Man City in 2017-18.
articles.content:
Mourinho jokes he’ll be lucky to see final Man City verdict

Mourinho's Man United finished second to Man City in 2017-18.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho joked he will be lucky to still be alive when the final verdict on the charges levelled at Manchester City is delivered.

City were last month found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

The Premier League confirmed in a statement on September 29 that, following an independent commission ruling, City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges of financial breaches brought against the club.

Among the breaches were the creation of ‘sham’ contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over nine years covering the 2009-10 season to the 2017-18 campaign.

City have appealed the decision but, should it be upheld, could face a punishment that would see them lose their Premier League status. A points deduction that relegates the club and exclusion from the Premier League have both been mooted as potential sanctions, while many have called for City to be stripped of the titles they won in the period in question.

Real Madrid boss Mourinho led Manchester United to a second-placed finish behind City in 2017-18. The Red Devils ended that campaign 19 points adrift of side managed by Pep Guardiola, who left the Etihad Stadium at the end of last season.

Mourinho has previously labelled that second-placed finish as one of his greatest achievements in a storied career.

But, with the independent commission having come to its decision over three years after charges were first brought against City, Mourinho isn’t expecting to imminently learn if he will be awarded a fourth Premier League title retrospectively.

Asked about the case in an interview with Corriere dello Sport, Mourinho said: “I prefer to laugh a little, because I think we’ll have an ending.

“We will have an ending. But the two of us [Mourinho and the interviewer], who are nearing 60, should be lucky enough to be here when the final verdict is delivered. Because now the sentence will come, and after a year, there will be an appeal.”

City confirmed their appeal last week.

The club’s statement read: “Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

“The club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

“The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

“We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”

articles.title: ‘They don’t care about the noise’ – Maresca hails ‘fantastic’ feeling in Man City camp

articles.content:
‘They don’t care about the noise’ – Maresca hails ‘fantastic’ feeling in Man City camp

City are set to face a fierce atmosphere at Anfield on Sunday.

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca described the feeling in the Manchester City squad as “fantastic” as they prepare to face Liverpool in their first game since the club was found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

The Premier League confirmed in a statement on September 29 that, following an independent commission ruling, City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges of financial breaches brought against the club.

Among the breaches were the creation of ‘sham’ contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over nine years covering the 2009-10 season to the 2017-18 campaign.

City have appealed the decision, and their future in the top flight hinges on the outcome of that process and the potential sanctions handed down.

Maresca’s men could hardly face a worse first fixture since the Premier League ruling as they travel to what will surely be a hugely emotional Anfield.

With City having finished ahead of Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool in thrilling title races in 2018-19 and 2021-22, the visitors can expect to face a ferocious atmosphere from a home crowd fuelled by the feeling those titles should have belonged to Liverpool.

However, Maresca seems undaunted by that prospect, making it clear spirits are high in the camp amid the crisis the club faces.

“The feeling is fantastic, to be honest,” Maresca said in an interview with the club’s in-house media ahead of the game with Andoni Iraola’s Reds.

“The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league. The players are just focused on that.

“They know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things.

“They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don’t care too much about the noise.

“They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield.”

City are top of the Premier League with a three-point lead over Arsenal, who open the weekend’s action against Leeds United in Saturday’s early kick-off.

articles.title: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert admits Spygate scandal ‘changed my life’ after escaping touchline ban
articles.summary: Tonda Eckert has spoken to the media after being handed a suspended six-week suspension for Southampton's 'spygate' scandal.
articles.content:
Southampton boss Tonda Eckert admits Spygate scandal ‘changed my life’ after escaping touchline ban

Tonda Eckert has spoken to the media after being handed a suspended six-week suspension for Southampton's 'spygate' scandal.

Last Update:

Southampton manager Tonda Eckert has admitted the club’s Spygate scandal “changed my life” after avoiding an immediate touchline ban ahead of Sunday’s Championship clash with Portsmouth.

The 33-year-old was handed a suspended six-week suspension on Wednesday following his involvement in Southampton secretly filming a Middlesbrough training session towards the end of last season.

The incident resulted in Southampton being removed from the Championship play-off final and receiving a four-point deduction for the current campaign.

Eckert accepted responsibility for his actions and was charged by the Football Association with three breaches of Rule E3.1 relating to misconduct.

Although the FA had pushed for a suspension of at least three months, an independent commission opted for a suspended six-week ban, allowing the German to remain on the touchline.

Eckert relieved after Spygate verdict

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s south coast derby against Portsmouth, Eckert expressed relief that the disciplinary process had finally reached a conclusion.

“We got a heads-up on Monday,” he said.

“It’s a big week for us as a football club. We’re heading into a very important game on Sunday and to have clarity as quick as possible going into such an important game, I think has not just been a relief for me but everyone involved.

“There was a fair chance that the verdict goes a different way. After such a long time, we have verdict from the EFL, we have a verdict now and whatever you expect is not necessary what you get in the end.

“For me it’s just to hold my head up, one more time I made a mistake and it’s for me to take the consequences.”

Southampton boss reveals personal impact

Eckert admitted the prolonged investigation and uncertainty surrounding his position had taken a significant personal toll.

The German, who joined Southampton in July 2025, faced questions over his future during the summer following the club’s punishment.

However, Southampton’s hierarchy continued to support him despite the controversy.

“Obviously it does make a big difference that we can draw a line now. Not just for me but also for the ones close to me,” Eckert said.

“It’s tough. It changes your life. If I was to say it has been all easy from the very [first] moment, it has not but you need to find a way.

“You need to find a conclusion at one point in the summer if you want to continue. That first decision was not for me but was for the club to make.”

Eckert thanks Southampton owners for backing

The Southampton manager also expressed his gratitude towards owner Dragan Solak and the club’s board for standing by him throughout the disciplinary process.

“I said this straight away but it’s for me to say thank you for the support and not just Dragan but the whole board,” he said.

“I think there are many football clubs that take a different decision in the summer.

“What makes this club special is that in times that are a lot tougher and especially with a lot of outside pressure, that we come to a decision the way we have done it.

“It will be and not just for the moment but that will be something to forever be grateful for.”

articles.content:
Granit Xhaka handed two-year suspended fine over fake Covid vaccination certificate

Granit Xhaka has been punished for forging a COVID-19 form.

Last Update:

Sunderland midfielder Granit Xhaka has confirmed he has received a two-year probation sentence after admitting to obtaining a fraudulent Covid-19 vaccination certificate.

The 34-year-old Switzerland captain addressed the outcome in a statement on Instagram on Thursday, accepting responsibility for his actions following an investigation by Swiss authorities.

Xhaka also revealed that his punishment includes a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000), while he has already paid the associated court fees.

The former Arsenal midfielder missed Switzerland’s four Nations League fixtures during the recent international break after withdrawing from the national team to cooperate with prosecutors.

“I accept the decision and take responsibility,” he wrote on Instagram.

“I now clearly see that this was the wrong course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry.

“I accept responsibility for this decision, am facing the process of addressing the facts, and am cooperating fully with the relevant authorities.”

Switzerland backed Xhaka’s decision to withdraw

Xhaka’s withdrawal from the national team came after discussions with the Swiss Football Association (SFV), with both parties agreeing that he should miss the international break.

Swiss football president Peter Knabel supported the midfielder’s decision to cooperate with the authorities and face the consequences of his actions.

“We welcome Granit taking this step and facing the consequences,” Knabel said last month.

“At the same time, we jointly concluded that it is in the team’s best interest to complete this training camp without him.”

Knabel also confirmed that Xhaka’s international future would be reviewed after the October fixtures.

“After the conclusion of this international match window, we will reassess the situation together with Granit and discuss the next steps.”

Erling Haaland says Manchester City must ‘stick together’ as Premier League pile-on continues

Erling Haaland has sent a message to Manchester City fans.

Last Update:

Erling Haaland has urged Manchester City supporters to remain united ahead of a crucial week for the club following the verdict in their Premier League financial case.

City are preparing to face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday before hosting Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain three days later.

The fixtures come amid uncertainty surrounding the club’s future after an independent commission found City guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations, with the club appealing the verdict.

Haaland, however, is focused on matters on the pitch and believes maintaining a positive atmosphere will be important as Enzo Maresca’s side attempt to continue their perfect start to the domestic season.

Speaking to Manchester City’s official website, Haaland encouraged supporters travelling to Anfield to enjoy the occasion and continue backing the team.

“I think they [the City fans travelling to Anfield] are gonna have a good time,” he said.

“We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive.

“No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile. We have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game.

“We have to stick together, and we have to spread the love to each other.

“So yeah, stick together, enjoy the ride and smile.”

City have won their opening five Premier League matches and head to Merseyside looking to strengthen their position at the top of the table.

Haaland is also in good form after scoring three goals in four appearances for Norway during the international break.

“It’s always special to play against Liverpool – I won there, drew there and lost,” Haaland added.

“It’s always special – every Premier League game is different and every Premier League game against Liverpool is special.”

articles.title: Mikel Arteta reveals Arsenal’s Champions League final defeat left ‘poison in my veins’
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has opened up on the scars of the Champions League final last season.
articles.content:
Mikel Arteta reveals Arsenal’s Champions League final defeat left ‘poison in my veins’

Mikel Arteta has opened up on the scars of the Champions League final last season.

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal’s Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain still hurts, but insists the disappointment will drive him and his players to pursue further success.

The Gunners reached their first Champions League final in 20 years last season but suffered heartbreak against PSG, losing on penalties following a 1-1 draw in May.

Arteta, who signed a new four-year contract with Arsenal on Wednesday, has now opened up about the lasting impact of that defeat and his ambitions for the club.

Speaking to The Athletic, Arteta revealed that missing out on European football’s biggest prize remains a source of motivation.

The Spaniard referenced former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who famously described defeats as leaving scars on a manager’s heart.

“I still have the scar, like Arsene says,” Arteta said.

“I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that’s when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody.”

Arteta outlines Arsenal ambitions after new contract

Despite the disappointment, Arteta believes the experience can help his squad as they attempt to compete for more major honours.

The 44-year-old has already guided Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 22 years, ending a lengthy wait for domestic success.

However, he believes there is still considerably more to achieve at the Emirates.

“Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we’re going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great,” he said.

“But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite.

“It feels like it’s still a lot to do, and it’s just the beginning.”

Arsenal boss recalls moment he knew title was coming

Asked which match from his time in charge he would choose to experience again, Arteta selected Arsenal’s 1-0 win over West Ham during their title-winning campaign.

The controversial result moved the Gunners closer to securing the Premier League crown and left Arteta convinced that his side would finish the job.

“This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people’s lives, goes one way or the other,” he said.

“You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it’s gone again.

“That day when I went home, I said, ‘We’re going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we’re going to get it done.'”

Arsenal return to Premier League action on Saturday when they host Leeds in the early kick-off.

articles.content:
Frank Lampard refuses to speculate on Manchester City charges ahead of Premier League return

Frank Lampard has been quizzed on Manchester City's financial charges.

Last Update:

Coventry City manager Frank Lampard has refused to speculate on Manchester City’s financial breaches or the potential consequences for his former club, insisting the appeal process must be allowed to run its course.

City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations following a lengthy investigation into their financial activities between 2009 and 2018.

The club have denied any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the independent commission’s findings.

Lampard, who spent the 2014-15 season at the Etihad Stadium towards the end of his playing career, admitted he was not in a position to judge the case.

“We’ve all seen the news, it’s obviously big news, Man City are appealing. I guess my reaction is that, right?” Lampard said.

“What can you say when an appeal is going on? I’m not inside the story, I’m outside it completely. I played for Man City a long time ago now, for one year.

“We’ll wait and see what the result of the appeal is and onwards. I don’t know the timelines at all.”

Lampard made 38 appearances in the Premier League during his single season with City, scoring six goals after leaving Chelsea.

Lampard unsure of impact on City’s season

The former England midfielder was also asked whether the ongoing controversy could affect Manchester City’s performances this season.

City face the possibility of significant sporting sanctions if their appeal is unsuccessful, although the final punishment has yet to be decided.

Lampard did not want to predict how the situation might influence the players or manager Enzo Maresca.

“I don’t know, for Man City? I’m outside the loop,” he said.

“I have this job and my, not problems, but things I need to work on and I always respect a manager for whatever situation, there are a lot of things you don’t know.

“This is obviously something we do know but they are obviously a huge football club now, a huge squad of quality players so we will see.”

articles.summary: Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey could return to action at Bournemouth next weekend after tests showed his hamstring injury was not as serious as first thought
articles.content:
Relief for Sunderland as Brobbey set for swift return from hamstring injury

Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey could return to action at Bournemouth next weekend after tests showed his hamstring injury was not as serious as first thought

Last Update:

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has confirmed star striker Brian Brobbey has avoided serious injury, although he won’t be available for Saturday’s game with Brighton.

Brobbey’s final act before the international break was to score a hat-trick in the Wearsiders’ 5-3 defeat at Manchester City. He then went away with the Netherlands but broke down clutching his hamstring 35 minutes into their opening game against Germany.

The former Ajax man appeared destined for a lengthy spell on the sidelines but Le Bris expects him, and Senegal midfielder Habib Diarra who is also absent with a hamstring problem, to return soon.

The Frenchman said: “Brian and Habib are on a similar schedule and will be available soon. Habib is really close. He’s in a good place. Almost every session is done for the full recovery. So, in around one week he’ll be fully available.

“With Brian, it’s going to be short term [as well]. It’s really positive, we were a bit worried when we saw the video but Brian, just after the game, wasn’t too worried because he experienced different injuries in the past. He was adamant that it wasn’t too serious and it’s the case. We won’t take too many risks, but it won’t be too long.”

Brobbey’s absence will mean Haiti striker Wilson Isidor can expect a decent run in the starting XI.

Le Bris said: “We have Wilson who is a really good striker with a different style of play but really competitive for the Premier League and showed his qualities last season.

“He’s a bit different and I think it’s positive to have different kind of players. He likes exploiting the places in behind, he’s quick and a good finisher as well. He’s really well connected with the club and the squad as well and that’s a positive.”

Ballard blow for Sunderland

There was less positive news on Dan Ballard. The Northern Ireland centre-half also sustained a problem during the international break and is set to miss a significant chunk of Sunderland’s busy upcoming schedule that includes games in the Premier League, EFL Cup and Europa League.

“It’s a shame for Ballard because he was in a good place and will be sidelined for a few weeks,” said Le Bris. “It’s a medium-term injury.”

Sunderland head into the weekend clash with Brighton in 14th place in the Premier League table.

The Seagulls are third after resounding wins over Coventry (5-0) and Arsenal (3-0).

“They have had a good start to the season with a young, dynamic squad,” said Le Bris. “It will be a challenge, but we know our strengths.”

articles.title: Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five players to axe ahead of Gameweek 6
articles.summary: Two of Liverpool's biggest names are among our quintet to dump from your Fantasy Premier League squads for this week.
articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five players to axe ahead of Gameweek 6

Two of Liverpool's biggest names are among our quintet to dump from your Fantasy Premier League squads for this week.

Last Update:

The international break has given Fantasy Premier League managers plenty to think about. Injuries have hit several popular players, while some of the season’s early stars are heading into much tougher fixtures. With Gameweek 6 approaching, these are five players worth dumping from your rosters.

Dominik Szoboszlai

Price: 6.9mOwnership: 32.3%Position: MidfielderOpponent : MCI (H), BRE (A), BHA (H)

Szoboszlai remains in roughly a third of FPL squads, but the numbers are getting harder to defend. His only attacking return in five matches was a penalty against Newcastle in Gameweek 1. He has created three big chances, so the creativity is there, but has managed just one shot inside the box all season. That is a problem for a 6.9m midfielder when cheaper alternatives are getting into far more dangerous positions. Liverpool now face Manchester City, Brentford and Brighton before Arsenal in Gameweek 9. Even with his set-piece duties, there is little in that run to suggest a sudden surge in points. If your squad is otherwise healthy, Szoboszlai looks like a sensible sell.

Alexander Isak

Price: 9.1mOwnership: 21.9%Position: ForwardOpponent: MCI (H), BRE (A), BHA (H)

Four goals in five matches is hardly a reason to panic, and Isak has certainly delivered for owners so far. The concern is what comes next. The Liverpool forward returned from Sweden duty with a thigh problem, described by national team boss Graham Potter as minor, but his fitness for Gameweek 6 still needs confirming. At 9.1m, he is an expensive player to carry if there is serious doubt over his minutes. The fixture list hardly offers much comfort either. Manchester City, Brentford and Brighton are up next, followed by Arsenal. Isak can score against anyone, so this is a conditional sell rather than an automatic one. If the injury restricts his involvement, that money could be better spent elsewhere.

Maxim De Cuyper

Price: 5.0mOwnership: 28.3%Position: DefenderOpponent: SUN (A), CRY (H), LIV (A)

De Cuyper has been one of the great early-season FPL finds. Listed as a defender but often playing on Brighton’s left wing, he has collected 38 points, with a goal, three assists and three clean sheets. He has also created 11 chances, more than any other defender. You can see exactly why managers have rushed to bring him in. The concern is whether those returns can continue at this rate. Brighton rank only 14th for expected goals conceded, while the returning Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh could threaten De Cuyper’s advanced role. Sunderland and Crystal Palace are decent short-term fixtures, but Liverpool and Manchester City follow. He’s worth keeping if you own him, but I’d think twice before buying now.

Brian Brobbey

Price: 5.7mOwnership: 6.8%Position: ForwardOpponent: BHA (A), BOU (A), LEE (H)

A hat-trick away at Manchester City is the sort of performance that sends FPL managers straight to the transfer page. Brobbey scored 17 points in Gameweek 5, having blanked in each of the previous four, and almost 200,000 managers have already brought him in during the break. That feels like a lot of faith in one explosive afternoon. The bigger worry is his hamstring. Brobbey lasted just 35 minutes for the Netherlands against Germany before coming off injured, and Sunderland have yet to confirm how long he could be out. Brighton, Bournemouth and Leeds are tempting opponents, but they mean very little if he cannot start. Wait for a clean bill of health before chasing his points.

Joao Pedro

Price: 7.7mOwnership: 64.4%Position: ForwardOpponent: BOU (H), EVE (A), TOT (H)

João Pedro is one of the hardest decisions facing FPL managers this week. His three goals and three assists made him a brilliant early pick, but a knee injury kept him out of Chelsea’s Gameweek 5 defeat to Brentford. Xabi Alonso has expressed hope that he will return against Bournemouth, although there is still no guarantee he is ready for a full match. That uncertainty matters when you are spending 7.7m on a forward. Bournemouth, Everton and Tottenham offer genuine attacking potential, so owners should not sell simply because he is flagged. However, buying him before the final team news is an unnecessary gamble. If his minutes remain restricted, the points could easily dry up for a couple of weeks.

articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27: Five players who will explode over the next three gameweeks

Arsenal have a decent run of fixtures coming up so now is a good time to target the Gunners in Fantasy Premier League. We identify two here...

Last Update:

With the international break coming to an end, Fantasy Premier League managers have an opportunity to reassess their squads ahead of Gameweek 6. Looking beyond the next round of fixtures, these five players stand out for their underlying numbers, favourable match-ups and potential to deliver over the next three Gameweeks.

Bukayo Saka

Price: 9.6mOwnership: 14.4%Position: MidfielderOpponent: LEE (H), NFO (A), EVE (H)

If you’re spending heavily in midfield, Saka makes more sense than chasing last week’s points. He has already scored three times, but the more persuasive stat is his six big chances – more than any other FPL midfielder – alongside 12 attempts inside the box. Martin Ødegaard’s return has freed him to attack the area rather than carry the entire creative burden. Leeds won’t be pushovers: they have conceded only three league goals and have protected their left flank well. Still, Arsenal host Leeds before a trip to Nottingham Forest and a home meeting with Everton. Saka’s potential penalty duties and share of Arsenal’s best chances put him firmly in the conversation.

Kevin Schade

Price:  6.2mOwnership: 12.4%Position: MidfielderOpponent: AVL (A), LIV (H), HUL (A)

Villa have had a rough time defending their right flank, and that is exactly where Brentford will want to release Schade. The German has three goals and two assists from five appearances, with 12 shots inside the area – not the profile of a winger living off one fortunate finish. Brentford’s attacking numbers are strong and their willingness to play quickly suits his running power. Villa have also conceded the third most big chances in the division. The slight concern is that Schade has scored three from 1.52 xG, so finishing at this rate may not last. Liverpool in GW7 is awkward, but Hull follows in GW8.

Ricardo Calafiori

Price: 5.9mOwnership: 50.6%Position: DefenderOpponent: LEE (H), NFO (A), EVE (H)

Arsenal’s defence remains one of the safest places to invest, but Calafiori brings something that a standard clean sheet pick doesn’t. He has two assists already, and Leeds’ defensive numbers give his forward runs a particularly interesting target: they have allowed 20 chances down their right, compared with 13 down the left. Leeds have also faced 29 efforts from set pieces and 17 headers, the most obvious crack in an otherwise stubborn backline. Calafiori has three clean sheets in five games, and Arsenal face Leeds, Nottingham Forest and Everton next. Rotation around the Champions League is worth watching, but at 5.9m he’s a convincing alternative to more expensive defenders.

Marcus Tavernier

Price: 6.1mOwnership: 6.9%Position: MidfielderOpponent: CHE (A), SUN (H), MUN (A)

Chelsea away isn’t normally a fixture I’d target, but their defence has made a habit of giving opponents opportunities. No side has conceded more Premier League goals this season, which brings Tavernier into the picture. He has three goals from his first five games, 13 shots and a healthy 2.61 non-penalty expected goal involvements. Bournemouth’s attacking threat isn’t all coming from their striker, and Tavernier’s set-piece involvement adds another way to contribute. The schedule remains interesting beyond Stamford Bridge, with Sunderland at home in GW7 and Manchester United away in GW8. He’s a more aggressive pick than the others, with European rotation a concern, but at 6.1m there’s upside.

Gonzalo García

Price: 6.0mOwnership: 4.3%Position: ForwardOpponent: IPS (A), HUL (H), COV (A)

One goal from 2.34 xG can put people off, but with García I’d look at the chances before the finishing. Fulham’s new striker has taken 15 shots, 13 of them inside the box, and seen four big chances come his way in five matches. This week he visits Ipswich, who have conceded 17 big chances, including plenty through central areas, and are still waiting for a clean sheet. Better still, Hull at home and Coventry away follow straight afterwards. Fulham haven’t been prolific, so there’s a ceiling to his appeal, but for a 6.0m forward this is a rare three-game window where both role and fixtures work in his favour.
