articles.title: Real Madrid must rue Mourinho mistake as Mbappe antics show club remains in turmoil
articles.summary: Real Madrid pinned their hopes on Jose Mourinho restoring harmony to a fractured dressing room. It has not worked as Kylian Mbappe's latest mis-step proves...
articles.content:
Real Madrid must rue Mourinho mistake as Mbappe antics show club remains in turmoil

Real Madrid pinned their hopes on Jose Mourinho restoring harmony to a fractured dressing room. It has not worked as Kylian Mbappe's latest mis-step proves...

Last Update:

Real Madrid moved for Jose Mourinho over the summer when all conventional logic suggested the 63-year-old was over the hill, spiralling downwards towards retirement.

His swagger had gone, the air of invincibility acquired during his early years at Porto, Chelsea and Inter Milan long since evaporated. Yes, he had won trophies elsewhere – the League Cup and Europa League at Manchester United and the Conference League at Roma – but he was no longer challenging for the game’s major prizes.

There was a sense he sought the big jobs more than the big jobs sought him.

And then, seemingly from nowhere, in stepped Real Madrid. The Portuguese’s previous spell at the Santiago Bernabeu was largely underwhelming. It was the first club at which Mourinho had arguably failed given the resources at his disposal.

In three years, he managed one La Liga crown and one Copa del Rey with his side playing second fiddle to Pep Guardiola’s bewitching Barcelona. As is often the case with Mourinho, his spell in the Spanish capital ended in acrimony, unloved by the players and the media while he played the victim.

It was an inglorious exit in 2013 and, bar one successful season on his return to Chelsea, the subsequent years have demonstrated a coach in decline. While the likes of Guardiola, Jurgen Klopp and Luis Enrique revolutionised, Mourinho remained married to his method of pragmatism.

Real Madrid needed a leader, just not Mourinho

So, why did Madrid chief Florentino Perez bring him back? The answer lies in a dressing room dynamic that saw off the rising star of European coaching, Xabi Alonso, and his successor Alvaro Arbeloa during a turbulent 2025/26 capmpaign.

Both men tried and failed to control a squad where egos and personal ambition ran rampant.

That was brought into sharp focus when Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde came to blows at the club’s training ground while the Madrid rumour mill went into overdrive dissecting the broken relationships between other talented, young millionaires.

Perez thought Mourinho would bring discipline, order and mutual respect. He was lauded as the man to restore integrity to a club that has always viewed itself as above all others.

Five weeks into the Liga season and it has not panned out that way.

A report this morning from Cadena Ser confirmed what many had long suspected: all is not well at Valdebebas. According to the respected radio station’s Anton Meana the situation has not improved one iota.

He said: “The atmosphere in the dressing room is still as icy as it was five months ago.

“This coldness in the dressing room, which even Mourinho’s intensity hasn’t managed to dispel, combined with the turmoil surrounding the Kylian Mbappe affair, has created a tense climate, far from ideal for approaching this crucial month of October.”

Mbappe doing little to help Real Madrid

The ‘Mbappe affair’ refers to the continued insubordination of the France captain and Real Madrid striker.

Mbappe injured his knee playing for Les Bleus in their opening game of the international break and, although it was a relatively minor issue, the club expected him to undergo his rehabilitation in private, ensuring he’d be ready for the league resumption against Villarreal this weekend.

The 27-year-old is set to be declared fit but the reaction of the Bernabeu could be revealing after Mbappe was pictured at a Parisian nightclub and cycling in the Swiss Alps before returning to Spain.

It is not the first time the former PSG man has taken his own path when injured. Last season, he went on holiday to Sardinia rather than work on his recovery from a hamstring injury in Madrid and subsequently missed the Clasico defeat at Camp Nou.

His dedication was questioned by then boss Arbeloa with the two trading barbs in the media. It was unbecoming and a fitting end to a throughly joyless season for Madrid.

Perez’s vision was that Mourinho would eradicate the tension, bring back a hierarchal system that put the team first and, from there, the results would follow.

Madrid have lost two of their first seven league games, are fourth in the table and already six points behind a Barcelona side seemingly on course to win the title for a third year on the trot.

Barca have their issues – the Negreira case continues to cast a dark shadow over the league – but, on the field at least, they are everything Madrid aspire to be.

And in Hansi Flick they have a coach whose thoughtful approach is mirrored by a group of players that play and behave in a joyful, respectful manner.

Mourinho’s return appeared a mistake at the time and there has been no evidence to suggest it’s not a mistake now.

articles.title: Premier League Predictions: Arsenal and Chelsea get back on track, Man United frustrated while City survive Liverpool storm
articles.summary: The international break is over and the Premier League returns with some mouthwatering fixtures. Here, we take a look at the games and give our predictions.
articles.content:
Premier League Predictions: Arsenal and Chelsea get back on track, Man United frustrated while City survive Liverpool storm

The international break is over and the Premier League returns with some mouthwatering fixtures. Here, we take a look at the games and give our predictions.

Last Update:

After the mother of all international breaks, during which time the Premier League landscape has changed enormously, the on-field action finally returns this weekend.

The game of round six comes at Anfield with disgraced Manchester City travelling to the team that has arguably suffered most from their financial chicanery, Liverpool.

The champions kick-start the programme buoyed by news of Mikel Arteta’s lucrative new contract.

Premier League

– Regular Season – 6

Saturday 10, October 2026

Sunday 11, October 2026

Monday 12, October 2026

SATURDAY

Arsenal v Leeds (12.30pm)It must have felt a long three weeks for Arteta, Arsenal’s obsessive manager pouring over every detail of their 3-0 hammering at Brighton before the break. That result came from nowhere with the Gunners seemingly carrying on this season as they finished the last with four successive victories. Leeds could be on the receiving end, although this is a very different outfit to the one that looked like rabbits in the headlights on their first away game since promotion last season. On that occasion, Arsenal romped to a 5-0 win. It should be much closer this time.Prediction: Arsenal 3-1 Leeds

Aston Villa v Brentford (3pm)It was perhaps inevitable that Villa would start slowly given the player trading that took place over the summer. Unai Emery has had to rebuild but the canny Spaniard is starting to get results with his side winning three of their last four in all competitions. They still sit in the lower reaches of the table and this is certainly not a routine assignment against a Brentford team that head to Villa Park unbeaten and still revelling in their 3-0 win over local rivals Chelsea last time out. Brentford have already secured draws on the road at Bournemouth and Leeds and we fancy another one here.Prediction: Aston Villa 2-2 Brentford

Chelsea v Bournemouth (3pm)Xabi Alonso may have signed a four-year contract in May but Chelsea’s ownership are not exactly renown for their patience. The big-spending Blues have gone three league games without a win and the manner of their capitulation at the Gtech Community Stadium would not have gone unnoticed. For now Alonso remains on solid-ish ground but another setback against winless Bournemouth would crank up the pressure on the former Real Madrid boss. Expectations are different at Bournemouth but their new head coach Marco Rose could also do with three points to prove he is an able replacement for Andoni Iraola.Prediction: Chelsea 2-1 Bournemouth

Ipswich v Fulham (3pm)Alonso does not have to look far to find someone who knows what he is going through. His close friend Alvaro Arbeloa is experiencing similar issues down the road at Fulham and this already looks a high-pressure game. Fulham have yet to win – in mitigation, they have had a difficult set of fixtures with which to start the season – and that record has to change sooner rather than later. A trip to Portman Road to face newly promoted Ipswich presents opportunity but also jeopardy. The Tractor Boys are ticking over quite nicely, sitting in mid-table with two wins so far. Another here would see them move into the top 10 and leave Arbeloa looking over his shoulder.Ipswich 2-1 Fulham

Sunderland v Brighton (3pm)Brighton would have rued the timing of the international break. They closed the first section of the season with a 5-0 win at Coventry and a 3-0 demolition of champions Arsenal. They now have to rediscover that groove when they head to the Stadium of Light. It has been a funny start for Sunderland. Dismissed as relegation fodder by most pundits, they have largely performed well but not got the results to back it up. Regis Le Bris’ men should have won at Brentford and could have got at least a draw at Manchester City were it not for a couple of contentious refereeing decisions. They need to start winning games before embarking on a hectic schedule in domestic and European competition.Prediction: Sunderland 2-2 Brighton

Manchester United v Tottenham (5.30pm)According to transfermarkt these two squads have a combined worth of almost £1.5billion and yet they have just one Premier League win between them. It is scant return for year on year of heavy investment. There have been flickers of progress, United brushing Ipswich aside while Spurs have kept clean sheets in two of their last three league games. We’re still clutching at straws, though. These two clubs ought to be doing an awful lot better. A draw here helps neither, so…Prediction: Manchester United 1-1 Tottenham

SUNDAY

Crystal Palace v Nottingham Forest (2pm)Palace fans pining for the return of Oliver Glasner will get their wish this Sunday, in a way. The Austrian, who led the Eagles to three trophies in his short time in South London, will stride down the touchline at Selhurst Park as Nottingham Forest boss looking to add to successor Pierre Sage’s problems. Sage is struggling to assert his influence over the Palace squad and one win from five games is testament to that. Glasner has not exactly torn it up at Forest either. Six of the previous seven games between these two have ended in a draw.Prediction: Crystal Palace 0-0 Nottingham Forest

Hull v Everton (2pm)Hull’s unbeaten return to the top flight ended at Newcastle last time out but the Tigers’ performance deserved more and offered another indication they may be here to stay. Their style is pragmatic but gets results, a point you could also make about Everton. The Toffees will never win awards for style under David Moyes but the Scot has turned them into top-half contenders having taken over a team more used to fighting relegation. This is unlikely to be one for the purists.Prediction: Hull 0-1 Everton

Liverpool v Manchester City (4.30pm)If you had to pick one ground Manchester City would have chosen to avoid this weekend it would be Anfield. The verdict by the Independent Commission that City were guilty of over 100 financial breaches – the club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing – did not go down well on Merseyside and we will never know what Liverpool would have won had it been a level playing field. That has, inevitably, created a hostility that will be in full force when Enzo Maresca and his players, who are all innocent parties to the misdemeanours, rock up at the weekend. If City can block out the noise then they ought to be good enough to beat a Liverpool team still finding their feet under Iraola. It’s a big if…Prediction: Liverpool 2-2 Manchester City

MONDAY

Coventry v Newcastle (8pm)Coventry’s win at Nottingham Forest before the international break was their first in the Premier League for 25 years but Frank Lampard’s overriding emotion must have been relief more than elation. His team had not looked equipped for top-flight football until their trip to the City Ground and the challenge now is to maintain that level against a Newcastle side that have started solidly. Dig deeper, though, and the underlying metrics suggest Matthias Jaissle still has plenty to do.Prediction: Coventry 2-1 Newcastle

articles.title: The Premier League returns: The five storylines to follow including Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea
articles.summary: The Premier League is back this weekend, albeit shrouded in uncertainty with the Manchester City case not yet resolved. What should we keep our eyes on over the next few days?
articles.content:
The Premier League returns: The five storylines to follow including Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea

The Premier League is back this weekend, albeit shrouded in uncertainty with the Manchester City case not yet resolved. What should we keep our eyes on over the next few days?

Last Update:

It has been an extraordinary three-week international break: Lionel Messi’s farewell game; Cristiano Ronaldo’s toddler-esque tantrum; and debut matches in new roles for Jurgen Klopp, Zinedine Zidane and Sebastien Pocognoli.

But there has been one story that has dominated the agenda: the guilty verdict handed down to Manchester City. The appeal process is ongoing and City continue to deny any wrongdoing but the issue is certain to cast a shadow over the Premier League until that appeal, and the sanctions, are boxed off.

In the intervening period, fans will be asked to throw themselves back into club issues knowing everything will be provisional until City’s punishment, if indeed there is one, is confirmed.

It will be a hot topic up and down the country this weekend as the Premier League returns.

Here are five things to look out for:

WILL CITY CHIEF AL MUBARAK ROCK UP AT ANFIELD?

City’s robust statement when launching their appeal indicated they remain confident all the charges will be dropped. With that in mind, will it be business as usual this weekend? The man central to the whole controversy is Khaldoon Al Mubarak. The City chairman is a regular at games and he has the chance to put on a show of solidarity with the players and fans by taking his seat in the directors’ box at Anfield. It is unlikely his presence would be welcomed by Merseyside Police with a very small element of Liverpool’s support baying for blood but the alternative is for Al Mubarak to let coach Enzo Maresca and his players – all innocent parties to the alleged misdemeanours – face the heat.

WEST LONDON BUDDIES IN DIRE NEED OF WINS

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso and Fulham counterpart Alvaro Arbeloa are close friends and it would not be a surprise if they sought each other’s company during the three-week hiatus. Both men head into this weekend knowing a defeat would ramp up the pressure on their positions. Alonso’s side host winless Bournemouth still smarting from their 3-0 hammering at Brentford. Not only was it an awful result but the manner of the performance would have the Chelsea board – not exactly renown for their patience – shuffling uncomfortably in their seats. There is less expectation at Fulham but owner Shahid Khan can’t be impressed by a record of two points from five games. The Cottagers go to newly promoted Ipswich knowing another defeat would mean they slip seven points behind one of their relegation rivals.

Premier League

– Regular Season – 6

Saturday 10, October 2026

Sunday 11, October 2026

Monday 12, October 2026

GREAT UNDERACHIEVERS SET FOR OLD TRAFFORD CLASH

Fans will tune into the Saturday tea-time kick-off between Manchester United and Tottenham fascinated to see if these expensively assembled teams are as bad as their records suggest.  According to Transfermarkt, United have the ninth most valuable squad in Europe (£786million) with Spurs one place lower at £708m. And yet, they have the princely total of one league win between them all season. That was secured by United at home to Ipswich. Tottenham spent huge numbers over the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Savio yet the suspicion remains they paid top dollar for fairly average players. That said, a win at Old Trafford would change the mood overnight.

PALACE AND PARISH MUST PINE FOR GLASNER

He would never admit it but Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish must rue his inability to persuade Oliver Glasner to remain at Selhurst Park. The Austrian led the Eagles to three trophies in a glorious, albeit short-lived spell in South London, and makes his first return this weekend with Nottingham Forest. Since his departure, Palace have managed just one Premier League victory with Pierre Sage struggling to make his presence felt. If there is any consolation for Parish, it is the fact Glasner has hardly set the world alight at Nottingham Forest either. Glasner should be afforded a warm welcome from the home fans but amid the appreciation there will be a sense of disappointment and regret.

WAS IT WORTH IT NEWCASTLE?

Newcastle’s trip to Coventry on Monday night comes five days after the fifth anniversary of the club’s takeover by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund. Five years since ecstatic Geordies danced outside St James’ Park wearing tea towels on their heads. When not committing human rights atrocities, the new owners promised trophies and good times. But, bar one Carabao Cup success, they have not arrived. This summer the club had to sell several of its crown jewels, such as Anthony Gordon, Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, replacing them with untried youngsters. Matthias Jaissle took over from Eddie Howe and, although they have made a solid enough start, the underlying metrics suggest it could still be a tricky season for Newcastle. Having sacrificed their integrity by jumping into bed with the Saudis, you have to ask ‘was it worth it’?

articles.title: Liverpool have doubts over Isak and Gakpo before Man City clash
articles.summary: Forwards are both doubts after international break
articles.content:
Liverpool have doubts over Isak and Gakpo before Man City clash

Forwards are both doubts after international break

Last Update:

Liverpool forwards Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo are both doubts to face Manchester City at Anfield on Sunday.

Both attackers returned early from international duty after picking up knocks, with Isak suffering a thigh problem while away with Sweden and Gakpo sustaining an ankle injury during the Netherlands’ Nations League clash against Serbia.

With Hugo Ekitike already sidelined on a long-term basis due to an Achilles injury, manager Andoni Iraola faces the alarming prospect of being without his primary attacking options for the visit of City.

“Alex Isak and Cody Gakpo both have had to leave the national teams with injuries,” Iraola told beIN SPORTS.

“Now it’s a matter of if they are going to recover in time to help us in the next game or not. But right now they are both injured.”

The potential attacking crisis adds to Liverpool’s broader selection headaches following the international break.

The Reds are already sweating on the fitness of central defender Jeremy Jacquet, who was left out of France’s 4-1 win over Belgium on Monday after suffering a hamstring strain, meaning Liverpool face major injury concerns at both ends of the pitch.

Sunday’s encounter represents the biggest test of Iraola’s tenure so far. Although Liverpool remain unbeaten with four wins and three draws, they come up against a relentless City outfit who have taken maximum points but are up it after the disciplinary news this week.

“We’ve been unbeaten but they’ve won all of them, so it makes a big difference in their side,” Iraola added. “I think we need to be very, very good if we want to beat City because they’ve been especially offensively scoring a lot of goals lately.

“We know the names that are very dangerous. But I think also we’ve shown good defensive improvements lately and I hope we can defend the threats that they have and also hurt them on the other side.”

articles.title: Guardiola set for City return in show of support
articles.summary: Pep is expected to attend the Champions League visit of PSG
articles.content:
Guardiola set for City return in show of support

Pep is expected to attend the Champions League visit of PSG

Last Update:

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is expected to attend the home game against Champions League winners Paris St-Germain next week in a show of support to his former employers.

Guardiola, 55, left the club at the end of last season after a trophy-lined spell in charge which saw him win the treble in 2023.

City have since been rocked with the news that an independent commission found them guilty of 114 charges of financial malpractice.

The club have appealed against the decision but their Premier League future remains uncertain.

In the aftermath of the verdict, Guardiola backed City’s owners and leadership and said he will “always” be behind the club.

“I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever,” he posted on social media.

“I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran (Soriano), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca) and you, our unique supporters.

“Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

The Premier League announced last week that the commission deemed the club had systematically broken the rules with “sham” contracts designed to inflate revenue and reduce costs.

The scale of the deception, reported to have totalled more than £900million, was breathtaking and a number of sanctions now lie on the table. City have continued to deny any wronging and on Friday lodged an appeal after declaring the verdict “unsafe”.

articles.title: ‘It was an incredible road’: Messi speaks out after Argentina retirement
articles.summary: Argentina great has ended his international career
articles.content:
‘It was an incredible road’: Messi speaks out after Argentina retirement

Argentina great has ended his international career

Last Update:

Lionel Messi thanked fans and former team-mates after bringing the curtain down on his international career with Argentina.

The 39-year-old scored on his farewell against Benin and retires having won the World Cup in 2022 with his country.

The Barcelona legend scored a record 126 Argentina goals and helped his country to lift the World Cup and two Copas America.

He wioll continue to play for MLS side Inter Miami but has pulled on the famous blue and white jersey for the last time.

Speaking on Instagram he said he already missed playing for his country and paid tribute to his nation’s other all-time great, Diego Maradona.

Messi’s international farewell is in stark contrast to the chaos caused by rival Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal.

Ronaldo put forward his version of recent events last night, outlining his desire to continue playing for Portugal and also revealing details of a private meeting with coach Jorge Jesus at which they agreed the wording the coach would use at a press conference prior to the Denmark game.

Messi’s statement in full

“Yesterday was my last game and I already miss wearing blue and white. I know I’m making the right decision. It was an incredible road, filled with joys and also some sorrows, but I’m clear that it was worth every step I took.

“And I’m left with a lot to say. It is impossible for me to express everything I feel in a few words or in a post. This trip would have been impossible without my family, who always stood by my side and supported me, especially during the difficult times, when I needed it most. 🙏

“They were also indispensable my friends, all the colleagues and technicians I had, along with their technical bodies. I don’t want to forget Diego, who put our country where it deserved to be and who, as I always say, I know that he helped us being here with us and also from heaven, in every step we took.

“Thanks to the clubs I played in, for always respecting my feelings and allowing me to dedicate myself to my country when it was time to put on the national team shirt. And, of course, thank God: without His guidance and His will, we wouldn’t even be dreaming of having come this far.

“I am a grateful person. I love you so much, I will miss you and I will always thank you for being by our side, by my side.”

articles.title: McTominay cleared for Napoli return following heart procedure
articles.summary: Scotland man back available for selection
articles.content:
McTominay cleared for Napoli return following heart procedure

Scotland man back available for selection

Last Update:

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay has received the green light to resume competitive football after undergoing a successful procedure to correct a heart arrhythmia.

The 29-year-old Scotland international underwent a planned procedure at Manchester’s Spire Hospital in September after medical assessments identified a mild, benign arrhythmia.

Following comprehensive follow-up testing, the Italian outfit confirmed on Wednesday that McTominay has been cleared to return to full sporting activity.

“Scott McTominay underwent further diagnostic tests, which showed that he is fit to play,” Napoli said in an statement.

“The Napoli player therefore resumed training with the rest of the team after the period spent training separately.

The former Manchester United midfielder has been sidelined since August, missing several key fixtures during his recovery. In his absence, Napoli suffered a 3-2 Serie A defeat against reigning champions Inter Milan and fell to a loss against Arsenal in the Champions League.

His return provides a timely selection boost for manager Massimiliano Allegri, with the Partenopei currently sitting ninth in the Serie A standings.

McTominay should be available for selection when Napoli host sixth-placed Frosinone on Saturday.

articles.title: ‘Thank you, football’ – former Chelsea forward Pedro retires
articles.summary: The Spain winger won the Premier League with the Blues
articles.content:
‘Thank you, football’ – former Chelsea forward Pedro retires

The Spain winger won the Premier League with the Blues

Last Update:

Former Chelsea and Spain winger Pedro has announced his retirement from professional football, bringing the curtain down on a decorated 20-year career.

The 39-year-old last played in Serie A with Lazio, but left at the end of last season having won virtually every major honour available across club and international football.

“I feel that now is the moment,” Pedro wrote on social media alongside a video featuring the best moments from his career.

“It’s the moment to take a step forward and start a new chapter in my life. I leave the game proud of fulfilling my dreams and of all the people who were alongside me making them a reality.

“Thank you, football, for making me so happy.”

Credit: Instagram / _pedro17_

Pedro arrived at Stamford Bridge from Barcelona in August 2015 for a fee of £21.4 million, instantly announcing himself to English football by scoring on his debut in a 3-2 victory away at West Brom.

Over a five-year spell in west London, the forward established himself as a reliable, hard-working big-game performer under Jose Mourinho, Antonio Conte, and Maurizio Sarri.

His most prolific Premier League campaign came in 2016-17, when he registered nine goals and eight assists in 35 appearances to play an integral role in Antonio Conte’s title-winning side.

Pedro collected a clean sweep of domestic and European silverware, winning the Premier League in 2017, the FA Cup in 2018, and the Europa League in 2019.

articles.title: Southampton praise FA over Eckert verdict… but vow not to ‘forget’ EFL treatment
articles.summary: Southampton have called Spygate 'a regrettable period'
articles.content:
Southampton praise FA over Eckert verdict… but vow not to ‘forget’ EFL treatment

Southampton have called Spygate 'a regrettable period'

Last Update:

Southampton have welcomed the FA’s decision to give head coach Tonda Eckert a six-week suspended ban from football, £28,000 fine and warning after being charged with three rule breaches over the Spygate scandal last season.

Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs by the EFL in May after admitting to charges of spying on Middlesbrough before their semi-final tie, which the club won 2-1 on aggregate courtesy of a victory by the same scoreline in their home second leg.

They were also found to have committed offences before Championship games against Ipswich Town and Oxford United.

Tonda Eckert FA punishment: Full Southampton statement

Southampton “welcomed the outcome”. “We hope this now brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history,” the club said.

“Measures have been put in place to ensure that such errors in judgement never happen again at our club.”

The suspended ban will last until June 2028 and be imposed if Eckert is found guilty of “requesting, authorising, taking or using information from any observation of the training of another club, in whatever guise that observation may take”.

Owner Dragan Solak echoed the relief voiced in Southampton’s statement. “We have already suffered enough and we appreciate the panel’s recognition of that,” the Serbian billionaire said.

“We are confident the manager has learned from this matter and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role.

“I firmly believe that Tonda is one of Europe’s most exciting young coaches and, with this distraction removed, I am confident he can lead the team to a successful season.

“I’d like to thank our fans for standing by us and showing the team so much support during a time when we have needed them more than ever.

“The FA process has been a positive experience. Tonda has been given the opportunity to be open and honest with the panel, and the panel has been able to see that he is simply a good person who made poor decisions.

“The same cannot be said for the EFL process and the way they have subsequently treated us is not something we will forget.

“However, now is the time to look forward to what I believe will be a great future for our club.”

Spygate: What punishment did Southampton receive?

In addition to being kicked out of the play-off final against eventual victors Hull City, Southampton were handed a four-point deduction this season. They are currently 13th, with 10 points from eight matches.

The club appealed against the EFL’s decision, alleging the punishment was “manifestly disproportionate”. That claim was dismissed by an arbitration panel.

Tonda Eckert role in Spygate scandal

Eckert was the central figure in the drama and had shown his frustration by storming out of his post-match news conference following the second leg against Middlesbrough when asked if he was a cheat.

The German, who oversaw a remarkable upturn in Saints’ form after replacing Will Still in November 2025, authorised the spying in what was described by an independent disciplinary commission as “a contrived and determined plan from the top down”.

How did Tonda Eckert respond to spying scandal?

Eckert said sorry for his actions in an emotional social media post in June.

Speaking to the club’s social media channels, he said: “What I’m going to say is not going to be perfect, but I will try to be as honest and clear as I can be.

“I think you deserve that. For everything that’s happened, I do want to apologise, and I hold my hand up because as a head coach, I am responsible.

“I am responsible for everything that has happened in this football club. I am responsible for everything that has happened in my coaching staff.

“I do apologise to the supporters, to everyone who has travelled with us, who has supported us over so many games.

“To the ones who have shared emotions game by game, who have managed to bring us all the way up to this very end of the season.

“We were supposed to play the biggest game of the season. I apologise to the players, who have done absolutely everything that they can.

“They have done absolutely everything in the last six months to bring this club back to where it belongs. They would have deserved to play the final.

“I apologise to all of the clubs that have been involved, and mostly I apologise to our supporters.”

Southampton owner Solak on Eckert

Solak said he would stand by the embattled 33-year-old in the immediate aftermath of the controversy.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Solak said: “He deserves a second chance and I would give it to him. My full support would be behind him actually, because I think he’s a super-talented manager.

“I believe Tonda that he didn’t know that it was the rule that he was breaking.

“My personal opinion, and the opinion of the board, is that he is a manager who deserves to be backed by us and to be supported by us.

“I will obviously seek advice from the team. I will seek advice from the players, from the fans. But yes, if it’s ultimately my decision, he stays.”

Solak said he hoped Eckert would learn from his mistake and there would be no repeat.

He added: “I told him: ‘You almost broke my heart. You do it again, you’ll kill me. The next time I see you in July, if you don’t know the EFL book of rules by heart, you can’t work for me. We can’t have another mistake.’

“I truly hope that he will learn from this experience and he will achieve an incredible career.”

articles.summary: The 40-year-old left the Premier League in 2020

David Silva: Former Man City midfielder out of retirement to play in Hong Kong

The 40-year-old left the Premier League in 2020

Last Update:

Former Manchester City midfielder David Silva has come out of retirement at the age of 40 to play for Hong Kong Premier League club Sha Tin.

Silva was one of the first marquee signings at City when he joined from Valencia in 2010.

The playmaker won four Premier League titles in a decade at the Etihad Stadium and also won the 2010 World Cup and two European Championships with Spain.

He retired in 2023 after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament tear during pre-season training at Real Sociedad but is now going to play in Hong Kong.

“I’m so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong,” Silva said on Instagram.

Promoted Sha Tin are eighth in the league after four matches, and will continue their campaign against Hong Kong Football Club on October 18.

“David Silva will be in Hong Kong soon to settle in, link up with squad training, and build up to peak match fitness before making his pitch debut,” Sha Tin said.

articles.title: Harry Kane: ‘Gentleman’ striker’s full England appearance record explained
articles.summary: Harry Kane is the oldest England player to score twice in consecutive games
articles.content:
Harry Kane: ‘Gentleman’ striker’s full England appearance record explained

Harry Kane is the oldest England player to score twice in consecutive games

Last Update:

Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton’s England appearance record and scored twice as the Three Lions completed a run of four Nations League games in the September and October 2026 international window.

Bayern Munich forward Kane made his 125th international appearance against Czechia on October 6, moving level with Shilton as the country’s most-capped men’s player.

Starting with a dangerous cross that was diverted in for the opening goal, Kane produced a performance worthy of the occasion as England won 3-0, finishing in a strong position to reach the quarter-finals from Group A3.

England vs Czechia: Harry Kane on ‘perfect night’

Former West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal slid Kane’s delivery past Lukas Hornicek to give England the lead before Kane completed a slick one-touch move by firing in from Morgan Rogers’ cross.

After the restart, the 33-year-old cracked a shot against the crossbar from outside the box following superb footwork and balance by Myles Lewis-Skelly. Lewis Hall then supplied the corner for Kane to head in his second.

“It’s an extremely proud evening,” Kane told ITV, reflecting on England’s victories over Czechia either side of a 7-0 win away to Croatia, having lost their first game of the window 3-2 at home to reigning world champions Spain.

“It was the perfect night for me personally, and for the team. It’s been a tough camp, long camp with some difficult games in there, so it’s nice to finish it off all together here at Wembley.”

How many England caps does Harry Kane have?

Kane’s caps total of 125 puts the former Tottenham talisman level with legendary goalkeeper Shilton, whose record has stood for 36 years.

On his senior England debut, Kane started as he intended to go on by scoring inside two minutes after coming off the bench in a 4-0 World Cup qualifying win over Lithuania at Wembley Stadium in March 2015.

Shilton, whose swansong was a memorable one as England reached the semi-finals of the 1990 World Cup, sent a message to Kane via the English FA before kick-off against Czechia.

“I know how much dedication and hard work you’ve put in to achieving this, especially as a striker,” Shilton said.

“I think that’s probably the hardest position to play – goalkeeper’s just behind that – because of the responsibility. You’ve been a great captain and will be in the future.

“You will go on and beat [the record] in [the Nations League in] November, I’m sure of that, and maybe go on and set a record that will never be beaten, because you’re still going strong, playing well and scoring goals.”

How many goals has Harry Kane scored for England?

Kane has now scored a remarkable 91 goals for England. His total of 32 at Wembley is the most by a Three Lions player at the national stadium.

“There’s not really much more you can say that hasn’t already been said,” teammate Jude Bellingham told the broadcaster.

“I can only really talk from my perspective, and that’s that he is, first and foremost, an unbelievable human being.

“As a captain, as a man, he looks after each and every single person. He’s the one to always take responsibility when something needs doing off the pitch.

“Then on the pitch, you run out of superlatives. He’s the best England player that’s ever worn the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him.”

Czechia coach Santi Denia suggested there is a “secret” behind Kane’s longevity at the very top. “He loves football,” explained the Spaniard.

“He’s an unbelievable player, he understands everything in the game. England supporters should be very proud of this player.

“He’s one of the best players in the world in terms of experience, quality, personality – and he’s a gentleman.”

Here are England’s top scorers of all time.

What next for Harry Kane? England fixtures, schedule

Here are England’s remaining matches in League A3.

When are the Nations League quarter finals? Will England be there?

The first legs of the Nations League quarter-finals take place between March 25 and 27 2027, with the return matches in the home-and-away format held between March 28 and 30.

Should England avoid losing by seven goals at home to Croatia in their next match, they are guaranteed to finish at least second in their section, which would ensure a place in the last eight.

articles.title: Jorge Jesus reacts to Cristiano Ronaldo’s statement as 41-year-old comes under fire from former Portugal winger
articles.summary: Jorge Jesus has had his say after Cristiano Ronaldo's outburst on Tuesday night
articles.content:
Jorge Jesus reacts to Cristiano Ronaldo’s statement as 41-year-old comes under fire from former Portugal winger

Jorge Jesus has had his say after Cristiano Ronaldo's outburst on Tuesday night

Last Update:

Jorge Jesus confirmed on Wednesday he had read Cristiano Ronaldo’s explosive statement but said his immediate focus was on the Portuguese national team.

The melodrama that was sparked by Jesus’ decision not to bring Ronaldo off the bench against Norway last week, a move that prompted the 41-year-old to walk out on the squad on the eve of the game against Denmark, shows no sign of abating.

Ronaldo put forward his version of events last night, outlining his desire to continue playing for Portugal and also revealing details of a private meeting with Jesus at which they agreed the wording the coach would use at a press conference prior to the Denmark game.

In that eight-point statement, Jesus is claimed to have agreed to point out Ronaldo’s loyalty, his positive impact on the national team and also admit it was a mistake not to bring on a player of the ‘stature of Pele or Maradona’ against Norway.

Ronaldo’s eight-point plan

Jesus ignores Ronaldo’s wishes

Instead, at the press conference Jesus insisted he was right in not bringing Ronaldo off the bench due to the match situation and also reiterated the fact he had to look after 23 players, not one.

While Ronaldo has returned to Saudi Arabia to prepare for Al-Nassr’s Pro League game with Diriyah on Friday, Jesus went about his business as normal this morning.

After being collared by reporters outside his home in Lisbon, Jesus said: “I read the statement. And now as I do every day I go to the Federation to work and think about the Portuguese national team. I have nothing else to say.”

While Jesus has stated previously he would have no objection to Ronaldo returning to the Portugal squad for next month’s internationals, the striker’s outburst appears to have thrown a spanner in the works.

He did, at least, apologise to his team-mates for walking out on the squad and accepted his actions warrant some form of punishment.

Simoes asks why Ronaldo is still playing

It will likely rest with Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca to broker a truce in a row that has divided the country.

Former Portugal international Antonio Simoes, who helped his country to a third-placed finish at the 1966 World Cup alongside Eusebio, sides with Jesus.

He said of Ronaldo: “Why does he have to have special treatment? Can you have a different status and be a team player? I played with the King called Eusébio, I lived with Pelé and Maradona, I’ve never seen something like that around a King. A 41-year-old man playing soccer… isn’t it better to stop?”

articles.title: The GOAT: Lionel Messi reluctantly walks away from Argentina on emotional night in Buenos Aires
articles.summary: Lionel Messi was afforded a fitting send-off as he played his final game for Argentina, a 3-0 win against Benin
articles.content:
The GOAT: Lionel Messi reluctantly walks away from Argentina on emotional night in Buenos Aires

Lionel Messi was afforded a fitting send-off as he played his final game for Argentina, a 3-0 win against Benin

Last Update:

Lionel Messi left the international stage in fitting fashion, with a goal, a dazzling display and an emotional speech in which he admitted he “didn’t want this moment to end”.

After his 208th and final appearance for Argentina, a 3-0 win over Benin that bordered on an exhibition game for much of the evening, Messi spoke from the heart to express his difficulty at having to walk away.

The 39-year-old, who scored a second-half penalty and added two assists against generous opposition, said: “There are so many emotions going through me right now. I’m surely forgetting many things I would like to say because this is a very difficult moment for me. The first person who comes to my mind is my dad.

“I leave grateful, proud and at peace. Thank you for everything.”

World Cup final defeat and death of father persuaded Messi to quit

Messi opted to retire from Argentina duty after the World Cup final defeat to Spain was followed by the death of his father Jorge. He leaves having scored 126 Argentina goals and helped his country to lift the World Cup and two Copas America.

“I have nothing left to do but thank this shirt,” he added.

“For 20 years, even through the worst moments, I never stopped fighting, pushing forward, giving everything I had and wanting to be here.

“Not coming here any more and no longer being with the Argentina national team is going to hurt a lot. If it were up to me, I would love to be here for my entire life, because playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing there is.

“I think I’m talking more than ever today because I simply don’t want this moment to end.

“But I think the time has come for me to retire. The last World Cup took a lot out of us after everything we went through. We arrived in the final with just enough left in us, but we fought until the very end, like we always did.

“We came very close to winning it again, and despite everything that was said about us, nothing strange happened. The match against England took a lot out of us because we gave absolutely everything.

“In 2022, we had the dream of fulfilling not only my dream, but the dream of an entire country: becoming world champions again. And we did it.”

Messi’s Argentina tale one of perseverance

Many of his team-mates openly wept as Messi spoke, reflecting on an international career that started with a red card a minute into his debut against Hungary in 2005 and ended at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

In between, his Argentina journey was one of two halves. The first saw him struggle for acceptance from a public that watched Messi leave for Europe aged 13 and become a focal point for Barcelona.

He struggled to live up to comparisons with Diego Maradona and, following a fourth final defeat in nine years, Messi retired from international football in 2016 after missing in a penalty shoot-out as Argentina lost the Copa America final to Chile.

He was persuaded to return but his Argentina career did not really take off until the appointment of Lionel Scaloni as coach. Scaloni found a way to build around Messi and win trophies with two Copas America and, most importantly, the 2022 World Cup all falling Argentina’s way.

The 2026 World Cup was a collective disappointment – Argentina’s behaviour in the final casting a shadow over their run to the final – but Messi shone throughout the tournament despite his advancing years.

Scaloni hails Messi as the ‘best in history’

Scaloni said after the game: “It’s been a dream come true. I never thought I’d be the coach of the best footballer in history.

“We are eternally grateful to him for giving us the opportunity to be with him.

“The tears are because so many things are going through my head. Not seeing him any more will be sad. He leaves us with an incredible legacy.

“The feeling of having him on your side is incomparable. I’ve never seen that aura in anyone else in my life.”

Messi is expected to make a swift return to the United States where he is scheduled to play for Inter Miami against DC United on Saturday night.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta signs new four-year contract with Arsenal to become the highest-paid manager in the Premier League
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has extended his stay with Arsenal by signing a new deal
articles.content:
Mikel Arteta signs new four-year contract with Arsenal to become the highest-paid manager in the Premier League

Mikel Arteta has extended his stay with Arsenal by signing a new deal

Last Update:

Arsenal have confirmed Mikel Arteta has signed a new, four-year contract with the Premier League champions.

Talks have been ongoing for several months with the Gunners eager to tie Arteta down after he led the club to the title for the first time in 22 years last season. His previous deal was due to expire next summer but he has now committed to fresh terms worth a reported £20million a year, making him the highest paid manager in the top flight.

Arteta joined Arsenal in December 2019 and, after guiding them to the FA Cup crown six months later, developed a reputation as a nearly man after a series of second-placed finishes in league and cup.

That changed in 2025/26 when Arsenal fended off the challenge of Manchester City to finish top of the Premier League, sparking wild scenes of celebration across the red half of North London.

Arteta told the club’s Arsenal’s website: “It’s a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal. This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.

“We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together. I’m extremely grateful to Stan and Josh for their trust and support, and feel honoured to be leading this club through such a special period in its 140-year history.

“This is such a proud moment for me and my family. I feel the love and respect from our fantastic supporters, and they have mine – and ours – in return.”

Kroenkes delighted Arteta is staying at Arsenal

Arsenal have made a strong start to this season, although their momentum was checked by a 3-0 hammering at Brighton immediately before the international break.

Arsenal co-chairs Stan and Josh Kroenke said: “It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead in this special relationship. Last season was an incredible moment in Arsenal’s history, a moment in which we created memories that will last a lifetime. We’re determined to create many more in the years ahead.

“We share a special bond with Mikel. We are so proud of everything we have achieved since he returned to the club in 2019.

“He has a deep understanding of Arsenal’s values and carries them in his heart. He knows what this club means to everyone connected to it and is committed to building on everything we have achieved together.”

Club CEO Richard Garlick added: “This is an important time in Arsenal Football Club’s history. We want to create a winning era together with Mikel. We will continue to work hard together as we aim to fulfil our long-term ambitions for the club and our supporters.

“Mikel has the belief, determination and the understanding of what it takes to build something remarkable and enduring here, and we are excited to continue that journey together.”

Forward together.

Mikel Arteta is here to stay ❤️ https://t.co/c02vnZsUVR

Arteta’s record marks him out as an Arsenal great

Arteta has been in charge of Arsenal for 361 games in all competitions. His win percentage stands at 62.05% – the best of any full-time manager in the club’s history.

The Spaniard’s coaching staff have also penned new deals for the same four-year duration.

Arsenal return to Premier League action this weekend with a home game against Leeds on Saturday (12:30 BST). Arteta will be eager to return to winning ways after the defeat at the Amex Stadium ended a run of four successive league victories.

articles.title: UEFA Nations League: Scotland promotion hopes dealt crushing blow by Slovenia turnaround
articles.summary: Scotland look likely to miss out on the promotion play-offs as well.
articles.content:
UEFA Nations League: Scotland promotion hopes dealt crushing blow by Slovenia turnaround

Scotland look likely to miss out on the promotion play-offs as well.

Last Update:

Scotland‘s hopes of automatic UEFA Nations League promotion are over following a 2-1 home defeat to Slovenia.

Sebastien Pocognoli’s men were looking to build on their 2-0 win in North Macedonia last time out, and took the lead on the half-hour mark when Ryan Christie bundled home from close range.

But Aljosa Matko slotted into the bottom-left corner in the 56th minute to level matters for Slovenia, who then completed the turnaround as Danijel Sturm capped a fine move down the right-hand side with a simple finish from Matko’s cross.

There were boos at Hampden Park from the home fans as Scotland slumped to a second defeat in four games, leaving them third in Group 1 in League B with just four points to their name.

And, with Switzerland easing to a 3-0 win over North Macedonia thanks in part to goals from Johan Manzambi and Dan Ndoye, Scotland cannot top the group, their eight-point gap to the leaders an unassailable one with two games remaining.

They are three points behind Slovenia, who occupy the promotion play-off spot in the group. With head-to-head record the tiebreaker, Scotland must better Slovenia’s results over the final two games next month to leapfrog them into that spot.

In League C, San Marino suffered heartbreak as they were denied a famous draw with Albania by a 93rd-minute penalty.

Kristjan Asllani broke the deadlock for Albania in the 11th minute to seemingly put them on course for a routine win against the perennial whipping boys.

But Lorenzo Lazzari stunned the crowd in Tirana when he turned home from Lorenzo Capicchioni’s in-swinging cross.

It looked as if that would be enough to earn San Marino a point, however, there was a crushing sting in the tail for the minnows when captain Fabbri was ruled to have handled in the area following a VAR review, allowing Asllani to rescue Albania and seal a 2-1 win by finding the bottom-right corner from 12 yards.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo hits out at Jorge Jesus in lengthy statement but insists he still wants to play for Portugal
articles.summary: Ronaldo said Jesus broke his word twice but still wants to play for his country.
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo hits out at Jorge Jesus in lengthy statement but insists he still wants to play for Portugal

Ronaldo said Jesus broke his word twice but still wants to play for his country.

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has released a lengthy statement insisting he still wishes to play for Portugal while hitting out at coach Jorge Jesus, accusing him of breaking his word in the latest development in the saga around his exit from the national team camp.

Ronaldo left the Portugal squad ahead of their UEFA Nations League match with Denmark last week, with Portugal’s record goalscorer seemingly furious after being an unused substitute in their away win over Norway.

Portugal subsequently beat Denmark and completed a double over Norway without Ronaldo to clinch their place in the Nations League quarter-finals with two games to spare.

Jesus said the door remains open for the 41-year-old to return to the national team. However, it has been reported that Ronaldo will not play for Portugal while Jesus is in charge, the Al-Nassr forward said to be upset that no public apology was offered by the coach during his most recent press conference.

Ronaldo: Jesus broke his word to me

Ronaldo’s statement confirmed his annoyance at Jesus’ lack of public contrition, but made it clear he has not retired from international football and still wants to compete for his country.

It read: “This is the truth on what has happened with Jorge Jesus.

“As I promised, I decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances surrounding the last training camp of the National Team.

“After the 2026 World Cup I prepared a letter to the Portuguese people, which I still keep, with the words I want to address to them when I leave our team for good.

“At the end of the competition, already on the flight back from the United States, the President of the Federation asked and insisted that I reconsider the decision to leave, because the FPF wanted me to continue.

“Right afterwards he asked me for my opinion on the name of the current head coach, which he was considering alongside other names he did not reveal to me.

“I told the President of the Federation that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice.

“That is why, on the day the current head coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results are confirming.

“A few days later I received a first contact from the new national team coach saying he would like to meet me in person. I said yes and we scheduled it for the end of my holidays.

“We met at the Cidade do Futebol [FPF training complex], where my club was holding its pre-season training camp.

“That day the coach told me he was counting on me and that my presence was fundamental to his project. He presented me, right there, with a plan for my participation. He told me I would play the first match [against Wales] and the last one [against Norway], and that for reasons of physical management he would always make three to four changes per match.

“At that point he raised the possibility of me not travelling with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He proposed that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then rejoin before the match at the Dragao.

“I refused this proposal immediately. It seemed obvious to me that I could not accept it. It was not because I would not play the matches abroad that I would stop captaining our team. That privilege of staying in Portugal would not be a good example.

“The coach ended up agreeing with my analysis.

“This conversation was attended by Simão Coutinho, sporting director of Al Nassr, the person to whom the current coach reported throughout last season and one of those responsible for his signing by the club in 2025.

“On the eve of the start of the camp the coach came to my house in Lisbon, at his request, for another conversation with me. The conversation was calm and all the principles agreed in August were maintained.

“I played the match at Alvalade and, although substituted, I made no problem of it. I put the armband on Bruno Fernandes myself, far from imagining that I might be taking my last steps as a player and captain of the National Team. What mattered to me that day was our victory. Winning is always good; in Portugal and for my country, even better.

“At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, an assistant to the coach came to the table where the group was having lunch and informed me that the coach wanted to speak to me.

“To my absolute surprise, the coach asked me if I was fit to play 30 minutes. I was fully focused on my physical recovery, integrated with my teammates as always, and thinking that I would not play that day. Without any problem.

“This request was something outside my physical recovery and training plan — because I was only going to play on the fourth at the Dragão — but of course I said yes. He replied that I should then be ready because I would play 30 minutes.The rest everyone knows. I warmed up from half-time, watched the minutes go by, and was not called.

“The coach had broken his word to me.”

Explaining his decision to walk straight down the tunnel rather than greeting the celebrating Portugal fans after the away win over Norway, Ronaldo added: “At the end of the match I only wanted everything to finish with the victory and to be alone. I did not go to greet the fans. A failing that is solely my responsibility and that should not have happened.

“I apologise to the Portuguese who supported us intensely there, I apologise to the fans, and I apologise to those who, without being Portuguese, may have travelled there to see me and whom I may have disappointed.

“Forty-eight hours later we had a conversation — myself, the coach and Simão Coutinho — since he had been the one accompanying our conversations in August. It was a deep moment, very frank, without any kind of filter.

“We agreed that there was only one way to close this “case”: that the coach repeat what he had just told me in private, in the presence of Simão Coutinho, but in the press room.

“What was agreed was simple: the coach would begin the press conference with this subject, seeking to close the matter by telling the truth. He would say that I never asked to play any minutes, that it was the coach and no one else who proposed the plan for this camp to me, and that it was a mistake to put me on to warm up and then not bring me on, and that if it happened again he would not do it.

“We ended that meeting with the coach asking me for a hug, promising me that he would say at the conference what he had just said to me, and that the matter would be overcome. I would not play in Denmark and I would play the match at the Dragão. All of this in the presence of Simão Coutinho, always.

“At the coach’s request, a meeting then took place between himself, Simão Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro by videoconference, in which what we had discussed was summarised.

“A short document was produced which I myself validated and which, with my knowledge, was delivered to the coach, as he had requested.

“The conference was what is known: the posture had nothing to do with our meeting; I heard expressions and an aggressiveness that I do not believe I deserved, an attitude of “I want, I can and I command” that he never showed me, not even remotely, in private the day before.”

“The notes I validated were the following:

“I think it is important, also because it is the truth, to clarify a few things before talking about Denmark:

“None of these notes, therefore, said that the coach should even apologise to me.

“It was the second time he had broken his word to me.”

Ronaldo insists he is available for Portugal

Ronaldo went on to apologise to his team-mates for leaving the camp, before stressing that he remains available for selection.

“I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further breach of word,” he explained. “For me the truth is still the most important thing in the relationship between people. However much it hurts, let them tell me the truth.

“In fact, in a conversation I had with the President of the FPF and with the coach on the morning of the day of that press conference — they can certainly confirm this — I reaffirmed that if they did not want me there they should tell me. It was enough for them to be frank with me. I would accept that and I promised that we would prepare something beautiful, as I dream will happen, and no one would be left angry.

“I remember it as if it were today. They replied in unison that no. That my place was in the National Team.

“Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career.

“I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.

“I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp.

“Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine.

“I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of one’s word has, for me, a defining impact. I felt that, from that point on, my remaining would only harm the working group, and I did what I have always said I would do if I did not feel useful: I packed my bags and left.

“The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor.

“I have already apologised, but I know that attitudes must have consequences. Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.

“On this subject, I have heard a great deal of talk about farewell matches, that I must have a dignified farewell and that the Federation wants to give me that opportunity.

“I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone.

“I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.

“But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing. That is what I thought on the day I was given the news of my father’s death.

“I was at a camp with our national team and I decided to stay there until the end of the match the following day. I did for the country what I would never do for any club.

“Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team.

“This is, believe me, the purest of truths. Cristiano Ronaldo.”

articles.title: Martin O’Neill clears up Celtic future after ‘time of reflection’
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill still believes he is the right man to lead Celtic.
articles.content:
Martin O’Neill clears up Celtic future after ‘time of reflection’

Martin O'Neill still believes he is the right man to lead Celtic.

Last Update:

Martin O’Neill has insisted he remains the right man to lead Celtic and is “raring to go” after using the international break to reflect on his future.

The 74-year-old appeared to cast doubt over his managerial career following a difficult run of results last month, admitting “it might be time to wrap it up” after Celtic suffered two defeats against Rangers.

Those losses came either side of a 3-1 home defeat to Ferencvaros in the Europa League, placing O’Neill under pressure despite his success since returning to Parkhead.

However, Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson publicly backed the experienced manager and O’Neill has now made clear that he intends to continue.

“I am extremely prepared now for it,” O’Neill said in an interview with the club.

“We had a difficult week. That can happen. You can lose to your arch-rivals, you can lose the European game.

“It’s certainly not the end of the world as it seemed to be described as. I thought I would take a bit of time, and it didn’t take me that much time to think about it.”

Celtic boss targets another league title

O’Neill returned to Celtic last season and ultimately had two spells in interim charge before signing a one-year contract to remain as manager.

His return proved successful as Celtic completed a league and Scottish Cup double, but their recent run prompted questions over whether he would see out his latest spell in Glasgow.

The Northern Irishman has now dismissed those doubts and set his sights on delivering further silverware.

“I want to lead the club, I want to try to win the league and I’m just as determined now than ever before,” O’Neill said.

“It was a time of reflection for a moment or two, but overall, I’m back, I’m raring to go and the team’s ready.”

articles.title: Liverpool handed huge injury concern ahead of Manchester City clash
articles.summary: Liverpool are sweating on the fitness of one of their stars.
articles.content:
Liverpool handed huge injury concern ahead of Manchester City clash

Liverpool are sweating on the fitness of one of their stars.

Last Update:

Liverpool are waiting to discover the extent of Jeremy Jacquet’s hamstring injury after the defender missed France’s 4-1 Nations League win over Belgium on Monday.

Jacquet had featured in France’s previous two matches, earning his first senior international appearances, but was left out of Zinedine Zidane’s squad for the win over Belgium.

The French Football Federation confirmed that the 21-year-old had suffered a “strain to his left hamstring.”

Zidane offered a more encouraging update, describing Jacquet as “slightly injured.”

Liverpool will now assess the centre-back following his return from international duty, with Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Manchester City at Anfield quickly approaching.

Any absence would be a significant blow for Andoni Iraola given Jacquet’s importance during the opening weeks of the campaign.

Liverpool face nervous wait before Man City

Jacquet has featured in all seven of Liverpool’s matches this season and started six of them alongside Virgil van Dijk in central defence.

Iraola does have alternatives available should the Frenchman be ruled out against City.

Ronald Araujo, who joined on loan from Barcelona, could step into the starting XI, while the experienced Joe Gomez provides another option in central defence.

However, Jacquet is not Liverpool’s only injury concern ahead of the weekend.

Alexander Isak returned early from international duty with Sweden after suffering a minor thigh problem, while Cody Gakpo’s involvement with the Netherlands was also cut short.

Gakpo sustained an ankle injury and appears to be the greater concern of the two forwards as Liverpool assess their squad before facing City.

articles.title: Benin don’t plan to mark Lionel Messi as defender reveals they want to give Argentina star the perfect send-off
articles.summary: There could be a cricket score in Buenos Aires tonight with Benin seemingly having no plan to spoil Lionel Messi's party
articles.content:
Benin don’t plan to mark Lionel Messi as defender reveals they want to give Argentina star the perfect send-off

There could be a cricket score in Buenos Aires tonight with Benin seemingly having no plan to spoil Lionel Messi's party

Last Update:

Benin are seemingly ready to party with Lionel Messi on Tuesday night with defender Tijani Mohamed admitting the African side are going to “give everything so that this celebration goes really well”.

Messi will bring the curtain down on his Argentina career in Buenos Aires with a special farewell game in front of an adoring crowd at the Estadio Monumental.

And it appears the adulation also extends to the visitors’ dressing room.

Mohamed told Argentinian TV station C5N: “We don’t need to mark Messi. We are going to enjoy this match. There’s no special plan to defend against Messi, we just have to enjoy this game, and that’s it. I’m going to look at him like this: ‘Messi, you are God’.

“For me he’s the best in the world.”

Benin want to enjoy celebrations with hero Messi

Messi will make his 208th and final appearance for his country and he appears a good bet to increase his goal tally that currently stands at 125 if Mohamed’s approach is anything to go by.

The centre-half, who is currently without a club after his deal at Swiss second division side Yverdon-Sport was terminated last month, says he is totally committed to ensuring his hero gets the send-off he deserves.

He added: “Benin is a very, very good team to play with, but I can’t talk about Benin right now because we have to enjoy this match, and we’re going to give everything so that this celebration goes really well.”

Messi is irreplaceable – Argentina boss Scaloni

It promises to be an emotional night with Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni conceding his side will struggle to replace the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, considered by many pundits to be the greatest player of all time.

“Leo is irreplaceable,” said Scaloni at Monday’s press conference. “We will seek to continue playing with the same identity, with the idea of being united and playing as a team. It is obvious that without Messi everything changes, but the national team has an identity and the challenge is to continue playing this way, that the guys who come join that cause.”

articles.title: Julian Alvarez makes major agent decision after Arsenal and Barcelona transfer saga
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez is looking to change agents after failing to get a move away from Atletico Madrid in the summer.
articles.content:
Julian Alvarez makes major agent decision after Arsenal and Barcelona transfer saga

Julian Alvarez is looking to change agents after failing to get a move away from Atletico Madrid in the summer.

Last Update:

Julian Alvarez is considering ending his long-standing relationship with agent Fernando Hidalgo.

The Argentina international worked with Hidalgo for almost a decade, but Alvarez and his family are now assessing alternative representation following a turbulent summer surrounding his future.

According to AS, the striker’s inner circle has been searching for a new agency since the transfer window closed, with his father Gustavo Alvarez playing an important role in the process.

An Argentine agency with links to former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Javier Pastore is reportedly leading the race to represent Alvarez.

Negotiations are said to have reached an advanced stage, although an agreement has not yet been formally signed.

Atletico defended Alvarez after transfer saga

Alvarez was heavily linked with a move away from Atletico, with Barcelona and Arsenal among the clubs associated with the forward.

Despite the speculation, he remained in Madrid after the transfer deadline and is under contract with Atletico until 2030.

The situation created tension around the club, although Atletico’s hierarchy reportedly did not blame Alvarez himself for how events unfolded.

Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin publicly defended the striker at the end of August and suggested attempts had been made to mislead the player during the transfer saga.

A change in the striker’s representation could therefore help ease some of the tension surrounding his future and reset his relationship with Atletico following the events of the summer.

Alvarez focused on Argentina duty

For now, Alvarez is concentrating on his responsibilities with Argentina rather than the uncertainty surrounding his representation.

The forward is away with the national team as they prepare to face Benin in a fixture expected to have added significance because of Lionel Messi’s final appearance.

Messi has been an important influence on Alvarez during his international career, with the pair playing alongside each other during Argentina’s recent period of success.

Alvarez is expected to return to Madrid at the end of the week, when attention will again turn towards his future off the pitch.

articles.title: Why Lamine Yamal was left off 2026 Golden Boy shortlist
articles.summary: Why was Lamine Yamal not nominated for the 2026 Golden Boy shortlist?
articles.content:
Why Lamine Yamal was left off 2026 Golden Boy shortlist

Why was Lamine Yamal not nominated for the 2026 Golden Boy shortlist?

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal is not among the final candidates for the 2026 Golden Boy award despite the Barcelona star remaining one of the most highly-rated young players in world football.

The final shortlist has been revealed after the field was cut down from an initial group of 50 players, with 25 of Europe’s leading Under-21 talents remaining in contention for the prize.

Yamal’s absence immediately stood out given his performances for Barcelona and Spain, but his omission has nothing to do with his form or credentials.

A player cannot win the award more than once and Yamal has already claimed the honour, having been named Golden Boy in 2024.

That previous success means he is automatically ineligible to compete for the award again.

Who is competing for the 2026 Golden Boy award?

The Golden Boy prize was established by Italian newspaper Tuttosport in 2003 and recognises the leading young footballer playing in Europe.

With Yamal unable to win for a second time, several of the continent’s most promising talents are competing to succeed him among the award’s list of winners.

Barcelona are still represented by Pau Cubarsi, Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart, while Real Madrid have Endrick and Yan Diomande among the contenders.

Premier League representation includes Chelsea duo Estevao and Jorrel Hato, Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly, Brighton pair Charalampos Kostoulas and Luka Vuskovic and Bournemouth’s Junior Kroupi and Rayan.

Manchester City’s Ayoub Bouaddi also features, alongside Bayern Munich’s Lennart Karl, Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Warren Zaire-Emery and Borussia Dortmund duo Joshua Gado and Konstantinos Karetsas.

Rodrigo Mora, Franco Mastantuono, Finn Jeltsch, Kerim Alajbegovic, Said El Mala, Jon Martin, Gianluca Prestianni and Victor Froholdt are also among those competing for the award.

Yamal primed for Ballon d’Or push

Instead, Lamine Yamal will be hoping to get his hands on the coveted Ballon d’Or later this month.

The 19-year-old appears to be facing up against Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane for the award.

Polls show the Spaniard neck-and-neck with the former Tottenham man, but Yamal will be keen to become the first Barcelona player to receive the Ballon d’Or since Lionel Messi.

articles.title: Jamie Carragher calls for multi-year Manchester City punishment after guilty charges
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has had his say on Manchester City's potential punishment from the Premier League.
articles.content:
Jamie Carragher calls for multi-year Manchester City punishment after guilty charges

Jamie Carragher has had his say on Manchester City's potential punishment from the Premier League.

Last Update:

Jamie Carragher believes Manchester City should face sanctions lasting between three and five years if their appeal against the Premier League’s financial verdict is unsuccessful.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaching the league’s financial rules, ruling that they inflated their revenue by more than £830 million across nine seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

No final punishment has been imposed while the appeal process remains ongoing, but Carragher believes a one-season points deduction would not provide a sufficient deterrent if the verdict is upheld.

Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate, the former Liverpool defender argued that any sanction should instead affect City across multiple campaigns.

“If the people talk about [a penalty of] 80 points or 100 points, but that’s just over one season that gets you relegated and then you come back again,” Carragher said.

“And I think players, a few of them would leave, but I think some of them would say, ‘I could put up with that for a year.’

“But I think, because this has gone on for so long, I do think the punishment should be over a number of years, three to five years, and then players would move on.”

City await outcome of appeal

Carragher’s proposal would potentially have a far greater long-term impact on City’s squad than a punishment confined to a single campaign.

An 80 or 100-point deduction would almost certainly leave a club facing relegation, but Carragher believes City’s resources could allow them to retain much of their squad and quickly return to the Premier League.

A sanction spread across several seasons, he argues, could make it considerably more difficult to convince leading players to remain at the Etihad.

The controversy surrounding City will provide the backdrop to their return to Premier League action against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

The two clubs have been major rivals for domestic honours over recent years and City can expect a difficult reception on Merseyside following the financial verdict.

Former City defender and manager Stuart Pearce believes Enzo Maresca must use the increased hostility as motivation for his players.

“The opposition, they’ll be rolling their sleeves up,” Pearce said. “The atmosphere in the stadiums is going to be red hot. It’s unbelievable it happens to be Liverpool this weekend. It’s going to be electric.

“So it’s going to stimulate everybody else against City, and it’s got to stimulate City against everyone else.”
