articles.title: As Lionel Messi stands aside, we ask: Who is the best player in the world right now?
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi departs the international stage, who will stand up and take his crown as the best footballer in the world? We look at the candidates...
articles.content:
As Lionel Messi stands aside, we ask: Who is the best player in the world right now?

As Lionel Messi departs the international stage, who will stand up and take his crown as the best footballer in the world? We look at the candidates...

Last Update:

Lionel Messi plays his final game for Argentina tonight – bringing an end to a magnificent international career and also his eligibility for the title of best player in the world.

Messi was still a contender while appearing on the global stage and his performances in the World Cup over the summer did little to dispel the theory that, even at 39 years of age, he had a legitimate claim.

But his departure from the international game means he will play out his final seasons in Major League Soccer and it would be hard to justify his position as top dog when bullying the opposition for Inter Miami.

Therefore, the stage is cleared for new contenders to assume the mantle of the world’s best. Three of our candidates have been around for some time but with Messi (and to a lesser extent Cristiano Ronaldo, who has been a fading force for a while now) heading into the sunset, they can make their pitches.

There are many players whose numbers defy belief and so there’s an element of personal taste in our selections, as well as the eye-test; which player do you enjoy watching, who gets you off your seat?

Here’s our top five:

5. Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)Long talked about as the heir to Messi and Ronaldo, the France striker continues to score goals at an impressive rate at the Santiago Bernabeu and successive Pichichi awards demonstrate his ruthlessness. A career record of 381 goals in 491 club appearances speaks volumes while his strike rate on the international stage – 67 in 107 – is equally formidable.

But there is no denying his move to Madrid has not worked out as planned. Mbappe was brought in to solidify Madrid’s status as the best side in Europe – they won the Champions League two days before his switch to the Spanish capital was confirmed. And yet it has not materialised. Madrid have flopped in the competition since and also fallen behind Barcelona in Spain.

At 27, you could justifiably argue Mbappe’s best days are behind him. His blistering acceleration will start to dwindle while he has already started to sustain niggling injuries that threaten to dilute his influence.

4. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich)Kane has shown Mbappe how to evolve as a footballer while not losing his predatory instincts. Watch Bayern or England and you’re struck by how deep Kane drops, often picking the ball up from the central defenders, to manipulate the game. His range of passing has improved over the years and the way he finds space using an economy of movement is reminiscent of Messi. And then there’s the stats…213 goals in 317 Premier League games for Tottenham and 152 in 154 appearances in all competitions for Bayern.

He’s also England’s record goalscorer and will soon overtake Peter Shilton’s record of 125 appearances.

Kane is 33 years of age but is poised to sign a new deal with Bayern and it’s easy to see why the German champions are eager to tie him down. His game is no longer just about scoring goals, he creates, he leads and he inspires. He has yet to land a major piece of silverware – the Champions League, European Championship or World Cup – but it wouldn’t be a major surprise if that record changed over the next few years.

3. Rodri (Barcelona)The conductor for Spain’s orchestra. The man who makes everything tick for the best international team in the world. Rodri makes football look ridiculously easy. The best defensive midfielder in the game without any doubt, the 30-year-old is one of only two non-forwards to have won the Ballon d’Or in the last 20 years – Luka Modric the other midfield recipient in an era dominated by Messi and Ronaldo.

Rodri has won every major honour, individually and collectively, available in the game. He won the domestic set at Manchester City and both the Euros and World Cup with Spain.

A summer move to Barcelona makes it almost inevitable he will replicate his achievements with City in Spain as well. Strong, physical when necessary but supremely gifted on the ball, Rodri possesses every quality required.

2. Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)What Yamal’s achieved at just 19 years of age is ridiculous. Already a European Championship and World Cup winner, the Barcelona and Spain winger is destined for superstardom for the next decade and beyond. Having made his Barcelona debut at 15, it is easy to forget just how much time he has to improve further, and that is a frightening thought. As a Camp Nou favourite, and also occupying the right-wing role, it is easy to make comparisons with Messi but Yamal’s record at this stage is more impressive. He has already made over 150 appearances for Barca and has three La Liga titles on his CV as well as the 2025 Copa del Rey.

As important as the numbers is the joy he brings, the dancing feet, the drops of the shoulder, the bursts of pace – he passes the eye test with flying colours. He also possesses a swagger, an on-field arrogance that is hard to ignore.

Yamal’s challenge is to maintain this level for the next decade. If he does, he would’ve built a record to challenge Messi’s.

1. Michael Olise (Bayern Munich)This selection may raise a few eyebrows and, admittedly, it does rely more on the eye test than some of the other candidates but when you watch Michael Olise play football, you see greatness in the making. Barca fans will no doubt disagree but he has the highest ceiling of any player on this list. The way he moves, the way he dictates games, the moments of outrageous brilliance that mark him out as a very special footballer. All delivered with a nonchalance, a Gallic shrug that indicates it was nothing out of the ordinary for a man which such natural gifts.

Olise has been special for some time but, this season, he has hit new heights. Twelve goal involvements in seven games for Bayern across domestic and European games highlights his brilliance while his recent appearances for France prove he is playing a different game to most at international level as well. Across Zinedine Zidane’s first four games as France coach, Olise has contributed four goals and two assists. Zidane, arguably one of the greatest players of all time, described him as “exceptional”.

At 24, the world is his to conquer…

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s 10 Greatest Moments For Argentina
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi prepares to play his final game for Argentina, we take a look at his finest moments on the international stage.
articles.content:
Lionel Messi’s 10 Greatest Moments For Argentina

As Lionel Messi prepares to play his final game for Argentina, we take a look at his finest moments on the international stage.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on one of the greatest international careers football has ever seen when he represents Argentina for the final time against Benin on Tuesday.

The 39-year-old is set to make his 208th and final appearance for his country at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, more than 21 years after his senior debut against Hungary in August 2005.

Messi will bow out as Argentina’s record appearance-maker and goalscorer, having found the net 125 times in 207 games.

His relationship with the national team has not always been straightforward. For years, Messi was judged against Diego Maradona and criticised for failing to reproduce his Barcelona brilliance in an Argentina shirt, with defeats in the 2014 World Cup final and three Copa America finals adding to the pressure.

But the final years of his international career completely transformed that story. Copa America glory finally arrived in 2021 before Messi led Argentina to the World Cup in Qatar 18 months later, while another Copa America triumph followed in 2024.

articles.title: Nations League: Italy go second with Turkey win as Northern Ireland held but remain top
articles.summary: Catch up on all of Monday's action in the Nations League
articles.content:
Nations League: Italy go second with Turkey win as Northern Ireland held but remain top

Catch up on all of Monday's action in the Nations League

Last Update:

A host of nations concluded their international period on Monday with their fourth games in the Nations League.

France completed a dramatic win over Belgium, while Italy took on Turkey, Northern Ireland hosted Georgia and Ukraine faced Hungary.

Check out our rundown of all the results below, while you can check out our in-depth report for the France vs Belgium game using the link above.

Italy 3-1 Turkey

Italy continued their impressive resurgence under Roberto Mancini in the Nations League with a 3-1 victory over Turkey in Bologna.

Gianluca Scamacca opened the scoring before Aral Simsir equalised for the visitors, but Riccardo Calafiori quickly restored Italy’s lead with his first international goal.

Francesco Pio Esposito then added a late third to seal another impressive win for Mancini’s side.

Ukraine 1-2 Hungary

Hungary claimed a crucial 2-1 victory over Ukraine to move level on points with their opponents in Group B2.

Milan Toth put Hungary ahead before Roman Yaremchuk levelled for Ukraine, but Mark Csinger struck five minutes later to restore the visitors’ lead and secure three points.

Northern Ireland 0-0 Georgia

Northern Ireland were held to a goalless draw by Georgia in Belfast despite having the chance to win it from the penalty spot.

Isaac Price saw his late spot-kick saved by Georgia goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili, leaving Northern Ireland still unbeaten but unable to extend their lead at the top of Group B2.

Bosnia and Herzegovina 1-0 Poland

Bosnia and Herzegovina secured a crucial 1-0 victory over Poland thanks to Ivan Basic’s late penalty.

The midfielder struck in the 84th minute to settle a tight contest and move Bosnia onto five points, keeping them firmly in the Group B4 promotion race.

Romania 0-1 Sweden

Sweden maintained their unbeaten start with a narrow victory over Romania in Bucharest.

Viktor Gyokeres scored the only goal after 12 minutes, giving Sweden another important three points at the top end of Group B4.

Cyprus 2-1 Latvia

Cyprus came from behind to beat Latvia 2-1 in Group C2. Eduards Daskevics put Latvia ahead after the break, but Ioannis Pittas equalised before Marcus Edwards scored in stoppage time to complete the comeback.

Montenegro 0-0 Armenia

Montenegro were held to a goalless draw by Armenia, missing the chance to strengthen their position at the top of Group C2. Armenia defended resolutely to claim a valuable point away from home.

articles.content:
Tottenham handed Micky van de Ven injury boost ahead of Manchester United clash

Micky van de Ven's injury he picked up on international duty is not believed to be too serious.

Last Update:

Tottenham have been handed a positive update on Micky van de Ven after the defender was forced off during the Netherlands’ 2-1 Nations League win over Serbia.

Van de Ven suffered a hand injury after Serbia striker Luka Jovic landed on him during Sunday’s match and was unable to continue.

The sight of the Spurs captain leaving the pitch provided another potential injury concern for Roberto De Zerbi ahead of the return of Premier League football.

However, Netherlands head coach Xavi played down the severity of the problem after the match, describing it as “not a big problem.”

Spurs travel to Old Trafford looking for their first Premier League win of the season after a difficult opening five matches.

King backs Van de Ven as Tottenham captain

Former Tottenham captain Ledley King believes Van de Ven has developed into the right player to lead the club.

King praised the Netherlands international’s individual qualities but believes the next stage of his development will involve raising the standards of those around him.

“I think he’s a fantastic player. His new role now is to make the players around him better,” King said.

“I think Micky takes care of himself. His ability to recover and put fires out is something we’ve seen over the last few years. That’s an important element for the team.

“So, I think the next role is to manage the group and get the best out of the group as a team.

“He’s grown into the role. Having seen Micky on the pitch, he leads by example, for sure and I think he was the right choice to be captain.”

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel hails King Kane as he prepares to equal England appearance record
articles.summary: Harry Kane will match Peter Shilton's England appearance record when he leads out the Three Lions against Czechia on Tuesday night
articles.content:
Thomas Tuchel hails King Kane as he prepares to equal England appearance record

Harry Kane will match Peter Shilton's England appearance record when he leads out the Three Lions against Czechia on Tuesday night

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel believes Harry Kane’s move to Bayern Munich has taken him to a new level with the England captain set to match a long-standing Three Lions record against Czechia on Tuesday night.

Kane comes into the Nations League clash one short of Peter Shilton’s all-time appearance record of 125 and will equal the former Southampton and Nottingham Forest goalkeeper’s mark when he leads England out at Wembley.

The 33-year-old, who netted twice in Saturday’s 7-0 hammering of Croatia to increase his England record tally to 89, joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 and has helped the club to two Bundesliga titles and one DFB-Pokal.

Former Bayern boss Tuchel said: ”I’m not sure I have anymore words [for Kane].

“He’s on the shortlist for the Ballon d’Or. We’ve spoken so often about him and I try to find new words which then make no sense!

“Everything he does, he does it on the highest level, he does it consecutively and I am very sure he will be the one leading the team out onto the training pitch, he will lead the team in the warm-up and not do one step less or one step slower. That is the level he has.

“Since he took this major role for Bayern Munich, he found a new level. It’s the highest level, on and off the pitch.”

England star Kane a goalscoring machine

Kane’s numbers continue to mark him out as one of the best number nines of his generation.

He is second on the all-time Premier League goalscoring list with 213 and has hit another 152 in just 154 games in all competitions for Bayern.

“All these number nines in world football, no matter in which league, they are built a bit different,” added Tuchel.

“They don’t only do it so their team wins, they also do it for themselves and for the records, ‘how many can I score? How many can I assist? Where is the next record?’

“That’s what drives them and it’s good that drives them. You will not find a striker of this calibre who does not have these individual goals.”

England suffer injury blows with Scott and Konsa ruled out

It wasn’t all good news for Tuchel on Monday, though, with Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa having to return to their clubs due to injury.

Konsa’s is not thought to be serious but Scott could be facing up to two months on the sidelines with a quad issue.

“With Alex, it’s a strange one, I’m very sad about it,” said Tuchel. “He trained in full before Croatia, did extra work after the training sessions, we knew he was in treatment but there were only green lights from him and the medics.

“When we were aware there was slight discomfort during the match and asked if he wanted to come off he said no. After the match, he said he could have played 90 minutes and didn’t feel an injury.

“Even before the scan he didn’t feel injured so it’s a strange one. There was zero risk taken from our side.”

Bournemouth unhappy at Scott injury

Bournemouth are thought to be unhappy with England’s treatment of Scott and Tuchel has sympathy with the Premier League strugglers.

“On a human level, I feel bad that he does not get his next cap tomorrow,” he said. “In my mind, he [would have] started tomorrow.

“I would not have taken any risk, even if it was a big opportunity for him. We wanted him to start but if we had the slightest idea it was a risk [to play him], we would not have taken it. We never do this. We – the medical and physical department – are always in communication with all the players who are with us.

“We share information, this is a totally open process. I can understand that Bournemouth are not happy because they lose a key player. But I can just say that from the moment we took the decision there was absolutely no risk apparent to me or our physical staff. It’s a one off.”

On Konsa, Tuchel added: “Ezri felt discomfort when he came into camp, played with it against Spain and it got a bit worse so he stayed in camp and tried everything for the match against Czechia and it came too soon.

“He tried everything for the game in Croatia, got the green light and came through all the training sessions so was ready to play.

“Unfortunately, he got another hit on the quad and that caused a light trauma and we decided not to let him play through this pain, so he left camp to get treatment for both his issues now. I think nothing major but not worth the risk taking.

articles.title: Manchester City star Haaland not injured but fatigued as he jets away for mini-break
articles.summary: Erling Haaland will recharge his batteries with a mini-break before returning to the chaos surrounding Manchester City
articles.content:
Manchester City star Haaland not injured but fatigued as he jets away for mini-break

Erling Haaland will recharge his batteries with a mini-break before returning to the chaos surrounding Manchester City

Last Update:

Norway coach Stale Solbakken defended Erling Haaland and several other Premier League players after they hired a private jet and made a swift getaway from Porto last night.

Just half an hour after the final whistle sounded at the Estadio do Dragao following Norway’s 2-1 defeat to Portugal, Haaland, Martin Odegaard, Sander Berge and Kristoffer Ajer were spotted getting into a minibus and being whisked to a local airport to travel back to England.

It is believed from there they will disappear for a short holiday before the Premier League resumes this weekend.

Solbakken told VG: “It wasn’t just Haaland who left early. There’s a whole bunch of people leaving now. They need a breather. They have been given a few days off from their clubs.

“I understand that they book a private plane when they have two or three days off. You have to remember that the teams that went far in the World Cup have many players who have had minimal holiday time. Then it’s right into the start of the season and then a mini international tournament. It’s an extreme strain.”

Haaland went off due to exhaustion

Haaland lasted 67 minutes of the game against Portugal before signalling to come off. He was spotted with a slight limp when leaving the stadium but Solbakken said the substation was always pre planned.

He added: “We were hoping for 60 minutes after the conversation we had yesterday, and he managed just over 65.”

When he returns from his mini-holiday, Haaland will walk into the maelstrom that has been absorbing Manchester City while he has been away.

City were found guilty on 114 charges of financial malpractice and also of obfuscating the investigation. They have denied any wrongdoing and last week appealed the verdict.

Former Borussia Dortmund star Haaland has not spoken on the subject since linking up with Norway and the City players are likely to be kept away from the media ahead of Sunday’s game at Liverpool.

City can expect a hostile reception at Anfield with Liverpool the club that have arguably suffered more than any other as a result of City’s methods.

Alex Scott facing two-month absence after withdrawing from England squad

Alex Scott is facing a spell on the sidelines due to a quad injury in what will be a bitter blow for Bournemouth

Last Update:

Alex Scott has withdrawn from the England squad and could miss the next two months with a quad injury.

The Bournemouth midfielder sustained the injury during his first international start against Croatia on Saturday, playing 70 minutes before being replaced by Everton’s James Garner.

The 23-year-old will undergo further tests when he returns to the South Coast club but The Athletic are reporting he could be absent for up to eight weeks in what will be a bitter blow to Cherries boss Marco Rose.

He has already been ruled out of Tuesday night’s game with Czechia at Wembley.

Scott stars for Bournemouth

Scott has been a key player for Bournemouth this season, starting all five games, scoring once and adding an assist.

He also made a huge impression with England, looking very comfortable alongside Elliot Anderson and Jude Bellingham in a midfield three that was instrumental in the Three Lions cruising to a 7-0 win in Rijeka.

Scott has grown in prominence since joining Bournemouth in 2023 from Bristol City and is now widely regarded as one of the best young midfielders in the country.

Rose’s side have yet to win in the Premier League this season, recording three draws and two defeats. They visit Chelsea when the league resumes this weekend before home games against Sturm Graz, in the Europa League, and Sunderland.

articles.title: Portuguese chief confident he can solve ‘misunderstanding’ but Jesus won’t apologise to Ronaldo
articles.summary: FPF president Pedro Proenca is confident he can broker peace between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo  and that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner will return to the squad in November
articles.content:
Portuguese chief confident he can solve ‘misunderstanding’ but Jesus won’t apologise to Ronaldo

FPF president Pedro Proenca is confident he can broker peace between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo  and that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner will return to the squad in November

Last Update:

Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca is confident the “misunderstanding” between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo will be resolved and hopes the veteran striker will return to the squad in November.

Ronaldo walked out on the team prior to last week’s Nations League game in Denmark following a row with Jesus that stemmed from the coach’s decision not to bring him off the bench against Norway the previous weekend.

The 41-year-old flew back from Copenhagen in his private jet just hours before the Denmark game and was not considered for last night’s return against the Norwegians in Porto, a game the hosts won 2-1 with Ronaldo’s replacement Goncalo Ramos scoring the deciding goal 11 minutes from time.

Ronaldo will return to action for club side Al-Nassr this Friday and it is hoped a resolution can be found prior to the November international break.

Proenca told RTP: “The FPF is not a house without rules but these dynamics happen within a working group.

“There is a very strong relationship between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo. If that were not the case, maybe Ronaldo would have already retired from the national team. Everything that will happen in the next few days are moments of tranquility, conversation, discussion and what we want is that in November he can be with our squad again.”

Ronaldo is our legend – Proenca

Proenca needs to tread a tricky line in not undermining Jesus but also attempting to smooth the waters for Ronaldo’s return.

“Ronaldo is the best player of all time,” added Proenca. “He has given more than two decades to Portuguese football. Cristiano Ronaldo is the greatest symbol of Portugueseness. He is in the national team for his own sporting merit and this is absolutely unquestionable. He will always be part of this squad whenever he is technically capable. Cristiano knows that this is the feeling.

“On the specific subject, let me say that we are facing a misunderstanding that has to be resolved internally. He’s part of the squad, he’s our legend. He was the captain for the first of these four games. The coach says he counts on him.

“Cristiano Ronaldo is a Portuguese legend, an absolutely extraordinary player who could have ended his career after the World Cup but did not want to do it because of the love he has for his national team. I am a witness of this relationship that Cristiano has with the Portuguese people, with our team. Therefore, now that these four games are over, we will all have time and tranquility to sit down and solve a misunderstanding.

“Ronaldo is part of our heritage and will be here whenever the coach wants him to be.”

Jesus – I won’t apologise to Ronaldo

Jesus said he would be happy to see Ronaldo return but ruled out apologising for not bringing the former Real Madrid superstar off the bench.

“I don’t apologise to anyone,” he said. “The problem that started all of this was that the player was warming up. I made the decision [not to bring him on]. What do I have to apologise for?”

He added: “I don’t know what Cris will decide. I’ve already said what I have to say, but I’ll add, for me, at first it was never a situation. It was something I thought was normal as a coach. There are principles as a coach that are non-negotiable.

“For me Cris will be in the next squad if he is playing for Al-Nassr and he wants to return to the national team. You can’t change, in my opinion, a one-year friendship in a situation that you can’t understand. It was something he created himself, and maybe well because he’s a legend, this whole problem of coming on, warming up, not coming on… How many warmed up today and didn’t come on? Will there be any problem? No. With Cris it’s different, he’s a legend. But is it a problem? It’s not a problem for me. If Cris wants to and is playing for Al-Nassr he will be called up. But it’s Cris who will decide.”

Portugal’s next games are during the November international break when they host Denmark before taking on Wales in Cardiff.

Nations League: Wales lose again as Netherlands go top of group

Catch up on Sunday's Nations League fixtures

Last Update:

Another packed night of Nations League action saw Wales take on Denmark and Netherlands face Serbia in the Nations League Division A.

Check out our round-up of all the action from Sunday, while you can also find in-depth reports for Portugal vs Norway, Greece vs Germany and Republic of Ireland vs Israel.

Wales 0-1 Denmark

Wales suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat to Denmark in Cardiff, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring the only goal from the penalty spot.

Danny Ward had produced several important saves but was punished in the 73rd minute after miskicking a pass and colliding with Gustav Isaksen, allowing Højlund to convert from 12 yards.

Craig Bellamy’s side pushed for an equaliser but could not find a way through as Denmark secured another important three points, with Wales suffering their third defeat in four Nations League games to leave them in danger of relegation from Division A.

articles.title: Teenager Sullivan breaks USMNT record with wonder lob against Mexico
articles.summary: The teenager is set to join Manchester City
articles.content:
Teenager Sullivan breaks USMNT record with wonder lob against Mexico

The teenager is set to join Manchester City

Last Update:

Cavan Sullivan wrote his name into the history books with a sensational goal in the United States’ emphatic 3-0 friendly triumph over fierce rivals Mexico.

The Manchester City-bound wonderkid produced a moment of pure magic at State Farm Stadium, cementing himself as the youngest goalscorer in US men’s national team history.

Remarkably, Mathis Albert (17 years, 131 days) had set the previous milestone just five days earlier against Chile. However, Sullivan shattered that benchmark at the age of just 17 years and five days.

With Mauricio Pochettino’s side already leading thanks to another teenage talent – 18-year-old Julian Hall – Sullivan made his definitive mark just after the hour mark.

Anticipating play brilliantly, the Philadelphia Union star intercepted a pass from Mexico goalkeeper Raúl Rangel before delivering an audacious 62nd-minute lob from distance to double the lead.

Speaking after the game, Sullivan reflected on the dream milestone:

“These are the moments you dream of when you’re a three, four, five or six-year-old,” Sullivan said.

“I manifested this moment, not just these past couple of hours when I found out I was starting, but my whole life.”

Recalling the strike itself, the teenager admitted there were a few anxious seconds as the ball floated toward the net.

“I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn’t hit the crossbar or go over,” Sullivan said.

“I was getting nervous when it was in the air and then everything was a blur.”

Things unravelled further for Mexico shortly after the strike. Substitute Luis Chávez received his marching orders in the 68th minute for pushing his hand into Sebastian Berhalter’s face.

Malik Tillman capped off a dominant display by adding a third in the 84th minute, but the night firmly belonged to Sullivan.

articles.content:
UEFA Nations League: Scotland grab first win while Switzerland and Finland continue strong starts

Catch up on all the action across the continent on Saturday.

Last Update:

Scotland picked up their first three UEFA Nations League points of the campaign, and their first win under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli, as they ran out 2-0 winners over North Macedonia.

Kieron Bowie gave Scotland a seventh-minute lead in Skopje before John McGinn converted a penalty 20 minutes from time to secure an morale-boosting victory for the Tartan Army.

But they had to see out the last few minutes of the game with 10 men after Scott McKenna saw red following a challenge on Eljif Elmas.

It was, however, a dominant display from Scotland on the occasion of captain Andy Robertson’s 100th cap.

The result leaves Scotland third in the table, level on points with second-placed Slovenia, who fell 2-1 to Switzerland.

The Swiss maintained their perfect start to the group thanks to an Erik Janza own goal and Dan Ndoye. Zan Vipotnik had given Slovenia the lead inside the opening two minutes of the match.

Finland maintain unbeaten start

Elsewhere, there was a resounding win for England over Croatia, while world champions Spain extended their impressive unbeaten run against Czechia.

Finland maintained their strong start to this season’s Nations League with a 2-1 victory over Albania.

Rey Manaj had given Albania the early lead before Etrit Berisha was given his marching orders mid-way through the first half.

The numerical advantage proved pivotal as Finland hit back courtesy of a brace from Leo Walta to give Jacob Friis’ men all three points.

They currently sit top of their group having accrued seven points from three games.

Meanwhile, Iceland saw off the challenge of Bulgaria with a 3-0 win. Orri Oskarsson netted two while Mikael Ellertsson added a third in stoppage time.

Belarus thumped San Marino 4-0 thanks to two goals from Artem Kontsevoy (2), Artem Shumansky and Max Ebong, while Estonia edged past Luxembourg courtesy of Rasmus Peetson, who grabbed the only goal of the game after five minutes.

articles.title: Tuchel hails ‘complete performance’ as England thrash Croatia
articles.summary: The hosts suffered their heaviest ever defeat at the hands of the Three Lions on Saturday.
articles.content:
Tuchel hails ‘complete performance’ as England thrash Croatia

The hosts suffered their heaviest ever defeat at the hands of the Three Lions on Saturday.

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel has hailed his side’s “complete performance” as England thrashed Croatia 7-0 in what was one of the most impressive results of the German’s tenure so far.

The Three Lions were ruthless in Rijeka, with both Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka helping themselves to braces, while Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and substitute Morgan Rogers were also on the scoresheet.

Following a disappointing 3-2 defeat to world champions Spain and a rather unspectacular 2-0 victory over Czechia, this appeared to be a real signal of intent from Tuchel’s men against a team with whom England share a rather chequered history in recent years.

However, on Saturday night, a gulf in class was evident, with Tuchel left delighted by the performance of his players.

“Maybe apart from three minutes after the 3-0, a big mistake and some easy ball losses, there was a 90-minute performance from the highest level,” Tuchel told ITV.

“From everyone. From the first until the last minute. Congratulations to the team.

“[We were] very, very impressive. We created so many chances. [It was] so fluid right from the start, it never stopped. Very clinical, stayed hungry, counter-pressing, the basics right. That’s why it was a complete performance.”

England’s ‘frightening’ talent

On a night where all the post-match headlines focussed on the result, plenty of the pre-match buzz centred around Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who was handed his full senior debut for the national team.

And it was an assured showing from the 23-year-old, who more than held his own against an experienced Croatian engine room featuring 41-year-old Luka Modric.

Speaking after the game, Scott admitted there was “no better feeling” and that “to start with a win like that is amazing”.

“We wanted to push Croatia as hard as possible and we did that today… pressing high… winning the ball back … being ruthless in the final third,” he added.

Scott described the talent at England’s disposal right now as “frightening” but insisted the team must “build now” and “go again”.

Scott, Tuchel and co. will not have long to bask in the victory, as they take on Czechia on Tuesday at Wembley, hoping to make it three Nations League wins from four.

articles.title: Mancini hails Italy ‘step forward’ after draw with France
articles.summary: Italy came from behind to take a point in Saint-Denis.
articles.content:
Mancini hails Italy ‘step forward’ after draw with France

Italy came from behind to take a point in Saint-Denis.

Last Update:

Roberto Mancini praised Italy‘s performance in their 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with France as a “step forward”.

After seeing Italy claim a 4-1 win over Turkey to claim their first victory of his second spell in charge last time out, Mancini was treated to another impressive display from his side against much more illustrious opposition at a raucous Stade de France.

It looked as if Italy would be made to pay for not taking their chances — most notably a sitter that Moise Kean somehow missed in the ninth minute — when a superb free-kick from Michael Olise put France ahead 10 minutes into the second half.

But the Azzurri responded confidently and equalised as Alessandro Bastoni pounced on a mistake from Lucas Da Cunha to score his second goal in as many games.

Italy were grateful to a host of excellent saves from goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, but they too had chances to win the game and may feel somewhat frustrated not to have done so after France centre-back Dayot Upamecano was sent off in the 85th minute.

But Mancini was very satisfied with what he witnessed in Saint-Denis.

“We knew it would be a very difficult match, especially at the start, but we did well to allow them very little in terms of chances, even if they had more possession,” Mancini told Rai Sport.

“We played as a team, attacking and defending together, and so it is certainly a very positive evening for us.

“I wanted this to be another step forward in our journey. I liked that we tried to play football, despite being against an extraordinary France side full of champions.

“At times we suffered, but always tried to score goals whenever we had the chance, so that’s very good.”

Bastoni: Italy can do it against anyone

Bastoni, meanwhile, believes Italy’s display should give them confidence they can compete with anyone despite missing out on World Cup qualification for the third successive time earlier this year.

“It was a tough game, we knew it would be, it’s hardly news, but I am so happy with the team performance,” Bastoni said to Rai.

“We fought hard, we suffered, we even ruined some of France’s objectives for tonight, as they were prepared for a big celebration. We knew we weren’t coming here for a walk in the park, and that’s how it was.

“It’s certainly pleasing to score again, but the moment it was done, I thought we had to make sure we didn’t concede another, otherwise it was all points. This is a good result that boosts our confidence going forward,

“I didn’t expect to score two goals, but I never lost faith in myself. I won’t let one or two situations ruin the career of over 300 games. I thank my family for being by my side and I hope that keeping my head up high is seen as a positive.

“We believed in our chances of victory from the start, and indeed had the best chances in the first half to break the deadlock. It’s a strong signal, because if we can put in a performance like this against France in Paris, then we can do it against anyone.

“Now there is another game in this run and we are not taking anything for granted, it is another important test.”

Italy host Turkey in Bologna on Monday in their final game of this extended international break.

articles.summary: It was a night of mixed emotions for Zidane.
articles.content:
Zidane ‘touched’ by Stade de France ovation but disappointed after Les Bleus draw with Italy

It was a night of mixed emotions for Zidane.

Last Update:

Zinedine Zidane was touched by the reception he received for his first home game as France coach but felt his side deserved better than their 1-1 draw with Italy.

After securing wins of Turkey and Belgium in his first two games in charge, Zidane received a rapturous ovation from the Stade de France crowd for Friday’s UEFA Nations League clash with Roberto Mancini’s side.

Despite an unconvincing first-half showing, it looked as if France were on course for three wins from three 10 minutes into the second when Michael Olise’s stunning free-kick gave them the lead.

But Italy responded well and stunned the home crowd when they levelled as Alessandro Bastoni pounced on a mistake from Lucas Da Cunha and confidently finished beyond Mike Maignan.

Both sides had chances to win the game thereafter, though Italy may be more irritated at not doing so after France saw Dayot Upamecano sent off five minutes from the end of normal time for a second bookable offence.

Though his side remain unbeaten, Zidane conceded to disappointment and frustration being his overriding emotions after the game.

“I’m very disappointed; we deserved better, but that’s the way football is,” Zidane told TF1.

“We should have sealed the win, but I’m proud of my players. The performance was very good; my players were exemplary. I’m frustrated for my players because they gave it their all.

“We had possession in the first half, but it was fruitless—that’s what we tried to correct at halftime. To hurt the opponent, you have to exploit the open spaces. In terms of our performance, we executed our game plan; they played their game—defensive, ‘Italian-style.’ We weren’t really in much danger.

“When you’re playing well the whole game and doing the right things, a small hiccup can throw you off a bit, and that’s what happened to us.

“The most important thing is what I saw from all my players. I’m very satisfied. They can be proud of what they did tonight in terms of performance.”

Asked about his return to the Stade de France and the reception from the fans, Zidane added: “It touches me; we would have loved to give the victory to an entire nation. It didn’t happen tonight, so we’ll rest up to win our fourth match.”

articles.title: UEFA Nations League: De Bruyne at the double for Belgium as Lewandowski scores treble and Dzeko bows out
articles.summary: It was a superb night for a couple of European football's modern greats.
articles.content:
UEFA Nations League: De Bruyne at the double for Belgium as Lewandowski scores treble and Dzeko bows out

It was a superb night for a couple of European football's modern greats.

Last Update:

Kevin De Bruyne scored twice as Belgium cruised to a 3-0 victory over Turkey in the UEFA Nations League.

Beaten 1-0 by France last time out, the Red Devils bounced back in style, with Napoli star De Bruyne the standout in Liege.

De Bruyne opened the scoring in the 10th minute, collecting the loose ball and skipping beyond the challenge of a defender before rifling into the bottom-right corner.

He bettered that fine goal with his second, which came just before the hour mark as he met Youri Tielemans’ lay-off with a trademark curling strike into the top-left corner.

Romelu Lukaku put the game beyond doubt in the 76th minute when he turned home from Charles De Ketelaere’s pull back to make it two wins from three for new boss Mark van Bommel. Belgium are second in League A Group 1 behind France, who drew 1-1 with Italy.

Turkey, meanwhile, are without a point from their first three games, their poor form under Vincenzo Montella continuing after a dismal group-stage exit at the World Cup.

Lewandowski leads Poland rout of Romania, Dzeko says farewell

Robert Lewandowski inspired Poland to their first win of the League B campaign, scoring a hat-trick in a 6-0 rout of 10-man Romania.

Lewandowski opened the scoring from the penalty spot after Radu Draugsin was sent off for a shove on the striker as he attempted to latch onto a long ball into the area.

He turned home his second from point-blank range two minutes into the second half following good work down the left from Nicola Zalewski. An own goal then put the game beyond doubt and, after Piotr Zielinski and Jan Bednarek added further gloss to the scoreline, Lewandowski completed his seventh international treble late on when he hammered home at the near post.

In Zenica, Edin Dzeko bid farewell to international football as he made his final appearance for Bosnia-Herzegovina in their 1-1 draw with Sweden.

The residential building behind the stadium was illuminated with flares in the 11th minute of the clash as tribute to Dzeko, who had a goal disallowed in first-half stoppage time for a foul in the build-up, with Sweden’s Viktor Gyokeres having earlier seen an effort chalked off for handball following a VAR check.

Gyokeres did break the deadlock in the 61st minute before Dzeko left the field to a guard of honour.

Kerim Alajbegovic equalised 10 minutes from the end of normal time to salvage a point for Bosnia, who are two points behind leaders Sweden and a point ahead of Poland in Group 4 of the second tier.

Northern Ireland surged to the top of Group 2 with a stunning 3-0 win over Ukraine in Slovakia, while Milos Kerkez scored the only goal of the game as Hungary beat Georgia 1-0.

Espi could make his senior debut when Spain host the Czech Republic in Oviedo on Saturday, October 3.

articles.title: I think I’m getting better: Pickford issues warning to Trafford as battle for England No.1 shirt intensifies
articles.summary: Jordan Pickford has been England's number one for nine years and is not willing to give up the shirt without a fight
articles.content:
I think I’m getting better: Pickford issues warning to Trafford as battle for England No.1 shirt intensifies

Jordan Pickford has been England's number one for nine years and is not willing to give up the shirt without a fight

Last Update:

Jordan Pickford claims he is “getting better” and warned James Trafford he won’t give up the England number one shirt without a fight.

Pickford has been first choice for his country ever since making his international debut in 2017 but had to watch from the bench as Trafford was preferred for England’s Nations League games with Spain and Czechia over the last week.

The Everton goalkeeper’s presence at Friday’s news conference suggests he will start Saturday’s game against Croatia in Rijeka and Pickford rubbished suggestions it was time for Trafford to be given a run.

“I’m 32 now, you see keepers playing still at 40, still playing at the highest level. It’s about me focusing on myself; I set myself my own goals,” he said.

“I want to push boundaries and keep improving and keep going to be the best version of myself. I’ll never stop until I stop. I’m not slowing down, I think I’m only getting better.”

Pickford has not had much competition for a place between the sticks in recent years but Trafford has impressed when playing in England’s various youth categories and has made a promising start to his career at Leeds after moving to Elland Road from Manchester City over the summer.

“I feel for me personally it’s always good to have good competition, I’ve always said in interviews I’ve always wanted that competition,” added Pickford. “We have a good crop of goalkeepers coming through and it’s a credit to England to have that and may it continue for longer.

“I’ll always push myself to be the best version of me and keep getting those caps. You can’t let your foot off the gas at any time, you want to push yourself to be who you want to be.”

Pickford happy with how he’s coped being back-up

Despite performing an unaccustomed back-up role this week, former Sunderland stopper Pickford has been pleased with how he’s adapted.

“Yeah it is not often I do that [be back-up],” he said. “Club or country.

“The manager told me the reasons why. It was good for me to see where I’m at. It’s about me being a good team-mate with good energy around the place and train well and have that leadership role. I think I’ve done it really well over the last two games.

“It’s not normal for me, but first and foremost, the manager asks to be the best team-mate. I love playing but if I’m watching, I just want the best for England and that’s to win and I think I dealt with it really well.

“It was different, but we have also been together in a cycle now for two years. Traff’s started really well for Leeds. It’s been a good unit around us for the last two years. That’s what the manager said and you have to respect that decision.”

Pickford wants World Cup repeat when England take on Croatia

Saturday’s game is a repeat of England’s opening game of the 2026 World Cup finals which they won 4-2 in Dallas after a strong second-half display.

And Pickford is hoping for a similar front-footed approach as England look to build on Tuesday’s 2-0 victory in Prague.

He said: “Yeah I think it’s visible to see how aggressive we were in the second half against Croatia at the World Cup and we didn’t let our foot of the gas. I think it was a bit edgy…first group game of the World Cup. It was always going to be a bit cagey, we wanted the second half to be the first half because of the standards we set ourselves.”

articles.title: Tuchel admits Manchester City verdict has been a hot topic in the England camp ahead of Croatia clash
articles.summary: England's players have been following news of Manchester City's troubles this week ahead of the clash with Croatia, according to boss Thomas Tuchel
articles.content:
Tuchel admits Manchester City verdict has been a hot topic in the England camp ahead of Croatia clash

England's players have been following news of Manchester City's troubles this week ahead of the clash with Croatia, according to boss Thomas Tuchel

Last Update:

Manchester City’s guilty verdict has been a “big topic in the camp” according to England boss Thomas Tuchel ahead of Saturday’s Nations League game with Croatia.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday what had been reported last week; that an independent commission deemed the club had systematically broken financial rules with “sham” contracts designed to inflate revenue and reduce costs.

The scale of the deception, reported to have totalled more than £900million, was breathtaking and a number of sanctions now lie on the table. City have continued to deny any wronging and on Friday lodged an appeal after declaring the verdict “unsafe”.

The story has dominated the news agenda this week and Tuchel admitted it had also been discussed among the Three Lions players, including Manchester City duo Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi.

“We had some time off between the matches and it is a big subject,” said Tuchel. “Everyone speaks about it, so there is no other voice needed. I am glad to not be that voice. No-one needs my half knowledge on the topic.

“Of course, the players talk about it. City players talk about it. We talk with them but only briefly. They are ready to go tomorrow. But of course, it’s a big topic in the camp.”

Tuchel would consider picking City players for England if they are relegated

One possible sanction for City is relegation from the Premier League and Tuchel said he would consider picking players from outside the top flight if it came to that.

He added: “There is always a possibility. I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, occasion, the tournament. I will never rule out that because they don’t play in the top flight in their country. We need to look at it case by case.”

Saturday’s game will be played behind closed doors – bar the presence of local schoolchildren and a limited number of England fans – due to repeated misdemeanours from Croatian supporters.

And Tuchel was wary of his players switching off due to a lack of atmosphere inside the HNK Stadium in Rijeka.

“First of all, I am happy for the children who will be at the match tomorrow, that they have the chance to come and watch the game and players that close,” said the former PSG and Chelsea boss. “I am glad that our 100 or 200 fans have the chance to be here. It means a lot to us. The most loyal fans have the chance to watch the game.

“To be behind closed doors, it’s never nice. It’s a strange atmosphere. Everyone would love the atmosphere in the stadium – a proper football crowd which would be very, very different. This is a part we have to take into consideration. We cannot switch off and be in holiday mood. It might feel a bit like pre-season but it’s not. It’s a crucial match in the Nations League.”

England boss Tuchel wary of dangerous Croatia

England bounced back from defeat to Spain last Saturday with a routine 2-0 victory against a Czechia side that played for three-quarters of the game with 10 men on Tuesday.

Croatia also beat Czechia before suffering a 4-1 defeat to world champions Spain.

“We expect a difficult match tomorrow against a big football nation and a proud country – a side full of quality,” said Tuchel. “A mix of young and experienced players with a young coach. Everyone will be ready to give their all for the new coach.

“It feels like a cup game – a cup semi-final maybe. I am a huge fan of Croatia’s players. They have a lot of quality technically and big competitors. It’s a promising game.”

Tuchel conceded he was not sure what system coach Slaven Bilic would employ.

“We don’t know what’s coming,” he said. “The coach before was very fluid and switching between back four and back five. With Bilic for two matches, he has gone with a back four. But we never know. It might be a surprise.

“It makes it a little difficult because we don’t have evidence with Bilic as Croatia coach. But sometimes it makes it easier because you don’t prepare for every scenario you see. You just have two matches.

“Hopefully we can implement our style. Croatia can hurt any team and it’s important to break the rhythm and it’s basically the task for tomorrow.”

articles.title: Manchester City confirm appeal against commission ruling as FA hints at separate action
articles.summary: Manchester City could face separate action from the Football Association after being found guilty of breaching over 100 financial regulations
articles.content:
Manchester City confirm appeal against commission ruling as FA hints at separate action

Manchester City could face separate action from the Football Association after being found guilty of breaching over 100 financial regulations

Last Update:

Manchester City have confirmed they will appeal against an independent commission ruling that found them guilty of 114 charges of financial malpractice.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday what had been reported last week; that the commission deemed the club had systematically broken the rules with “sham” contracts designed to inflate revenue and reduce costs.

The scale of the deception, reported to have totalled more than £900million, was breathtaking and a number of sanctions now lie on the table. City have continued to deny any wronging and on Friday lodged an appeal after declaring the verdict “unsafe”.

A club statement read:”Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

“The club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

“The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

“We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”

FA monitor City case closely

The Football Association could hit City with separate charges after admitting the ruling of the independent commission has “significant implications for the integrity of the game”.

An FA statement read: “The Independent Commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.

“As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely.”

It is common practice for the FA to apply separate punishments to clubs once a Premier League investigation is completed.

articles.title: Hojlund shoves Portugal boss Jesus and explains Ronaldo celebration
articles.summary: Rasmus Hojlund made his feeling clear on Cristiano Ronaldo both during and after Denmark's defeat to Portugal on Thursday night
articles.content:
Hojlund shoves Portugal boss Jesus and explains Ronaldo celebration

Rasmus Hojlund made his feeling clear on Cristiano Ronaldo both during and after Denmark's defeat to Portugal on Thursday night

Last Update:

Rasmus Hojlund insists he was not disrespecting Cristiano Ronaldo by copying his ‘Siu’ goal celebration when scoring for Denmark against Portugal on Thursday night.

With Ronaldo absent after a fall-out with Portugal boss Jorge Jesús, all eyes were on whether Jesus’ side could cope without their record-goalscorer but, rather than struggle, they flourished, winning 4-2 in Copenhagen.

Hojlund made it 2-2 on the night with a lovely chipped finish before running away and performing Ronaldo’s trademark jump and turn celebration.

Vitinha and Joao Felix netted in the final 25 minutes to hand Portugal the win after which there was a slightly bizarre exchange between Hojlund and Jesus. As they shook hands and patted it each other on the chest, the Napoli striker appeared to push the 72-year-old away before turning to give him an angry look.

Hojlund praises Ronaldo: he is my idol

Asked about the celebration afterwards, Hojlund revealed Ronaldo was a huge inspiration to him.

He said: “I just wanted to send a strong message to the Portuguese national team, that if they don’t value Cristiano, there are many people around the world whom he has inspired and who still admire him.

“It was a tribute to a man who may be finished with his national team career – after what has happened.I just wanted to pay tribute to him once again. It has nothing to do with lack of respect. He’s my big idol.”

Jesus’ approach pays off as Portugal sparkle

Portugal’s performance was vindication for Jesus’ hardline approach with the veteran striker, who walked out on the camp on Wednesday night.

The squad looked liberated and performed with an attacking verve not often seen in recent months.

Asked if the players are behind him, Jesus told Sport TV: “There’s no reason for them not to be behind me. What matters is what we have to do. I know why you asked that question, but things happen—they don’t divide the team, and they won’t divide us.”

Portugal fly home on Friday ahead of Sunday’s home game with Norway in Porto.

It seems unlikely the situation with Ronaldo will change before then but Jesus said it would be discussed after that game.

He added: “After the Dragão match, we’ll see what happens.

“It’s difficult to wait until then, but the most important thing now is to think about the next match and what we can deliver in it.”

articles.title: Ronaldo saga ‘will not divide us’, Jesus vows after Portugal win over Denmark
articles.summary: Jesus' men put the episode to one side to claim a brilliant win.
articles.content:
Ronaldo saga ‘will not divide us’, Jesus vows after Portugal win over Denmark

Jesus' men put the episode to one side to claim a brilliant win.

Last Update:

Jorge Jesus vowed that the saga surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo “will not divide” his Portugal side after they claimed a superb 4-2 win over Denmark in Copenhagen without their record goalscorer.

Ronaldo sensationally left the squad this week after a dispute with Jesus, seemingly bringing an end to his storied international career.

The apparent breakdown in the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo overshadowed the build-up to Thursday’s UEFA Nations League game in Copenhagen, but it had no influence on an excellent attacking display from Portugal.

After beating Norway 2-1 with a disgruntled Ronaldo left on the bench, Portugal went ahead in the 13th minute through Joao Cancelo.

Mikkel Damsgaard equalised with a sublime curling strike 10 minutes later, only for Goncalo Ramos to give Portugal the lead again soon after.

Rasmus Hojlund drew Denmark level for the second time eight minutes into the second half, but Vitinha’s first goal for Portugal restored their advantage once more, before Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr team-mate Joao Felix added a fourth late on to secure a third win from three games for the defending Nations League champions.

Portugal will next face Norway in Porto on Sunday in their final fixture of an extended international break, and Jesus made it clear the squad will remain united despite the fallout from the Ronaldo episode.

Asked if the players are behind him, Jesus told Sport TV: “There’s no reason for them not to be behind me.

“What matters is what we have to do. I know why you asked that question, but things happen—they don’t divide the team, and they won’t divide us.”

Vitinha hails Jesus after Portugal’s latest win

Speaking to RTP, Vitinha backed up his coach’s comments, praising Jesus for his influence on their excellent start to the Nations League.

“Because of the coach’s work,” Vitinha said when asked for reasons for the improvements made in Jesus’ first three games in charge.

“The truth is, we played an excellent game—there’s no denying it. It’s very hard to win here. We learned that lesson last year or two years ago. We lost, and it was really tough. Don’t be fooled by the result. Beyond the result, it was the performance. It was our best so far.

“We’ve been improving over these last three games. The more time we spend with the coach, the more we absorb his ideas and develop more dynamic play. Defensively, we’ve always been strong and capable. We’ve taken a step forward on offense. I hope we continue this way. It was a very hard-fought victory. It’s important to say that—it’s tough to play here. Beyond the win, it was an excellent performance.

“The coach’s work is starting to pay off. You can see it—it was crystal clear today. Fortunately, things are going well, and that’s how we want to keep it up. Now, we just need to tell everyone to pack the Dragao so we can make it four wins in a row, which would be perfect.”

On the situation with Ronaldo, Vitinha added: “We tried to stay out of it. We focused on the game and succeeded. We responded incredibly well. Congratulations to the whole team for that.”

Parrott stars on the international stage again

The Netherlands fought back from 2-0 down to rescue a draw with Greece in the Nations League as former Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders struck in the 89th minute.

Goals from Fotis Ioannidis and substitute Giorgos Masouras put Greece into an early position of control.

Elsewhere, the match ​between the Republic of Ireland and Austria was disrupted when tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium by those protesting against the Irish team ⁠fulfilling their fixtures against Israel.

Ireland were 1-0 up in front of a sell-out crowd when the referee suspended the match briefly in the 20th minute as tennis balls featuring the ⁠Palestinian flag were thrown onto ​the ⁠pitch.

Troy Parrott put Ireland ahead in ​the 12th minute, dancing through the Austrian defence ‌and into the area ⁠before striking low into the far corner.

And the former Tottenham man doubled the lead from the penalty spot before late goals from Alex Prass and Michael Gregoritsch drew Austria level.

Wales returned to winning ways with a fine win at home to Norway.

Fulham forward Oscar Bobb put the visitors ahead in Cardiff only for Dan James to fire in a fine cross on the run from Sorba Thomas.

And after Norway were reduced to 10 men at the start of the second half Neco Williams powered in a free-kick to seal the win.

articles.title: Ramos stars as Portugal put Ronaldo drama behind them against Denmark

articles.content:
Ramos stars as Portugal put Ronaldo drama behind them against Denmark

Ramos put Portugal on course to maintain their perfect Nations League record.

Last Update:

Goncalo Ramos helped Portugal put the saga surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo behind them with an assist and a goal in the first half of their UEFA Nations League clash with Denmark.

Ronaldo sensationally left the squad this week after a fall out with coach Jorge Jesus, seemingly bringing an end to his storied international career.

The drama around Portugal’s record goalscorer understandably overshadowed the build-up to the game with Denmark at Parken, but it had little impact on the performance of Jesus’ men in the early stages.

Ramos, who started ahead of Ronaldo against Norway and was picked to lead the line again in Copenhagen, went close to breaking the deadlock as his snap shot hit the post.

But just moments later he teed up the opener, his return ball to Joao Cancelo collected by the Barcelona full-back, who then produced a finish that belied his position as a defender by delicately lofting over Mads Hermansen to give Portugal a 13th-minute lead.

Rafael Leao was subsequently denied by Hermansen before seeing an effort from point-blank range deflected wide.

And Denmark made the most of his profligacy, with Mikkel Damsgaard bending into the far corner to restore parity, though it did not last long.

Indeed, a stunning one-two with Bruno Fernandes sent Ramos through on goal, and the AC Milan striker made no mistake with a composed low finish, illustrating why Portugal may be better off without their 41-year-old talisman.

Only a reflex save by Hermansen with his legs prevented Ramos from making it 3-1 shortly before half-time following good work from Leao.

Portugal are aiming to make it three wins from three to start the defence of the Nations League title they won for a second time in 2025. In Ronaldo’s absence, they put themselves on course to maintain their perfect record.

articles.content:
Messi buys Spanish side Eldense

Messi now has stakes in two Spanish sides

Last Update:

Argentina legend Lionel Messi has finalised an agreement to take over Spanish second-tier outfit CD Eldense, subject to regulatory clearance, the club confirmed on Thursday.

The 39-year-old Inter Miami forward has secured a majority stake in his second Spanish club of the year, having already acquired UE Cornellà back in April.

The former Barcelona and Argentina captain struck a deal last month to purchase the entire shareholding previously held by Eldense’s majority owners, a Colombian investment group.

“Club Deportivo Eldense officially announces the acquisition of the club by Leo Messi, marking the start of a new and exciting chapter in the club’s history, which spans more than a hundred years,” read a statement published on the club’s official website.

Founded in 1921, Eldense will be eager for an immediate boost from their high-profile new owner. The club currently sit 19th in the Segunda División table and remain locked in an early-season relegation scrap, having suffered four defeats in their opening seven fixtures.

articles.title: Downing Street responds to Andy Burnham backlash over Manchester City comments
articles.summary: Downing Street has hit back at criticism of Andy Burnham after his comments on Manchester City.
articles.content:
Downing Street responds to Andy Burnham backlash over Manchester City comments

Downing Street has hit back at criticism of Andy Burnham after his comments on Manchester City.

Last Update:

Downing Street has insisted Manchester City are not “above the rules” after Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced criticism over his response to the club’s Premier League financial case.

Burnham said on Wednesday that he would be “really concerned” if City’s owners decided to sell the club following the independent commission’s guilty verdict.

His comments drew criticism from the Conservatives and surprised some within football, prompting No. 10 to clarify the Prime Minister’s position on Thursday.

“As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules,” a Downing Street spokesperson said.

“He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

“Wherever wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.”

City deny wrongdoing and have until Friday to submit an appeal against the commission’s findings.

The Premier League said this week that City “systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade”, with the independent commission finding that the club arranged “sham contracts” with commercial partners as part of a scheme involving more than £830m in disguised funding.

Burnham would be ‘really concerned’ if City owners left

Burnham, who served as mayor of Greater Manchester until June, discussed the verdict during an interview with the BBC on Wednesday.

He stressed that he did not want to interfere with the Premier League’s disciplinary process and highlighted that City continue to contest the findings.

Burnham said it would be “wrong” to “jump to a conclusion” while the process remains ongoing.

However, when asked about the possibility of City’s owners selling the club as a consequence of the case, Burnham highlighted their contribution to Manchester since taking control in 2008.

“I would be really concerned to lose them,” Burnham said.

“They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.

“I can’t intervene more in the process, it would be wrong for me to do that.”

City have been owned by Sheikh Mansour since 2008. Mansour is a member of Abu Dhabi’s ruling family and serves as deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

articles.title: Manchester City to use Abu Dhabi government argument in appeal against financial verdict
articles.summary: Manchester City have their argument ready to try and save their Premier League status.
articles.content:
Manchester City to use Abu Dhabi government argument in appeal against financial verdict

Manchester City have their argument ready to try and save their Premier League status.

Last Update:

Manchester City are reportedly preparing to argue that money directed towards key sponsorship agreements came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club’s owners as they challenge the verdict in their Premier League financial case.

An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the league’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

City have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the decision.

A central part of the case concerned sponsorship revenue and the commission’s finding that City artificially inflated commercial income through “sham” agreements.

Abu Dhabi United Group, the private investment company belonging to City owner Sheikh Mansour, was found to have topped up commercial agreements as part of what the commission described as a “disguised funding scheme”.

The total involved was said to be £830.69m, with the commission finding that the arrangements allowed City to present higher commercial revenue while attempting to comply with Premier League and UEFA financial regulations.

However, City are expected to challenge that conclusion when their case reaches an appeal board.

Reports claim the club will present evidence which it says shows that money directed to sponsors originated from the Abu Dhabi government rather than ADUG.

Premier League rules allow state-owned organisations to enter sponsorship agreements with clubs.

Commission rejected City’s explanation

The independent commission rejected City’s explanation and concluded that the claim regarding the source of the funding was “untrue”.

In its findings, the commission said: “We concluded that it was an ‘explanation’ that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme.”

City have strongly disputed the commission’s conclusions and signalled their intention to challenge the decision.

Following the verdict, the club said the opinion contained “clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has also referred to what he described as “irrefutable evidence” supporting the club’s position.

Sheikh Mansour is a member of Abu Dhabi’s ruling family and the brother of UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.

Etihad considers legal action

Etihad Airways, City’s principal sponsor, has said it is considering legal action against the Premier League following publication of the commission’s findings.

The UAE’s state-owned national airline said the release had “damaging implications…despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings”.

Etihad added that “it categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements”.

The airline is owned by sovereign wealth fund L’Imad, which is chaired by the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi.

articles.content:
Tottenham chief backs Roberto De Zerbi despite winless Premier League start

Roberto De Zerbi still has the backing of the Tottenham hierarchy.

Last Update:

Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham has backed Roberto De Zerbi despite the club sitting bottom of the Premier League after five matches.

Spurs are still searching for their first league win of the campaign following a summer in which more than £380 million was committed to new signings.

The results have increased pressure on De Zerbi after successive 17th-placed finishes, but Venkatesham believes there have been encouraging signs beyond the points total.

“The club had made significant changes over the summer, both on and off the pitch, and recognised that these might take time to take full effect,” Venkatesham said.

He also “expressed confidence in Roberto De Zerbi, in the players brought in and in the changes made, noting the considerable work under way behind the scenes.”

Venkatesham explains Tottenham’s financial constraints

Venkatesham also outlined the financial situation facing Spurs despite their huge summer expenditure.

The Lewis family, Tottenham’s majority owners, injected another £120m of capital into the club last month, but Venkatesham said financial regulations continue to influence their transfer strategy.

“The club needed to improve as a seller of players, having achieved limited returns in previous years and doing so is important in modern football for compliance with financial regulations,” Venkatesham said.

“Financial regulations represented a genuine constraint. The club had not recorded a profit since 2019 and its costs were rising through investment in the men’s team in wages and transfer fees.

“Successive 17th-placed finishes and the absence of European revenue this season had also affected the club’s revenue position.”

articles.title: Negreira case: UEFA looking into Barcelona documents
articles.summary: Real Madrid believe payments made by Barca helped them on the pitch
articles.content:
Negreira case: UEFA looking into Barcelona documents

Real Madrid believe payments made by Barca helped them on the pitch

Last Update:

UEFA have confirmed receipt of a “large quantity of documents” submitted by Real Madrid in relation to the ongoing investigation into Barcelona over the so-called Negreira case.

European football’s governing body has acknowledged that its ethics and disciplinary inspectors have obtained the dossier to review as part of their broader monitoring of the Catalan club, which follows months of pressure from the Real hierarchy.

Barcelona have now responded, saying they are complying with the proceedings.

What is the Negreira case?

The Negreira case is an ongoing investigation centred around payments of €7million made by Barca to companies linked to José María Enríquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Spanish referees’ committee (CTA), between 2001 and 2018.

Madrid believe they led to on-field decisions in favour of Barcelona.

Barca insist there was no wrongdoing and claim the payments were made to Negreira to act as a consultant on the technical aspects of refereeing.

Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez previously confirmed the preparation of an extensive 500-page dossierafter calling the controversy “the biggest case of corruption in history,” with Madrid subsequently submitting a formal request demanding the resumption of disciplinary proceedings against their rivals on the grounds that the allegations pose an “extremely serious danger to the integrity of competitions.”

The latest development comes amid improved institutional relations between Madrid, UEFA, and the European Club Association, with the Spanish giants keen to ensure the issue is rigorously assessed internationally amid frustration over a perceived lack of traction domestically.

While UEFA reiterated that receipt of the dossier does not constitute the opening of formal disciplinary proceedings or immediate sanctions, it ensures Madrid’s evidence is now under formal examination by UEFA inspectors under the Article 31(4) inquiry originally opened in March 2023.

At the centre of the dispute are historic payments exceeding €7.5m made between 2001 and 2018 to companies linked to former refereeing official José María Enríquez Negreira, an affair that has previously raised questions over potential competitive bans.

Barcelona continue to strongly refute any wrongdoing while maintaining the fees were strictly for legitimate external technical reports and advisory work on refereeing tendencies.

What have Barcelona said?

In a fresh statement on Thursday, the club said:

“UEFA has not opened any new proceedings against FC Barcelona. The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate. The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

“The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are “ongoing.” It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

“It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid’s complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

“In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so.”

articles.content:
Who will wear the number seven shirt for Portugal against Denmark following Ronaldo’s escape act?

Portugal's number seven shirt will not be worn by Cristiano Ronaldo against Denmark on Thursday. But who gets to put on one of the most famous shirts in football?

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo’s exit from the Portugal camp has left vacant one of the most iconic shirts in football but who will wear the famous number seven against Denmark on Thursday night?

Ronaldo’s decision to leave the team following his row with coach Jorge Jesús means the numbers for the game at Parken have had to be moved around.

Ronaldo has always worn the number seven and it has become part of his brand CR7.

Leão to benefit from Ronaldo absence

It may be a one-off – or part of a longer-term approach should Ronaldo’s Portugal career be over – but the shirt has gone to Galatasaray winger Rafael Leão against the Danes.

Leão wore the number 17 jersey for the Nations League games with Wales and Norway but will don the number seven tonight. Fabio Silva will wear number 17.

It will be discombobulating to see another player wear the number seven of Portugal with it belonging to Ronaldo for almost all of his 234 international appearances.

He also wore that number at Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and it’s his at current club Al-Nassr.

Ronaldo flew into Madrid last night after summoning his private jet to collect him from Copenhagen. His exact whereabouts are unknown but he will make his way back to Saudi Arabia before next Friday’s Pro League clash with Al-Diriyah in Riyadh. He faces a busy schedule for Al-Nassr with nine games in 28 days.

Ronaldo has left a trail of destruction behind him in Denmark with even Portuguese prime minister Luís Montenegro speaking to both him and Jesus in an attempt to smooth relations.
