Ivan Toney pleads not guilty to alleged nightclub assault in London

Ivan Toney has denied charges of assault made against him in court.

Last Update:

England striker Ivan Toney has pleaded not guilty to assaulting a man at a nightclub in central London.

The 30-year-old appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, where he denied a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

Toney is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during an incident at a nightclub in Soho on December 6.

The case was due to be heard in the magistrates’ court, but Toney elected to have the matter dealt with at Crown Court in front of a judge and jury.

The forward was released on unconditional bail and is due to appear at Southwark Crown Court on October 29.

Toney’s England career

Toney has won 10 caps for England and was part of the squad that reached the Euro 2024 final.

The striker began his professional career with Northampton before spells with Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United.

He joined Brentford in 2020 and established himself as one of the Premier League’s leading forwards during his time in West London.

Toney later moved to Saudi Arabia and currently plays for Al-Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

articles.title: Portuguese public turn against Cristiano Ronaldo and back Jorge Jesus after row that could end striker’s international career
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has lost the support of the Portuguese public after walking out on the national team following a row with boss Jorge Jesus
articles.content:
Portuguese public turn against Cristiano Ronaldo and back Jorge Jesus after row that could end striker’s international career

Cristiano Ronaldo has lost the support of the Portuguese public after walking out on the national team following a row with boss Jorge Jesus

Last Update:

The Portuguese public appear to have turned against Cristiano Ronaldo with an overwhelming majority backing Jorge Jesus in the row that has engulfed the national team.

The severity of the matter was demonstrated by reports Prime Minister Luís Montenegro has spoken to the two warring factions in a bid to resolve the differences that led to Ronaldo walking out on the Portugal squad on the eve of Thursday’s Nations League game against Denmark.

The dispute started at the weekend when Jesus promised to bring Ronaldo off the bench towards the end of the game with Norway only to change his mind due to the match situation.

That angered the 41-year-old, who then skipped training on Monday and Tuesday. Showdown talks were held on Tuesday night with Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca also involved. Ronaldo’s ally, Spanish journalist Edu Aguirre, claims Jesus apologised to Ronaldo personally and said he would make a public apology at Wednesday’s press conference.

However, after being grilled about the situation by the media, Jesus then said Ronaldo would again be on the bench against Denmark and that he would be treated the same way as any other player.

Aguirre claims Ronaldo saw this as a betrayal and immediately summoned his private jet to Copenhagen to pick him up.

The issue has dominated the news cycle in Portugal and it seems Jesus’ handling of Ronaldo and his ego has won the fans over. Despite the fact Ronaldo has won the most caps for the country (234) and scored the most goals (146) – both global records as well – and played a key role in their first major tournament win at Euro 2016, it seems he has lost the affection of the public.

A Bola vote favours Jesus, not Ronaldo

Leading sports newspaper A Bola carried out a poll of its readers with the bulk blaming Ronaldo for the fall-out.

Under the question, who is at fault, the readership voted:

Cristiano Ronaldo – 77.4%

Jorge Jesus – 14.5%

Pedro Proenca – 8.1%

The matter will more than likely bring an end to Ronaldo’s international career unless some middle ground is found.

But his age means it would need to be swift, otherwise Ronaldo’s glittering spell on the global stage will grind to an underwhelming finish.

articles.title: Gary Neville calls for Manchester City owners to be removed after dragging Premier League ‘through the mud’
articles.summary: Gary Neville has had his say on Manchester City's current situation after being found guilty of 114 financial breaches.
articles.content:
Gary Neville calls for Manchester City owners to be removed after dragging Premier League ‘through the mud’

Gary Neville has had his say on Manchester City's current situation after being found guilty of 114 financial breaches.

Last Update:

Gary Neville has called for Manchester City’s current owners to be removed from the Premier League following the club’s guilty verdict in their long-running financial case.

An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them, with the Premier League confirming the findings earlier this week.

The sanctions have yet to be decided, with a points deduction, fines, a transfer ban, stripping of titles and even expulsion from the Premier League among the potential outcomes that have been discussed.

Neville believes none of those punishments would go far enough and instead argued that removing the club’s current ownership would represent the strongest available consequence.

Speaking on the latest episode of Stick to Football, the former Manchester United captain said: “Manchester City will recover as a football club because Manchester City have been there longer than these owners, they’ll be there long after them, and it’s got an immense history.

“Points deductions, fines, transfer bans, removing the titles – not giving them to others, just removing the titles – it’s significant punishments. The only punishment that would be fair would be have huge consequences – the biggest consequence – would be removing the owners.

“That is the only consequence if I was Manchester City that I would be worried about. And as a fan of Manchester City, if you wanted to keep the investment that you’ve currently got, that would be the one I’d be most concerned about.”

Neville compares City case with Italian football crisis

The former United defender said he was concerned about the potential impact of the case on the reputation of the Premier League, particularly given how the competition is viewed around the world.

He referenced the damage caused by scandals in Italian football over the past quarter of a century, including the fallout from Calciopoli, which resulted in Juventus being relegated from Serie A in 2006.

“However, if you’re in football and you’re thinking about consequence, what can be more serious than industrial-level financial doping that we’ve seen and they’ve been found guilty of? I’m not celebrating.

“I’m chilled. This is chilling. I support Manchester United, Jamie Carragher supports Liverpool, Roy Keane and Ian Wright played for Manchester United, Arsenal, Jill Scott played for City.

“This is chilling to listen to this. It’s chilling. The Italian game has suffered immeasurably over the last 25 years, maybe from after Calciopoli. You know, we’ve played Juventus, we’ve alluded to this before, we felt at the time that this wasn’t right.

“And I’m not saying that’s going to happen to the Premier League. But we always think we’ve got this enormous integrity, the Premier League, that we are the league that sets the standard and it’s other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match fixing, referee scandals.

“This has now come into our country, this has now come into our league. This is the greatest export that we have in our country in the world. If you go around the world and talk about Liverpool, Manchester, Arsenal – people talk about the Premier League more than anything when you tell them where you’re from in the world. And at the moment, we’re being dragged through the mud.”

articles.title: Betrayal, betrayal, betrayal: Ronaldo ally reveals why striker quit Portugal camp
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal camp last night following a row with boss Jorge Jesus. His friend, Edu Aguirre, reveals what happened...
articles.content:
Betrayal, betrayal, betrayal: Ronaldo ally reveals why striker quit Portugal camp

Cristiano Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal camp last night following a row with boss Jorge Jesus. His friend, Edu Aguirre, reveals what happened...

Last Update:

A close friend of Cristiano Ronaldo has claimed the striker left the Portugal camp having felt betrayed by coach Jorge Jesus.

Edu Aguirre, a Spanish journalist known to be close to the 41-year-old, made the claims on El Chiringuito last night – not long after Ronaldo confirmed he was leaving the team hotel ahead of the Nations League game with Denmark in Copenhagen.

According to Aguirre, the situation had been brewing ever since Ronaldo had been named among the substitutes for Sunday’s game in Norway. Jesus had promised to give him some minutes towards the end but then changed his mind due to the closeness of the match his side eventually won 2-1.

Ronaldo failed to train on Monday and Tuesday, prompting showdown talks with Jesus and Portugal Football Association (FPF) president Pedro Proença.

Aguirre said: “There was a meeting on Tuesday night, between the president of the Federation, Jorge Jesus and Cristiano. Jorge Jesus apologised for making Cristiano warm up for 30 minutes without coming on.

“And not only did he [Jesus] apologise in private, but he says he will also do it publicly. This was Jorge Jesus’ promise to Cristiano Ronaldo.”

Ronaldo exploded, claims Aguirre

Inevitably, Wednesday’s press conference ahead of the Denmark game was full of questions relating to Ronaldo and Jesus struck a very different tone.

“Jorge Jesus goes to the press conference and talks lies. That’s why Cristiano exploded. Because he felt betrayed,” claimed Aguirre.

“Jorge Jesus in private says that he was wrong and that he will apologise at the press conference. And then he talks to the press and says that he is in charge and that Cristiano is just another player. The situation surprised many people. Betrayal, betrayal, betrayal.”

Jesus certainly struck an aggressive tone when addressing the media, insisting there were no special conditions for Ronaldo. He also said Goncalo Ramos, who replaced the former Real Madrid and Manchester United star against Norway – and scored the winner, would get the nod against Denmark.

“If I need [Ronaldo], he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t,” he said.

Ronaldo and Jesus worked together at Al-Nassr

The situation is a surprise given Ronaldo and Jesus worked in complete harmony last season as Al-Nassr won the Saudi Pro League.

But the question now remains: has Ronaldo played his final game for Portugal?

Before he departed Copenhagen on his private jet, he wrote on Instagram: “After the press conference of the national team, and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have made the decision to leave the national team training camp.

“In due course, I will tell all the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led me to leave the national team, to which I always dedicated myself.

“Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my team-mates good luck, without exception.”

The FPF also released a statement, insisting the focus was now on the Nations League clash with Denmark and the return against Norway.

It read: ”Preparation for the two matches against Denmark and Norway continue as planned with the 24 remaining squad members.

“The entire delegation remains totally focussed on the national team’s next fixtures and on achieving the established objectives.”

articles.summary: The first game of the post-Lionel Messi era ended in a convincing win for Argentina
articles.content:
No Messi, no problem as Argentina crush sorry Bolivia

The first game of the post-Lionel Messi era ended in a convincing win for Argentina

Last Update:

Argentina proved there could be life after Lionel Messi with a 4-0 rout of Bolivia last night.

Messi will play his farewell game next week against Benin after opting to retire from international football following this summer’s World Cup.

Boss Lionel Scaloni named a side that contained youth and experience for the game in Cordoba and his team shone, goals from Lautaro Martínez, Nico Paz, Cristian Romero and José López seeing them past a weak Bolivia side.

“It was wonderful to see so many young players enjoying themselves and singing the national anthem like any other player,” Scaloni said. “For any coach, it’s exciting to give a player their debut. For a national team coach, even more so, because you can see on the players’ faces what it means to play in this shirt.”

Scaloni also reserved praise for some of the older players, led by new skipper Romero.

“I like how the players approach the match, especially those who have been here for a while. They all come with a sense of joy, and they show it when they step onto the field.”

Paz the star as Argentina cruise

Paz occupied Messi’s role as chief playmaker and produced a hugely impressive display, the Como midfielder capping his performance with a lovely chipped finish to add to Martinez’s opener.

Romero’s header made it 3-0 before debutant Lopez notched his first goal for his country late on.

Lopez said: “I try to make the most of every opportunity the coach gives me. It’s an honour to play with the National Team. Very happy, luckily the goal came, the first one and it’s a gift from life.”

Argentina face Burkina Faso on Saturday night before the Benin clash on Tuesday on what is sure to be an emotional night in Buenos Aires.

The likes of Rodrigo De Paul and Gonzalo Montiel will return for the Benin game but Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina and Enzo Fernandez will miss out due to suspensions incurred during Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain.

articles.title: Man City whistleblower: Infantino helped club avoid sanctions and should have ‘no place in football’
articles.summary: The whistleblower who exposed Manchester City’s serious financial breaches says FIFA president Gianni Infantino helped the club and Paris Saint-Germain avoid financial fair play punishments. Man City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, though they still remain steadfast in their denial of any wrongdoing. The investiation into […]
articles.content:
Man City whistleblower: Infantino helped club avoid sanctions and should have ‘no place in football’

Last Update:

The whistleblower who exposed Manchester City’s serious financial breaches says FIFA president Gianni Infantino helped the club and Paris Saint-Germain avoid financial fair play punishments.

Man City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-year period, though they still remain steadfast in their denial of any wrongdoing.

The investiation into City was launched following information released into the public domain via the Football Leaks website, which was created by Rui Pinto.

Pinto has now said that Infantino intervened to help City and Paris St-Germain avoid financial fair play sanctions from European football’s governing body Uefa.

“Back in 2014, there was a man who was already aware of the irregularities involving Manchester City,” 37-year-old Portuguese Pinto wrote on Wednesday.

“The infamous Gianni Infantino, then Uefa general secretary, abused his authority, shared confidential documents and, in short, outmanoeuvred the investigatory chamber, doing everything in his power to ensure that both Manchester City and PSG would merely receive a fine, avoiding a deeper investigation that could have led to a Champions League ban.

“All of these details were also revealed through Football Leaks.

“Given his actions as Uefa general secretary and, more recently, as Fifa president, I can only say, in my humble opinion, that Gianni Infantino has become a cancer on football and should have no place in the future of the game.”

When the allegations first emerged, Uefa insisted that assisting with such matters fell within the general secretary’s remit, explaining that this could involve discussions, meetings, offering assistance to find solutions and other interactions to support the investigating body.

Infantino likewise defended his involvement, arguing that his role naturally involves “discussions” and “conversations”, as well as the exchange of documents, drafts and ideas across a wide range of issues.

He added that if those interactions were being portrayed negatively, there was little more he could do beyond carrying out his job “in an honest way” and “in a professional way”, while seeking to protect the interests of football.

More pressure on Infantino

The allegations pile more pressure on FIFA president Infantino, who came under fire after his now-shelved plans to sell stakes of the World Cup to private investors.

The Swiss administrator lost a swell of support for his position as a result, with UEFA calling for him to step down, but he has indicated his plans to stand for re-election in March 2027.

European football’s governing body Uefa accused Infantino of “criminal mismanagement” over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, while the Swiss Football Association (SFV) is the latest association to withdraw its support for the Fifa president.

“The decision follows a comprehensive reassessment of developments over the past few months,” an SFV statement read.

“From the SFV’s perspective, various incidents raise fundamental questions regarding leadership, governance, transparency and decision-making processes within Fifa.”

articles.title: Tuchel opens door for Bellingham to play ‘as a nine’ for England but says it will be ‘impossible’ to replace Kane
articles.summary: Bellingham scored seven goals for England at the 2026 World Cup
articles.content:
Tuchel opens door for Bellingham to play ‘as a nine’ for England but says it will be ‘impossible’ to replace Kane

Bellingham scored seven goals for England at the 2026 World Cup

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel has indicated he is willing to play Jude Bellingham as a central striker for England after a cameo up front in the 2-0 win over Czechia.

Bellingham came on for Harry Kane in Prague, taking up a more advanced position than his usual one in midfield, offering the potential for an alternative to their captain and record goalscorer in the future.

The Real Madrid star scored seven goals for the Three Lions at the 2026 World Cup and is regularly a goal threat for his club, with Tuchel incidating he has the attributes to be a success as a striker.

“I like him as a nine,” Tuchel said of Bellingham. “Then he can contribute to both sides and overload the sides and doesn’t affect so much of the balance.

“We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides. We are working on that.

“He is a natural goalscorer and he has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to be there and have the decisive action, so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a nine or a 10.”

‘You will not get another Harry Kane’

Kane is, of course, still the main man up front for England, with the Bayern Munich star scoring a record-extending 87th international goal against Czechia, with the striker the favourite for the Ballon d’Or after a sensational 12 months.

The 33-year-old will not go on forever, though, and there are concerns over Kane’s long-term successor up front.

Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have both filled that role at the last two major tournaments, but the Saudi Arabia-based duo are now into their thirties and were overlooked for the latest Nations League squad.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin remains among the options, although he too is approaching 30, leaving Liam Delap as the only England centre-forward under the age of 27 to have scored in the Champions League.

“You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all,” Tuchel said.

“He is the first one to push everyone and that is his mindset and he became a very, very hardworking forward on top of his finishing skills. He is a complete package.

“We look for different options and solutions. We finished the game with Jude [Bellingham] up front as a number nine.

“There will be someone else, but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.”

articles.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp: How CR7’s international crisis unfolded
articles.summary: Ronaldo has reportedly fallen out with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus
articles.content:
Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp: How CR7’s international crisis unfolded

Ronaldo has reportedly fallen out with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has sensationally left the Portugal camp after reports of a rift with manager Jorge Jesus.

Ronaldo’s international future is now in serious doubt, with the 41-year-old indicating in a statement that he will reveal more about the circumstances around his departure in due course.

But just how did the situation get to a point where Portugal’s captain, most legendary player, record goalscorer and record appearance maker has left in such controversial circumstances?

Here is the timeline of how CR7’s Portugal fallout unfolded.

Ronaldo and Portugal: How the crisis unfolded

Ronaldo’s Portugal future appeared settled just one week ago.

The 41-year-old had publicly revealed that he had considered retiring from international football after the 2026 World Cup, but said a conversation with Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca and new head coach Jorge Jesus had convinced him to continue.

Seven days later, Ronaldo has left Portugal’s training camp after a dramatic breakdown in relations with Jesus.

7 July — Ronaldo leaves the World Cup without committing to Portugal

Portugal were eliminated from the 2026 World Cup following a 1-0 defeat to eventual champions Spain. After the match, Roberto Martínez announced his departure as Portugal manager.

Ronaldo was asked about his own international future but refused to make an immediate decision.

“Now is not the time to make that decision,” he said. He did, however, confirm that the 2026 tournament would be his final World Cup.

10 July — Jorge Jesus takes over

Jorge Jesus was appointed Portugal head coach three days later. The former Al Nassr boss already knew Ronaldo well, having coached him in Saudi Arabia.

Jesus immediately made clear that Ronaldo would not receive special treatment. “Cris will never be a problem, either for the Seleção or for me,” Jesus said.

“I had the pleasure of working with him for a year. When I thought he should play, he played. When I thought he shouldn’t play, he didn’t. I’ll do what I think is best for the Seleção.”

18 September — Ronaldo is selected

Jesus announced his first Portugal squad for the Nations League and Ronaldo was included, with his international career looking poised to continue under former Al-Nassr boss Jesus

23 September — Ronaldo confirms he is staying

Speaking at the Portugal Football Summit in Oeiras, Ronaldo admitted that he had considered leaving the national team immediately after the World Cup.

But he revealed that conversations with Proenca and Jesus changed his mind.

“Yes, I considered [leaving the national team after the World Cup]. I’m always thinking about my decisions, my future, my present. I’m a thinker. I have to think about everything,” Ronaldo said.

Then came the clearest confirmation of his intentions. “That’s why you see me here now. It means I’m going to continue.”

Ronaldo explained why he had chosen to stay.

“I had a conversation with our president and our coach. They count on me. I still believe I can help the national team achieve what they want.”

He was also highly complimentary of Jesus, describing him as “the perfect choice” for Portugal.

24 September – Ronaldo starts against Wales

Ronaldo started Portugal’s Nations League campaign against Wales in Lisbon but endured a frustrating evening, missing two huge chances as his Al-Nassr team-mate Joao Felix scored the winner.

The appearance came just one day after his public confirmation that he intended to continue playing for the national team.

27 September – Ronaldo is left on the bench against Norway

Three days later, the situation changed dramatically. Portugal travelled to Oslo to face Norway as Jesus selected João Félix and Gonçalo Ramos in attack, leaving Ronaldo on the bench.

Ronaldo did warm up during the second half, but the substitution never came. He remained an unused substitute as Portugal won 2-1, with Ramos scoring the winning goal.

27 September – Ronaldo heads straight to the dressing room

The situation attracted further attention after the final whistle.

While Portugal’s players acknowledged the travelling supporters, Ronaldo headed towards the dressing room.

28-29 September – Ronaldo trains away from the group

Ronaldo did not take part in Portugal’s normal group training sessions on the following days.

The FPF maintained that he had no physical problem and that he was working individually in the gym.

29 September – Portugal chief changes his plans

The situation had become serious enough for FPF president Pedro Proença to change his plans and travel to Copenhagen.

Proença was due to meet Ronaldo and Jesus as Portugal prepared for their next Nations League fixture.

The development was particularly significant given Ronaldo’s comments just six days earlier, when he had said that both Proença and Jesus counted on him.

30 September – Jesus insists there is no problem

With Portugal preparing to face Denmark, Jesus attempted to calm the situation. “He didn’t refuse. He’s going to train today,” Jesus said.

“It’s the fourth day, so he’s going to train. And he didn’t refuse to train. It’s impossible. Do you believe that? Not Cris.”

Jesus also said that he had been forced to speak to Ronaldo about an issue that, in his view, did not exist.

“They forced me to talk to Cris about an issue that didn’t exist. There was nothing to talk about.”

According to Jesus, Ronaldo had told him: “I’m here for you to decide. If you want me to play, I’ll play. If you want me to go to the stands, I’ll go.”

30 September – Ronaldo leaves the Portugal camp

The situation then escalated dramatically. After Jesus’ press conference and a conversation with Proenca, Ronaldo decided to leave Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen.

A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

Ronaldo said he would explain his reasons at a later date.

“In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons behind my departure from the national team, to which I have always been fully committed.”

The FPF subsequently confirmed that Ronaldo had left the camp.

articles.title: Erling Haaland ‘no different’ after Manchester City guilty verdict
articles.summary: There has been no discernible change in Erling Haaland's behaviour despite the uncertainty surrounding his club career at Manchester City, according to Norway defender Kristoffer Ajer
articles.content:
Erling Haaland ‘no different’ after Manchester City guilty verdict

There has been no discernible change in Erling Haaland's behaviour despite the uncertainty surrounding his club career at Manchester City, according to Norway defender Kristoffer Ajer

Last Update:

Erling Haaland has been “no different” in his behaviour after the “sham contract” verdict against Manchester City, according to Norway team-mate Kristoffer Ajer.

Haaland will play for the first time on Thursday since the Premier League’s damning verdict on Man City, which said the club has artifically inflated their club revenue by £900million between 2009 and 2018.

Norway take on Wales in the Nations League on Thursday, when Haaland will be in the spotlight as his club faces a huge amount of uncertainty after the Premier League statement.

“Ever since I met him brings lot of energy and joy to the group,” said Brentford centre-back Ajer when asked about Haaland’s demeanour in the Norway camp since City’s guilty verdict was announced on Tuesday.

“That’s the biggest compliment I always give, he hasn’t changed a bit from the moment I met him, even though he’s the the biggest star on the planet right now.

“He been exactly the same the last few days as well which is is not a surprise for me.”

Reports of City’s guilty verdict first surfaced in the media on Friday.

City verdict ‘not discussed’ in Norway camp

Haaland scored against Portugal in a 2-1 defeat two days later, after earlier scoring two versus Denmark to extend his record as the Nations League’s all-time top scorer to 22.

Ajer said: “He’s the best player in the world if you ask me, so hopefully he scores a few tomorrow as well.

“I have to admit that honestly I’ve read very little into it [the City situation]. We don’t talk about it much here.

“Obviously, it was a statement released yesterday, so it’s quite fresh and new.

“But we’re just footballers, we don’t know all the ins and outs and all the stuff that’s being talked about in the media.

“So we haven’t really had any fantastic discussions about it where we know a lot.”

Man City verdict: Haaland future uncertain

Haaland and many of his team-mates’ futures could be thrown into serious doubt following the verdict, with the punishment yet to be decided.

No pubishment is said to be off the table, with suggestions the club could be expelled from the Premier League, which would surely see the likes of Haaland depart the club.

No current player has commented on the verdict, although City have released another statement reaffirming that they strenously deny the claims and have irrefutable evidence to clear their name.

articles.title: BREAKING: Cristiano Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp as international future thrown into doubt
articles.summary: Ronaldo may have played his last game for Portugal
articles.content:
BREAKING: Cristiano Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp as international future thrown into doubt

Ronaldo may have played his last game for Portugal

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal’s camp following manager Jorge Jesus’ comments about leaving him on the bench for their 2-1 win over Norway.

The 41-year-old wrote on his Instagram on Wednesday night: “Following the national team manager’s press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp.

“In due course, I will tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons behind my departure from the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

“Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception.”

A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

The Al-Nassr player is set to board his private jet to Madrid in the next few hours after the fallout, despite Jesus insisting only a few hours ago that “there was never a problem between the pair”.

Ronaldo’s international future is now said to be in serious doubt, with the forward near certain not to feature in Portugal’s remaining two Nations League games against Denmark and Norway.

The former Real Madrid and Manchester United star was an unused substitute in Portugal’s win in Oslo on Sunday, with his replacement Goncalo Ramos on the scoresheet in the victory.

He started in the Selecao’s 1-0 win over Wales last week but was substituted in the 67th minute.

Ronaldo has 234 caps and is their record goalscorer with 143 goals, winning the Euros and the Nations League during his time with his national team.

The Al-Nassr veteran was expected to depart after the World Cup in the summer, which he scored three goals at as Portugal exited in the round of 16.

Portugal manager Jesus: ‘I’m in charge of who plays’

While Jesus played down in any issue between the pair in his pre-match press conference for the Denmark game, he made it clear that he would be in charge of the decisions, and that reputations will not affect his tactical choices.

“I can promise whatever I want. I’m the coach. I’m the coach, I told the player he wasn’t going to play,” Jesus said.

I’ll put you on the bench. If I need you for 30 minutes, you’ll play; if not, you won’t. No player will make me change my mind.

“Not him, not anyone in football. Not any president. Never, absolutely no one.”

Ronaldo leaves the Portugal camp: How it all unfolded

What began with Cristiano Ronaldo being left on the bench against Norway quickly developed into a major story around the Portugal camp.

Here is how the situation unfolded.

A few days ago — Ronaldo starts on the bench against Norway

The controversy began in Oslo during Portugal’s Nations League clash with Norway.

Cristiano Ronaldo was surprisingly named among the substitutes, with Jorge Jesus opting to start João Félix and Gonçalo Ramos in attack.

The decision appeared to pay off on the pitch. Both Félix and Ramos scored as Portugal secured a 2-1 victory.

However, the focus soon shifted from the result to Ronaldo.

Ronaldo does not come on

Despite warming up during the second half, Ronaldo remained on the bench for the entire match and did not make an appearance.

It was an unusual sight for Portugal’s captain and all-time leading goalscorer.

Ronaldo heads straight to the dressing room

Following the final whistle, Ronaldo reportedly went straight to the dressing room rather than joining the celebrations with his teammates.

The incident immediately fuelled speculation about his reaction to being left out.

The following day – Ronaldo misses training

The situation escalated when Ronaldo did not join the other substitutes for training the following day.

Jorge Jesus subsequently sought to play down the situation, describing Ronaldo’s absence as something “normal” for the Madeira-born forward.

Pedro Proença changes his plans

The biggest indication that the situation was being taken seriously came when Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença changed his plans and travelled to Copenhagen.

His purpose was to meet with both Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus.

Wednesday morning – Ronaldo, Jesus and Proenca meet

The meeting took place in Copenhagen on Wednesday morning, bringing together Portugal’s captain, his head coach and the president of the Portuguese Football Federation.

The development intensified speculation surrounding Ronaldo’s position within the national team.

Jorge Jesus insists there is no problem

Despite the growing attention surrounding the situation, Jorge Jesus maintained that there was no problem involving Ronaldo.

The coach knows Ronaldo well, having previously worked with him at Al Nassr, where the pair won the Saudi league.

The situation escalates

What had initially been a surprise decision to leave Ronaldo on the bench against Norway had, within a matter of days, developed into a significant issue surrounding the Portugal camp.

Ronaldo’s omission from the starting XI, his failure to make an appearance, his subsequent absence from training and the intervention of federation president Pedro Proença all contributed to the growing uncertainty.

At this stage, the events described above establish a clear sequence of developments – but they do not, on their own, establish the precise terms or circumstances of any permanent departure from Portugal.

articles.title: Burnham would be ‘really concerned’ to lose Man City owners over financial breaches
articles.summary: The prime minister praised City Football Group's impact on Manchester.
articles.content:
Burnham would be ‘really concerned’ to lose Man City owners over financial breaches

The prime minister praised City Football Group's impact on Manchester.

Last Update:

UK prime minister Andy Burnham would be “concerned to lose” Manchester City‘s Abu-Dhabi-based owners if they were forced out after the club was found guilty of 114 breaches of financial regulations.

City were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League, which confirmed the decision by an independent commission in a statement on Tuesday.

Among the breaches were the creation of ‘sham’ contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over nine years covering the 2009-10 season to the 2017-18 campaign.

City have until Friday, October 2, to appeal, and will exercise their right to do so. They could eventually take the case as far as the High Court and claim the process was not impartial.

A points deduction that effectively relegates City from the Premier League to the Championship is viewed as a likely punishment, while a transfer ban and a massive fine are also distinct possibilities.

The prospect of expulsion from the Premier League, which could see the club doomed to non-league if the EFL refuses to accept them as a member, has also been raised. However, a motion on expulsion would require 15 of the 20 Premier League clubs to vote in favour to pass.

The Independent Football Regulator, set up by the UK government in 2025, said City’s case raised “serious issues” and indicated it would explore its options, including the possibility of stripping the owners of their licence to own the club once the appeal process reaches its conclusion.

In an interview with the BBC, Burnham, an Everton fan, referenced their points deduction for a breach of the Premier League’s Profit and Sustainability Rules in 2024. The Toffees were originally docked 10 points, but that was reduced to six on appeal.

“I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time, and you know, with hindsight, I think more people would say that wasn’t fair the way that was handled,” Burnham said. “So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I’d had before becoming prime minister.”

The former Mayor of Manchester also praised the City Football Group, the subsidiary that runs the club and is 81 percent owned by Abu Dhabi United Group, for its impact on the local area.

“I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn’t just put into the Etihad and the campus around it but also into the city,” he added.

“I would be really concerned to lose them. They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester. Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.

“I can’t intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it’s ongoing, and because it’s still contested by Manchester City, then I think it’s right that I don’t say much more.

“I have to keep my distance from it. It would be wrong for me to do anything else. It’s an independent legal process that has to play its course through.

“So for the reasons I gave at the start, you know, I was involved in one myself in relation to Everton. I think it’s frustrating when people rush to judgment and proclaim people guilty. I think the thing has to be allowed to run its course.”

articles.summary: Klopp is happy with his achievements at Anfield.
articles.content:
Klopp ‘far from preparing for a title’ after Man City guilty verdicts

Klopp is happy with his achievements at Anfield.

Last Update:

Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp laughed off the prospect of his team being retrospectively awarded further titles after Manchester City were found guilty of 114 breaches of financial regulations.

The Premier League confirmed in a statement on Tuesday that, following an independent commission ruling, City had been guilty of all but one of the charges of financial breaches brought against the club.

Among the breaches were the creation of ‘sham’ contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over nine years covering the 2009-10 season to the 2017-18 campaign.

City have until Friday, October 2, to appeal the decision, and will exercise their right to do so. They could eventually take the case as far as the High Court and claim the process was not impartial.

Several severe punishments could be on the cards if City’s appeal fails. A points deduction that dooms them to relegation to the Championship appears a likely penalty, with a massive fine and restrictions on signing players also distinct possibilities.

The prospect of expulsion from the Premier League has also been raised. That could see City condemned to non-league if the EFL refuses to accept them as members, but 15 of the 20 top-flight teams would need to vote in favour of an expulsion motion for it to become a reality.

There have also been calls for City to be retrospectively stripped of the titles they won during that nine-year period.

Klopp’s Liverpool finished second to Pep Guardiola’s City in 2018-19 and 2021-22. In the period in question, Liverpool lost the 2016 EFL Cup final to City on penalties.

Speaking in a press conference ahead of his country’s game with Serbia, Germany coach Klopp dismissed the idea of further honours coming his way, adding that he is satisfied with the successes he enjoyed during a storied tenure at Anfield.

“I’m far from preparing for a title or anything like that,” Klopp said.

“I’m absolutely fine with what we’ve achieved in Liverpool. We fought hard on the pitch. I can’t say more about that because I don’t know the details.”

articles.title: ‘There was never a problem’ – Jesus rejects talk of Ronaldo fallout after omission from Norway game
articles.summary: Jesus blamed the media for forcing the clear-the-air talks between the two.
articles.content:
‘There was never a problem’ – Jesus rejects talk of Ronaldo fallout after omission from Norway game

Jesus blamed the media for forcing the clear-the-air talks between the two.

Last Update:

Jorge Jesus stressed there was never any issue between himself and Cristiano Ronaldo over the Portugal star’s absence from their win over Norway, with the coach insisting his omission was pre-planned and that the record goalscorer had not refused to train ahead of Thursday’s meeting with Denmark.

Portugal’s visit to Parken will take place amid a backdrop of drama after a 2-1 UEFA Nations League victory at Ulleval Stadium, from which Ronaldo was left out.

Ronaldo was replaced in the starting XI by Goncalo Ramos and was not selected to come on as a substitute. The 41-year-old was visibly irritated and marched straight down the tunnel at the final whistle rather than joining his team-mates as they celebrated a fine win with the travelling supporters.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward subsequently did not train with the other unused substitutes on Monday in Malmo, Sweden as Portugal prepared to face Denmark in Copenhagen.

The Al-Nassr star appeared before Tuesday’s training session but was not involved, with the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF)  explaining that Ronaldo was on a specific training programme for which the Eleda Stadium did not have the right facilities.

Jesus: Ronaldo omission was pre-planned

A Bola reported Ronaldo and Jesus held clear-the-air talks in an effort to resolve their differences but, speaking in his pre-match press conference, Jesus insisted there was never an issue between the two.

Jesus clarified the arrangements for Ronaldo during an extended international break, saying: “Yes, it’s true that I agreed [a plan] with him, but I didn’t agree with him alone.

“We put a plan in place, just as I did with Bruno Fernandes.

“I told Cristiano that I believed he would not play in the Norway and Denmark matches.”

“When we held our first press conference in Portugal, he [Cristiano] himself spoke about this matter.

“He said that it was up to what the coach wanted, whether the coach wanted him to play, sit on the bench, or whatever else.

“So, he didn’t refuse anything at all. That’s exactly what happened. But I’m not going to sit on the bench thinking, ‘After 60 minutes I’ll do this, and after 70 minutes I’ll do that’. That’s not how I work. The match itself will tell me what I need to do.

“I was thinking that perhaps, despite our agreement that he wouldn’t play the first two matches, I might need him in the final few minutes.

“But the match imposed other things on me. It started telling me different things, and that’s why I didn’t bring him on. That’s the reality of it.

“What happened was simply that I told Cris he wouldn’t play in the first two matches, and then during the game I thought: perhaps I’ll need him.

“I asked him to warm up, and afterwards I didn’t bring him on.

“Any player and I was a player myself, who warms up for 20 or 30 minutes and then doesn’t come onto the pitch will feel frustrated. Any player, let alone Cris, given his status. Even if it were Pelé or Maradona, if they warmed up for 30 minutes and then didn’t come on, they would feel frustrated.

“That is what status means. But the rights are equal for everyone.”

Dismissing reports about Ronaldo deliberately skipping training, Jesus added: “He did not refuse to train.

“Cristiano did some work in the gym, did some mobility exercises on the pitch, and then did some additional muscle-strengthening work at the hotel. That’s exactly what happened. He did not refuse to train.

“Today he will train, and if you come and watch the training session, you will see him training, because today is the fourth day, so he will train.

“Sometimes I find it difficult to understand certain things. Do you really think that any player at national-team level could refuse to train? I’m not talking about Portugal only, but any national team.

“Unless he wants to leave and has another program arranged, but simply refusing to train like that? No. That’s what I wanted to clarify.”

Jesus blames media for ‘clear-the-air’ talks

It had also been reported that the tension between Jesus and Ronaldo prompted FPF president Pedro Proenca to travel to Copenhagen for the game.

But Jesus emphatically dismissed the significance of Proenca’s presence, while accusing the media of forcing him to have talks with Ronaldo because of the scale of the coverage around his omission.

“You, so to speak, forced me to speak with Cristiano about an issue that didn’t exist in the first place,” Jesus said. “Because you keep talking about this so much in Portugal, and honestly, I don’t understand what’s going on.

“There was nothing to discuss. And what we talked about was exactly what he said on the first day during our press conference.

“He told me: ‘You decide. If you want me to play, I’ll play. If you don’t want me to play, I won’t play. If you want me to go into the stands, I’ll go into the stands.’

“That’s exactly what happened between us.

“As for the president, it’s completely normal for him to be here. The club president and the federation president should be with the national team. And because of everything that was being said in Portugal, he wanted to know what had happened, right?

“But Cristiano and I had already discussed it after dinner. And the truth is, the problem is that there was never a problem in the first place.”

articles.content:
Ruben Dias asked about Manchester City uncertainty and defends Cristiano Ronaldo from accusations of selfishness

Ruben Dias was surprisingly put up by Portugal to answer questions ahead of Thursday's game with Denmark. He was asked about Manchester City and Cristiano Ronaldo...

Last Update:

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias refused to discuss the uncertainty around the club after they were found guilty of breaching 114 financial fair play regulations.

The Premier League confirmed on Tuesday what had been reported last week; that an independent commission deemed the club had systematically broken the rules with “sham” contracts designed to inflate revenue and reduce costs.

The scale of the deception, reported to have totalled more than £900million, was breathtaking and a number of sanctions now lie on the table. City have continued to deny any wronging and are planning an appeal.

Dias, who is on international duty with Portugal, was asked about the situation ahead of tomorrow’s Nations League game with Denmark but swerved the question.

The central defender said: “I understand the question perfectly, but I won’t comment on anything that is not related to the National Team.”

Dias defends under-fire Ronaldo

Dias was a little more forthcoming when it came to Cristiano Ronaldo and his role in the national team.

Ronaldo has hit the headlines this week after failing to train after being left on the bench for Sunday’s 2-1 win in Norway. The issue has overshadowed the build-up to the game against Denmark and, although boss Jorge Jesus insisted the 41-year-old had not refused to take part in two training sessions, there appears no other logical explanation.

Ronaldo also disappeared straight down the tunnel at the Ullevaal Stadium at the weekend, failing to celebrate the victory with his team-mates. Portugal won the game thanks to a goal from Ronaldo’s replacement Goncalo Ramos but the Al-Nassr striker’s actions have stolen the headlines away from his team-mates.

Asked for his thoughts on the incident, Dias said: “It was a moment of frustration of 10, 15 or 20 seconds. Out of nothing they [the critics] take away his commitment of more than 20 years with our team. In one moment you have this period of frustration and after five minutes we are all celebrating an important victory of our national team.”

There’s no split in the Portugal camp due to Ronaldo – Dias

It is unlikely Ronaldo’s behaviour would have gone down well with the rest of the squad but Dias insisted there was no friction within the group.

He added: “Today you will see in training. You will feel the joy, you will see us smile, you will see us happy. It’s a new cycle. We are all very happy to be diving into this new adventure and we are excited about what’s coming.”

Asked if he had spoken to Ronaldo, he said: “These are moments that happen, as with any other. Tell me a player who has never had a problem with a coach, or a complicated situation, a moment of friction? Who never had a moment of frustration with the coach or with himself? They are natural things that we live. It’s important to know how to move on.”

articles.title: Pep Guardiola says he is ‘behind my owner and my chairman’ after Manchester City found guilty of financial doping
articles.summary: Pep Guardiola has spoken out in defence of Manchester City despite the club being found guilty of numerous counts of financial malpractice
articles.content:
Pep Guardiola says he is ‘behind my owner and my chairman’ after Manchester City found guilty of financial doping

Pep Guardiola has spoken out in defence of Manchester City despite the club being found guilty of numerous counts of financial malpractice

Last Update:

Pep Guardiola has launched an extraordinary defence of Manchester City, insisting he is “more than ever” behind the club’s owners after they were found to have broken multiple financial rules.

On Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18, and the majority of charges relating to a failure to co-operate with the investigation.

A damning statement that concluded the probe by an independent commission highlighted a series of “sham contracts” set up by the club to artificially inflate revenue and reduce costs via a ‘disguised funding scheme’ to the scale of over £900million.

That enabled City to circumnavigate PSR rules and spend lavishly in the transfer market with Guardiola able to bolster his squad with the likes of John Stones, Ilkay Gundogan and Leroy Sane.

Those players went on to win multiple trophies at the Etihad with Guardiola eventually standing down at the end of last season having claimed six Premier League crowns, three FA Cup trophies and the 2023 Champions League title.

City have repeatedly protested their innocence and intend to appeal with Guardiola regularly speaking up in defence of the club’s owners, the City Football Group Limited spearheaded by Abu Dhabi royal family member Sheikh Mansour and run by Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Ferran Soriano, during his time in Manchester.

Guardiola remained staunch in his defence of the club on Wednesday with a post on Instagram that read: “I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

“Let me be clear: we will get through this together.

“I love you all.” 🩵

A post shared by PepTeam (@pepteam)

City maintain their innocence

City were quick to respond with a statement of their own on Tuesday afternoon after the Premier League dropped their bombshell, claiming they have a “body of irrefutable evidence” that would lead to all charges being dropped.

There had been speculation Guardiola, who is currently keeping a low profile after a relentless period at City, would speak out against the owners but he has opted to offer them his unflinching support.

The main question now is what happens if City’s appeal is thrown out. Relegation, a transfer ban, a hefty points deduction and a fine have all been mentioned as potential punishments.

Whatever happens, the case has cast a dark cloud over the Premier League ever since the initial charges were announced in February 2023.

Enzo Maresca replaced Guardiola at the helm and he now has the tricky task of trying to focus the minds of the players, who are facing an uncertain future, when they return from international duty. City’s next Premier League game is at Liverpool a week on Sunday and former Reds defender and current Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher is predicting a hostile atmosphere at Anfield.

“Liverpool are probably the biggest losers in all this,” said Carragher with Liverpool finishing as runners-up to City numerous times over the affected period.

“The atmosphere will be electric. In the last five years, Liverpool v City has been ‘the’ game of the Premier League.”

articles.title: Selfish Ronaldo needs to follow Messi’s lead and walk away rather than tarnish Portugal legacy
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's self-importance has sparked another debate this week, jeopardising Portugal's chances of victory against Denmark tomorrow night. It is time the veteran striker walked away with his legacy intact.
articles.content:
Selfish Ronaldo needs to follow Messi’s lead and walk away rather than tarnish Portugal legacy

Cristiano Ronaldo's self-importance has sparked another debate this week, jeopardising Portugal's chances of victory against Denmark tomorrow night. It is time the veteran striker walked away with his legacy intact.

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal are heading for a messy break-up.

Portugal enjoyed a hugely impressive win in Norway on Sunday night with Ronaldo’s replacement Goncalo Ramos scoring the winner nine minutes into the second half.

The 41-year-old was expected to come off the bench towards the end but remained rooted to his seat, marking the first time in 18 years the veteran striker was not called upon by his country when fit.

What came next was entirely predictable.

Rather than congratulate his team-mates, in particular Ramos who has been remarkably patient in waiting for his opportunity, and celebrate the three points with the travelling fans, Ronaldo skulked off down the tunnel.

Immediately, the attention turned from the win, the focus on a fine performance against a strong opponent, to the middle-aged man conspicuous by his absence.

Ronaldo fails to train as debate rages

Since that point, Ronaldo has not trained, on Monday when the rest of the unused players did a work-out, or on Tuesday, preferring instead to follow an individual programme at the team hotel.

No injury has been reported by the Portuguese Football Federation when it has had ample opportunity to do so. We can only assume, therefore, that Ronaldo has thrown his toys out of the pram and refused to participate.

Reports in Portugal suggest Ronaldo and boss Jorge Jesus thrashed out their differences on Tuesday evening and we now wait to see if the former Manchester United and Real Madrid man trains tonight ahead of tomorrow’s Nations League clash with Denmark in Copenhagen.

It should be noted that Ronaldo is acting this way despite working with Jesus last season to help deliver the Saudi Pro League title for Al-Nassr. They know each other well and yet Ronaldo still displays this level of disrespect.

The brave thing for Jesus to do is not indulge this level of selfishness. Keep Ramos in the team and Ronaldo sulking on the bench.

At his age, Ronaldo must accept he is no longer the player he was, his influence has been waning on the international stage for some time. If he claims to love Portugal the way he says he does then he must stand aside, with grace, and let Jesus manage.

Ronaldo tantrum nothing new

This is not the first time Ronaldo has put individual before collective.

There was the armband throwing episode in 2021 when a goal was disallowed against Serbia in a World Cup qualifier, the refusal to come on as a late substitute for Manchester United in 2022 and the crotch-grabbing incident in 2024 when rivals fans chanted for his age-old rival Lionel Messi, leading to a suspension. And many others.

Reaction to his latest nonsense in his homeland is divided.

Many feel Ronaldo’s time with the national team is over, that this indulgence has hampered the team’s chances at recent major tournaments and that he should show some humility and walk away with his legacy intact.

Others are more eager to point at his enormous influence on a country that struggled for significance on the international stage until his arrival. He played a prominent role in Portugal’s first major trophy – the 2016 European Championship – and led them to glory in the Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

One notable commentator even suggested Portugal should treat him the same way Argentina have built around Messi, protecting him from the advances of age and giving him the platform to succeed. The difference is Messi was still Argentina’s best player at this summer’s World Cup, the driving force behind their run to the final. And how could anyone forget the way he dragged his country, almost single-handedly, to the 2022 title in Qatar?

Messi inspires, Ronaldo sulks

Ronaldo has not held the same platform for Portugal for some time.

Messi opted to retire from international football after the World Cup, and is now looking forward to his farewell game next week in front of an adoring crowd in Buenos Aires. It was the right call at the right time, putting his country first.

Ronaldo continues to push on to the detriment of Portugal. For his own good, he needs to call it a day, rather than let someone have to make a call that will prompt endless debate and argument.

It’s difficult to see what he is hoping to achieve at this stage. Protect your legacy, cherish the good times, and walk away a hero. The time is now Cristiano.

articles.title: What is going on with Cristiano Ronaldo? Portugal star misses training and has talks with Jorge Jesus after being dropped
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has not trained since being left on the bench for Sunday evening's win in Norway
articles.content:
What is going on with Cristiano Ronaldo? Portugal star misses training and has talks with Jorge Jesus after being dropped

Cristiano Ronaldo has not trained since being left on the bench for Sunday evening's win in Norway

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal boss Jorge Jesus are reported to have had clear-the-air talks after the Al-Nassr striker failed to come off the bench during the 2-1 win in Norway on Sunday.

Having been replaced in the starting XI by Goncalo Ramos, Jesus admitted afterwards he told Ronaldo he would come on at some point during the game at the Ullevall Stadium. But he reneged on that promise, instead keeping the 41-year-old on the sidelines.

Ronaldo was visibly irritated and marched straight down the tunnel at the final whistle rather than joining his team-mates as they celebrated a fine win with the travelling supporters.

The apparent fall-out has stewed since with the team moving from Norway to Malmo, Sweden to prepare for tomorrow night’s game with Denmark in the Nations League.

Ronaldo skips training for two days

The other substitutes that did not play against Norway trained on Monday but Ronaldo was absent, despite there being no word on any physical issue.

On Tuesday, Ronaldo joined the rest of his team-mates at the Eleda Stadium and appeared before training started, sitting on the bench drinking coffee, before then being whisked back to the hotel while the squad went through their paces.

The Portuguese Football Federation explained that Ronaldo was on a specific training programme and the Eleda Stadium did not have the right equipment and he would therefore undergo an individual session back at the team base.

A Bola claim Ronaldo and Jesus, who are known to have a strong working relationship after combining to help Al-Nassr win the Saudi Pro League last season, spoke last night in a bid to iron out any differences.

But it now remains to be seen if the former Manchester United and Real Madrid star will be available for the game with Denmark given he has not trained since the weekend.

For his part, Ronaldo has not voiced any frustration and took to social media yesterday to post a picture of himself next to emojis of the Portuguese flag and a heart.

Jesus is due to speak to the press this afternoon and will be accompanied by a player yet to be determined. Training at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen will follow and it could be that another no-show by Ronaldo means he is not in contention to play in tomorrow night’s Group A4 clash.

Denmark boss Riemer believes Portugal are better with Ronaldo

That news would be welcomed by Denmark boss Brian Riemer who talked up Ronaldo’s importance to Portugal.

Speaking on TV2, he said: “It’s a bit silly to be discussing this around Cristiano Ronaldo. I believe that many people underestimate his importance to the Portuguese team. On the day he retires, Portugal will have a problem. There are many strong personalities in a national team like Portugal’s and who will organise the hierarchy [when he goes]? It will be a great challenge.

“Ronaldo’s importance should not be underestimated. The best team in Portugal includes Ronaldo. When you face Portugal, you face world-class players in all positions. I tell the players: these are the challenges they need to face with determination.

“We are not the favourites, even playing at home. We know that we will face a very good team and that we will have to present an exceptional performance to have a chance of winning.”

articles.title: Gordon ‘showing he belongs’ as Tuchel hails Alexander-Arnold and ‘excellent’ Hall
articles.summary: It's three goals in Gordon's last three games for England.
articles.content:
Gordon ‘showing he belongs’ as Tuchel hails Alexander-Arnold and ‘excellent’ Hall

It's three goals in Gordon's last three games for England.

Last Update:

Anthony Gordon is “showing he belongs” at the highest level, England captain Harry Kane said after the winger continued his excellent form for his country in their 2-0 away win over Czechia.

Gordon was on target last Saturday as England suffered a 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley in a thrilling UEFA Nations League opener for the Three Lions.

And it was the Barcelona man who broke the deadlock on Tuesday as Thomas Tuchel’s men bounced back in Prague, meeting Trent Alexander-Arnold’s superb right-wing cross with a stooping header under two minutes into the second half to put England in front against a Czechia side that had Pavel Sulc sent off in the first half.

That goal made it three in Gordon’s last three appearances for England, the former Newcastle United man having put them ahead in the 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Kane then doubled England’s lead to effectively put the game beyond doubt with his 123rd senior international goal.

But the Bayern Munich talisman reserved praise for Gordon when speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live after the game.

“He’s showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England,” said Kane.

“His performances in the last couple of games have been some of his best that he has played in an England shirt and I think he is just relishing putting the shirt on and being one of the main men in the team.

“He is an important player for us and he showed that during the World Cup.”

Gordon regularly combined extremely well down the left-hand side with former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall.

Both Hall and Alexander-Arnold were omitted from the squad from the World Cup before being handed recalls for the first international break of the new season.

And Tuchel was impressed with the performances of both full-backs.

Speaking to ITV, Tuchel said of the pair: “Both good. The position in the second half suited Trent more than in the first half. Lewis did excellent on the other side.

“Credit to all of them because they deserved [it] and now it is important that we relax and enjoy the evening, do a good recovery and then prepare for Croatia.”

Real Madrid defender Alexander-Arnold’s absence from the England set-up under Tuchel has regularly attracted criticism.

Prior to Tuesday’s game, Alexander-Arnold’s last appearance for his country came against Andorra in a World Cup qualifier in June last year.

In further praise of his display on his return, Tuchel added to 5Live: “He did very well. He had an excellent assist. Overall like everyone [he] was professional, top attitude and one decisive action.”

articles.title: Lamine Yamal makes Ballon d’Or claim after starring for Spain against Croatia
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal says he has enough arguments to win the Ballon d'Or this season.
articles.content:
Lamine Yamal makes Ballon d’Or claim after starring for Spain against Croatia

Lamine Yamal says he has enough arguments to win the Ballon d'Or this season.

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal strengthened his case as the Ballon d’Or frontrunner with a superb display during Spain’s 4-1 win over Croatia on Tuesday night.

The Barcelona winger scored twice and provided an assist as Spain made the perfect start to life in their new campaign, with the win extending their unbeaten run to 40 matches.

Yamal opened the scoring inside the opening minutes before adding Spain’s third goal after the break.

His first strike came after a move involving Alex Baena and Fermin Lopez left him with an opening inside the penalty area, with Yamal choosing to shoot towards the near post and catching goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic off guard.

Yamal explained afterwards that his familiarity with the Croatia goalkeeper helped him decide where to place the finish.

“I already know him from training, I have thought about training, about what he does and it has entered me,” Yamal said.

Yamal gives blunt Ballon d’Or answer

Yamal was asked whether his performance had provided another argument for him to win the Ballon d’Or, with the winger answering with two words.

“Another one.”

The vote for this year’s award has already closed, meaning Yamal’s latest performance will not have an impact on the result, but the 19-year-old insisted the individual prize is not driving his ambitions.

“In the end I don’t just play for this Ballon d’Or, I play for myself, for the fans, for next season, for my team, to continue winning,” Yamal said.

“I don’t know, I don’t vote, nor do I know who won, I don’t know anything. Let’s wait and keep playing.

“We are very excited to be able to bring the cup here and show it to the fans and be able to win and bring it home, great.

“We always have to come out plugged in, what the coach tells us, what we talk to each other and very happy for the victory,” Yamal said.

articles.title: AFCON 2027 qualifying: Nigeria humiliated as Ghana also suffer shock defeat
articles.summary: The Super Eagles' qualification hopes took a huge hit.
articles.content:
AFCON 2027 qualifying: Nigeria humiliated as Ghana also suffer shock defeat

The Super Eagles' qualification hopes took a huge hit.

Last Update:

Nigeria suffered a humiliating 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau on a day of shocks in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

The Super Eagles, three-time AFCON champions, missed out on the 2026 World Cup, and their hopes of featuring at next year’s tournament in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda suffered a significant setback in Bissau.

Franculino Dju curled Guinea-Bissau into a 15th-minute lead before Mama Balde fired in off the post to double that advantage. Alvaro Djalo added a third in stoppage time, sending Guinea-Bissau three points clear of Nigeria at the top of Group L, which contains a Tanzania side that has already qualified as hosts, meaning only the group winners will progress.

Ghana face an uphill battle to reach the AFCON finals after the Black Stars suffered a second successive defeat.

Following their 2-0 loss to Ivory Coast in their opening Group C game, Carlos Queiroz’s men were beaten 4-2 at home by Gambia.

Ghana appeared in command after a penalty from Ernest Nuamah and a goal from Felix Afena-Gyan gave them a 2-0 lead. However, Gambia produced a superb comeback, Muhammed Badamosi pulling one back from the penalty spot and Omar Colley levelling matters before half-time.

Ebrima Colley completed the turnaround, and then settled the contest with his second in the first minute of stoppage time.

Ivory Coast left it late to see off Somalia 2-0, an 89th minute goal from Coventry City’s Yann Gboho breaking the deadlock before Newcastle’s United Bazoumana Toure fired in on rebound in stoppage time.

Meanwhile, Morocco made it two wins from two in Group A by beating Lesotho 2-0 away from home.

The Atlas Lions, controversially awarded the 2025 title after the result of their final with Senegal was overturned by CAF, prevailed thanks to goals from Brahim Diaz and Azzedine Ounahi.

Nicolas Jackson set up Aston Villa team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye for the only goal of the game as Senegal got their first win in Group J, claiming a 1-0 away victory against Ethiopia having started with a 1-1 draw against Mozambique.

Egypt responded to the frustration of their opening draw with Angola by thrashing South Sudan 5-0, Tottenham forward Omar Marmoush scoring twice in a Group B rout in Juba.

But Cape Verde, whose progress to the knockout rounds made them one of the stories of the World Cup, are without a point from their two Group K games after losing 2-1 at home to Rwanda.

Benchimol gave Cape Verde the lead, but goals from Claude Niyomugabo and Elie Iradukunda Tatou turned the game around. Cape Verde are now six points shy of a qualification place.

Algeria avoided a major shock in Group I as they came back from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Burundi. In Group G, a second-half own goal spared Cameroon’s blushes, the Lions of Teranga coming from 1-0 down to earn a 1-1 draw with Congo.

articles.title: McGinn urges Scotland to overcome ‘big setback’ after humbling loss to Switzerland
articles.summary: John McGinn has had his say on Scotland's 3-0 loss to Switzerland.
articles.content:
McGinn urges Scotland to overcome ‘big setback’ after humbling loss to Switzerland

John McGinn has had his say on Scotland's 3-0 loss to Switzerland.

Last Update:

John McGinn has called Scotland’s 3-0 Nations League defeat to Switzerland at Hampden Park a “big setback” and insisted the side must use it as a learning experience, after Jack Hendry’s red card inside the opening quarter-hour stripped the hosts of any chance of getting their Group B1 campaign off the ground.

Hendry’s initial yellow card for a foul was upgraded to a red by VAR in the 11th minute, and Switzerland made their numerical advantage count almost immediately when Ruben Vargas was tripped in the area and Zeki Amdouni’s club team-mate Fabian Rodriguez stepped up to convert the penalty in the 12th.

Nico Elvedi doubled the lead before half-time as Dan Ndoye caused Scotland relentless problems, and Zeki Amdouni added a third to complete a ruthless Murat Yakin side’s second consecutive clean sheet.

The result leaves Sebastien Pocognoli’s side, who drew 0-0 away to Slovenia on Saturday in the manager’s debut, bottom of Group B1 with one point from two games. Switzerland sit top.

McGinn, one of the few Scotland players to emerge with any credit, acknowledged the scale of the evening’s damage while pointing to the fact that a squad still adjusting to an entirely new coaching approach under the 39-year-old Belgian, who replaced Steve Clarke in August.

“We could have done better at times but we’re starting a new chapter, learning to play a different way,” the Aston Villa captain said. “That was a big setback for us. We’ve got a lot to learn from tonight but a lot to take from it as well.”

“I thought Oli McBurnie was outstanding. He’s had a lot of criticism in a Scotland shirt but tonight was a thankless task and he gave everything for us.”

“Going down to 10 men, it’s a test of character, you need to dig in. It’s a huge learning curve for us and when we play them away we need to win now.”

That reverse fixture, Scotland travelling to Switzerland for the Matchday 4 encounter, now carries enormous weight in terms of whether Pocognoli’s side can remain competitive in the promotion race.

Switzerland’s superior goal difference after two games gives them a buffer the Scots will need to claw back.

articles.title: Yamal scores and assists as Spain take lead over Croatia
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal has scored and assisted for Spain in the Nations League against Croatia.
articles.content:
Yamal scores and assists as Spain take lead over Croatia

Lamine Yamal has scored and assisted for Spain in the Nations League against Croatia.

Last Update:

Spain have made a rapid start against Croatia and once again, Lamine Yamal has been at the centre of almost everything, with the score 2-1 to the world champions heading towards half-time.

Yamal opened the scoring inside the opening 90 seconds, the fastest goal of the 2026-27 Nations League so far.

He combined with Alex Baena and, after Fermin Lopez’ dummy helped create the opening, calmly swept the ball into the far corner with his trademark left foot.

He has since added an assist for Marc Pubill’s 31st-minute header. Yamal played a short corner to Fermin, received it back and floated a cross into the box for Pubill to power home.

That means the Barcelona winger has one goal and one assist, days after scoring in the 3-2 win over England.

He has also been heavily involved beyond the numbers. In the 20th minute, Yamal nearly picked out Mikel Oyarzabal with a clipped pass from the right, while Spain have repeatedly looked to him as they keep Croatia pinned back.

Croatia briefly levelled through Dion Beljo after Ivan Perisic delivered an excellent cross, but Spain remain in the driving seat thanks to Yamal’s efforts.

It coincides with his push to win the Ballon d’Or, which looks like a shootout between him and England captain Harry Kane.

The award will be decided next month at the London Palladium.
