articles.title: Rio Ngumoha: Why the Liverpool forward will ‘save club £130 million’… and has a ‘really big chance’ this season
articles.summary: The versatile forward was at Chelsea for eight years
articles.content:
Rio Ngumoha: Why the Liverpool forward will ‘save club £130 million’… and has a ‘really big chance’ this season

The versatile forward was at Chelsea for eight years

Last Update:

By the time Rio Ngumoha struck with a solo effort in Liverpool’s 3-1 win at Yokohama during pre-season, the 16-year-old’s dazzling runs and productive delivery had made a goal seem inevitable.

England Under-17 youth international Ngumoha had also shone four days earlier against Milan in Singapore, including an assist for Dominik Szoboszlai’s equaliser in the 4-2 defeat.

Reds manager Arne Slot has been cautious in his praise of Ngumoha and warned him about his occasional pass selection, but others have been more effusive in their predictions.

Here’s what winger Ngumoha has had to say about his latest spell in the first team and why team-mate Harvey Elliott and two ex-Liverpool regulars believe he has a huge future.

Best NFL Betting Promos | NFL Preseason GW1 Bonus Bets

Rio Ngumoha: Liverpool’s Lamine Yamal?

Former Chelesa prospect Ngumoha joined Liverpool’s academy in September 2024, scoring two goals in eight assists in the Premier League 2 last season and making six Uefa Youth League appearances.

Jason McAteer, who made 139 appearances for Liverpool between 1995 and 1999, believes Ngumoha could solve a future transfer headache.

“When you look at the way the transfer windows are going for this type of player, we spent [up to] £116m on [Florian] Wirtz,” former right-back McAteer told LFC TV.

“As the seasons go on, that’s only going to increase and you’ll be looking at 120, 130, 140. In two or three seasons’ time, when he’s 19, and probably before that, when he’s ready to go in as a first-team regular, that’s going to save them 130 million.

pic.twitter.com/qBo70eOAkd

“It can be daunting when you move into a first-team environment, but he’s flourishing. I’m not putting him up there with [Barcelona’s Lamine] Yamal – certainly not – but if you’re good enough, you’re old enough.

“It’s vitally important that Liverpool are producing academy talent season after season. The pathway for the academy talent is there if they’re given the opportunity. He’s a very, very special boy.”

Harvey Elliott: Ngumoha ‘incredible’

Harvey Elliott, who knows about expectations during a Liverpool career that began with the winger starting an EFL Cup match as a 16-year-old in 2019, called Ngumoha “fearless”.

“He showed that against AC Milan, one of Europe’s big teams,” said Elliott. “He looked like a kid in a park, although he is a kid. He just needs to carry on like this.

“We’re trying as much as we can to help him out. If he keeps on performing the way he is and working hard, the kid’s got an amazing future.

“I’m really excited to see where things go. Myself and the younger lads are closer to him in age. There aren’t many 16 or 17-year-olds in the team. He’s in because he’s incredible at his age and able to handle to himself.”

“It’s important the younger lads are around him and look after him, which is what we’ve been doing. Not leave him out – bring him into the squad and make him feel really part of it.”

Ngumoha: Andy Robertson an inspiration

Ngumoha, who started Liverpool’s 4-0 home win over Accrington Stanley in the FA Cup on January 11, called his display against Yokahama “a very big night” and “just the first of many.”

“I’ll keep on working hard and show the manager what I can do,” he vowed, crediting Andy Robertson with “really helping me a lot”.

“He’s so experienced and one of the best left-backs in the world. I feel like having him behind me, you can’t really ask for anything more.

“He teaches me a lot. [For the goal] I think they lost the ball and then Robbo passed it to me. In my mind, I was thinking ‘can I score?’, because I had a chance last time.

“My brother is the biggest person in my life – him and my mum – and he’s definitely buzzing. I’m not trying to rush because I’m still only young.

“At the same time, I want to show the manager what I can do and not get too complacent, because I want bigger and better things for me and the club.”

Staying sharp ⚡️ Quick feet from Rio ✨ pic.twitter.com/fPeEs8kJrf

Rio Ngumoha loan move: ‘You can get lost’

Neil Mellor was prolific for Liverpool at youth level but did not establish himself as a first-choice striker during his time at the club between 1999 and 2006.

“Decisions have to be made with these young players, whether it’s training with the under-21s or the first team,” said Mellor.

“Where’s his game time going to be? It’s not going to be in the reserves, like it was for us. Does he get enough in the under-21 or under-19 games?”

Mellor feels Ngumoha should not go out on loan. “I’m a big believer that somebody who’s as talented as that needs to learn the standards for what’s expected at Liverpool Football Club,” he explained.

“To train every day with the best players in the world would be massive for his development. If he went on loan to someone like, I don’t know, West Brom in the Championship or Southampton, you can get lost or go backwards a little bit. It doesn’t suit everybody.

“I think he’s in the right place and right environment, with where this football club is at, to be in a position to say ‘I might be needed, in a year or two years, to play in the first team’.”

Conor’s touch 🪄Rio’s finish 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/Wc4nyI1m4l

Wirtz and Salah make team-mates ‘better’

Ngumoha was a month younger than Elliott when he featured against Accrington, although he is second to Jerome Sinclair – who was 16 years and six days of age against West Brom in the EFL Cup in 2012 – as the club’s youngest ever player.

“There are some 16-year-olds coming through who do well and are adaptable to their surroundings,” suggested McAteer.

“He’s one of them, I think. It’s a hard one because he’s a very, very talented player, but he’s 16. When I speak about ‘if you’re good enough, you’re old enough’ – that’s in a football maturity world.

“In life, there’s an immaturity about him because he’s 16. That’s not being critical. There’s a lot to learn – we’ve all been 16.”

McAteer also believes Ngumoha should stay put. “He needs protecting, in that sense, in staying at the club rather than going on loan,” he said.

“If he was 19… I’d put him out on loan at Blackburn or somewhere like that. Liverpool will be thinking whether he’s old enough to go out on loan or be kept hold of and develop.

“With the likes of Wirtz and [Mohamed] Salah, he’s only going to get better and mature quicker this season where he is.”

An incredible team move for the first 👏Rio Ngumoha with a brace for #LFCU21s against Aston Villa ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/sV8uH0pXNC

Will Ngumoha play in the Premier League this season?

Elliott is backing Ngumoha to continue breaking through in 2025/26. “He’s going to have a massive shot this season,” said the Under-21 Euro winner.

“We can all see his quality and I think he has a really, really big chance. In the upcoming years, hopefully he can show the world and everyone at Liverpool why he’s so highly rated.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Manchester City found guilty of all 115 Premier League charges after creating ‘sham’ contracts worth £900m
articles.summary: Manchester City have officially been found guilty of all 115 financial charges.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Manchester City found guilty of all 115 Premier League charges after creating ‘sham’ contracts worth £900m

Manchester City have officially been found guilty of all 115 financial charges.

Last Update:

Manchester City have been found guilty of all 115 charges relating to serious breaches of Premier League regulations, with the league confirming the long-awaited verdict on Tuesday.

City denied all of the allegations throughout the case, but an independent commission has now ruled against the club on every charge.

It includes creating a stream of ‘sham’ contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over nine years.

The Premier League issued a 1,545-word statement confirming the decision, bringing an end to an eight-year process which began with the league’s investigation into City’s financial affairs.

The club now have until Friday, October 2, to exercise their right to appeal.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters described the decision as the most significant disciplinary ruling in the competition’s history.

“The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

“It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

“It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

“This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.”

City maintain innocence and prepare appeal

Manchester City responded by once again rejecting the commission’s findings and insisting that evidence exists to support the club’s position.

City said they were “disappointed and surprised” by the decision and confirmed that they intend to pursue the appeal process.

A club statement read: “Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today. The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

“The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

“The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.”

Punishment still to be decided

Despite the scale of the verdict, Manchester City’s eventual punishment has not yet been confirmed.

The Premier League has stressed that the sanctions process is a separate stage of the case, meaning the commission’s findings do not immediately determine what disciplinary action the club will face.

Masters confirmed that sanctions remain outstanding and said the league wants the process to move forward as quickly as possible.

Potential punishments have been widely debated throughout the case, from points deductions to stripped titles, but no decision has yet been taken on what consequences will follow from the 115 guilty verdicts.

City’s appeal could also prolong the process, with the club now able to challenge the commission’s conclusions before any final outcome is reached.

articles.title: Vinicius Junior explains pointing at Bruno Guimaraes during Brazil win: ‘He knows’
articles.summary: Vinicius Junior scored in front of the Brazil fans against Australia
articles.content:
Vinicius Junior explains pointing at Bruno Guimaraes during Brazil win: ‘He knows’

Vinicius Junior scored in front of the Brazil fans against Australia

Last Update:

Vinicius Junior says he “needed a bit of confidence” after going seven matches without a goal before scoring in Brazil’s comeback win over Australia in an action-packed international friendly in Brisbane on Tuesday.

Forward Vinicius Junior’s only previous goal this season had been for Real Madrid in a 4-1 home win over Real Sociedad in La Liga on August 26, with his penalty 10 minutes from time against the Socceroos the 26-year-old’s first in four internationals.

Vini Jr finally gets his goal with a perfect penalty! ✨ The Real Madrid star picks out the bottom corner, leaving Patrick Beach with no chance 🎯 Watch #AUSvBRA live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/Wr5pMtH4QK

“Bruno is the penalty taker for us when [Raphinha] isn’t there and I thought he wanted to take it,” Vinicius Junior told SporTV, explaining why he had pointed at the Arsenal midfielder before converting the spot kick for the final goal in the 4-2 win.

“But he knows I needed a bit of confidence. It had been a few games since I last scored, but it’s important to get back to scoring and important to get back to playing with our national team.

“Now it’s time to rest over these next few days and travel to India [for a friendly on Saturday], because our fan base there is huge and they are waiting for us.”

Bruno Guimarães fires Brazil back into the lead! 🇧🇷The Arsenal midfielder gets his fourth international goal, finishing off a pinpoint pass from Endrick 👏Watch #AUSvBRA live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/OqsQ8pFnLX

Australia vs Brazil: Raphinha ‘was penalty taker’

Selecao head coach Carlo Ancelotti saw Raphinha score the first of Brazil’s two penalties, equalising in the 45th minute after Vanderson had given the visitors an early lead but Alessandro Circati’s flick and Connor Metcalfe’s long-range strike had put Australia 2-1 ahead.

“Raphinha was the penalty taker and he took the first one,” said Ancelotti, also referencing Bruno Guimaraes’ finish at the end of a slick team move to put Brazil 3-2 in front in the 69th minute.

“Bruno was the second but Bruno had already scored, so I think Vini deserved to score. He took the penalty well.”

Raphinha, who is the runaway top scorer in La Liga with 12 goals this season for Barcelona, was replaced at half-time by Endrick, who set up Bruno Guimaraes’ goal.

Brazil said Raphinha had been replaced because of muscle discomfort.

Ice cold from the spot by Raphinha 🥶The FC Barcelona star levels the score for Brazil with a clinical penalty 🎯Watch #AUSvBRA live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/mIpsKILxhP

Vinicius Junior penalty ‘best for Brazil’

New £75 million Gunners signing Guimaraes suggested the situation over the penalty reflected a set of Brazil players who “don’t have any ego”.

“In [a previous] game, Ancelotti told me to take it,” said the 28-year-old, who spoke last week of his enduring pain at having a penalty saved in Brazil’s 2-1 last-16 exit to Norway at the World Cup 2026.

“Today, he told Vini to take it. Vini also needed to score a goal… he went up and took it really well. We want what’s best for Brazil, that’s what matters to us.

“I’m happy for him and for the game we played.”

Alessandro Circati levels it for the CommBank @socceroos after some VAR confusion! 🔥His flick looping perfectly into the back of the net for Australia's first of the night, with replays proving that he was not offside! 💪Watch #AUSvBRA live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/P8il95HXlD

Bruno Guimaraes: Brazil ‘on new path’

Record five-time world champions Brazil have been criticised for their showing at the finals, which included falling behind in a draw with Morocco and conceding first against Japan in the last 32 before securing a last-gasp win.

The tournament was Ancelotti’s first as a national manager. The Italian this time gave a debut to 20-year-old goalkeeper Otavio following a 1-1 draw with Australia four days earlier in which Rayan equalised for the visitors in the 94th minute.

“It’s the beginning of a new journey for us,” said Guimaraes. “A lot of people want immediate results right away and we really understand the fans because they’re suffering and hurt, and so are we because of everything that’s been happening.

WHAT A STRIKE FROM CONNOR METCALFE! 🚀The hero from the CommBank @socceroos’ first 2026 FIFA World Cup match is at it again, rocketing Australia into the lead! 🔥Watch #AUSvBRA live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/PY554vAVRH

“The first game [against Australia] wasn’t good at all – nothing like what we were expecting. Today we came in with a new strategy.

“But beyond the system we play, whether it’s 4–3–3 or 4–2–4, we as players also have to take responsibility to perform better.

“In the first game, the pitch made things very difficult for us. Today the pitch was a bit better and we performed better and were able to keep the ball more.

“We also have to highlight that today we changed seven players from the last game, so it’s a team in development. We know we need to give a response.

“Anyone who loves the Brazilian national team will be happy with the result and the performance. It was good. It can be better, but it shows we’re on a good path – or so I hope.”

Brazil are off to a lightning quick start in Brisbane ⚡️🇧🇷Vanderson gets his first goal for the Seleção, picking out the top corner inside three minutes 🎯Watch #AUSvBRA live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/8ggyrsTV7P

Brazil team vs Australia

Danilo Santos, Guimaraes, Raphinha and Vinicius Junior were the only retained players in Brazil’s line-up from the draw four days earlier.

Santos midfielder Gabriel Bontempo also made his debut and PSV winger Mauro Junior was given a full bow, having come off the bench in the first game against Australia.

Brazil: Otavio, Vanderson, Jair Cunha, Gabriel Magalhaes, Mauro Junior, Gabriel Bontemp, Bruno Guimaraes, Danilo Santos, Rayan, Raphinha, Vinicius Junior

Substitutes: Hugo Souza, Marquinhos, Douglas Santos, Endrick, Willian Estevao, Matheuzinho, Vitor Reis, Arthur Dias, Breno Bidon, Douglas Luiz, Pedro, Matheus Martinelli, Andrey Santos, Samuel Lino, Pedro Morisco

articles.title: Wayne Rooney rubbishes claims Manchester United should be handed 2012 winners’ medals and says ‘I wouldn’t want one’
articles.summary: Manchester City could be stripped of the crown despite pipping Manchester United in 2012 but Wayne Rooney does not want to be given a medal
articles.content:
Wayne Rooney rubbishes claims Manchester United should be handed 2012 winners’ medals and says ‘I wouldn’t want one’

Manchester City could be stripped of the crown despite pipping Manchester United in 2012 but Wayne Rooney does not want to be given a medal

Last Update:

Wayne Rooney wouldn’t want a Premier League winners’ medal from 2012 if Manchester City were stripped of the title, insisting Manchester United didn’t deserve to finish above their crosstown rivals.

United thought they had wrapped the crown up 14 years ago after their 1-0 win at Sunderland on the final day. City had to beat QPR to pip them but were 2-1 down when the whistle went at the Stadium of Light. The United players were poised to celebrate only for last-gasp goals from Edin Dzeko and, memorably, Sergio Aguero to spark pandemonium at the Etihad.

The subsequent claim that City have broken 114 financial rules has led to calls for them to lose all the titles accrued over the affected period, including the 2012 title.

That could mean United are gifted another Premier League trophy and Rooney’s former team-mates Rio Ferdinand and David De Gea have both suggested it is right that their personal medal hauls are increased.

Rooney – United didn’t deserve to win the league

But Rooney is adamant the City players should not be punished for alleged indiscretions at board level.

Speaking on Stick To United, he said: “I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal… I wouldn’t really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I’m being honest.

“I don’t think we deserve it, we didn’t do enough that season to win the league. I think we were six or seven points clear with four or five games to go and we threw it away.

“I’ve seen everything that has come out over the past few days and listening to people and I was putting myself in a Man City player’s shoes… they’re players, they’re doing everything they can to try and win the Premier League title and in their mind they have done it, those players have no understanding of what is going on above them, if that happened to me… I would be absolutely devastated.

“It might happen, they might take them [medals] away, but I wouldn’t want it [a medal] because I don’t think as a team we deserved it that year because obviously we didn’t finish first.”

I’m happy with my five titles – Rooney

The Premier League have yet to confirm City have been found guilty – the story was broken by the Athletic last Friday – and there is no clarity on the sanctions the club could face.

Rooney added: “I see team-mates saying ‘I want a medal’, I’m happy with the five I’ve won. I wouldn’t want this one. Should they get it stripped for what the owners have done? Yeah maybe, but I wouldn’t feel comfortable accepting it.”

articles.content:
Nations League results: Italy thrash Turkey as France win late in Belgium

Four of the eight Nations League games featured at least four goals

Last Update:

New Italy head coach Roberto Mancini earned the first win of his second spell in charge with the help of three first-half goals by the Azzurri against Turkey on Nations League Matchday 2 in Bursa.

The 4-1 victory gave Mancini’s side their first points of their campaign following their 2-0 home defeat on Friday to Belgium, who were also in action on Monday.

New Red Devils head coach Mark van Bommel suffered a late defeat to France, who remained perfect under new boss Zinedine Zidane following their 1-0 win in Turkey four days earlier.

There were also six matches elsewhere across Europe in the competition, including a goal for Arsenal’s Viktor Gyokeres as Sweden won.

Turkey vs Italy: Flying start helps visitors win

Alessandro Bastoni’s strike from Matteo Ruggeri’s corner, Davide Frattesi’s tap-in and Michael Kayode’s drive put Italy 3-0 ahead after 28 minutes and Turkey firmly on course for consecutive defeats following that loss against Les Bleus.

Baris Alper Yilmaz pulled one back with an arrowed finish but Italy restored their three-goal cushion soon afterwards, Pio Esposito nodding in after Sandro Tonali had shot against a post.

“We had a really good approach on a difficult pitch that was muddy,” Mancini told Sky Sport Italia, describing himself as “satisfied”.

“I am very happy for these lads, as they deserve it.”

Belgium vs France: Olise goal gives Zidane win

Bayern Munich wideman Michael Olise settled an absorbing contest in sensational style in the 88th minute, bringing the ball down inside his own half 11 minutes after coming on and charging to the edge of Belgium’s penalty area before unleashing a precise winner.

Paris Saint-Germain and France winger Desire Doue went closest during the first half, firing a shot against the crossbar following a flourish of superb footwork inside the box to evade a clutch of markers.

“We were brave,” Zidane told TF1. “We were not afraid to get into the opposition half, even if we dropped the tempo a bit in the second half.

“We dominated over the course of the match and fully deserved it.”

Nations League results: September 28 2026

Elsewhere in the Nations League on Monday, Northern Ireland drew 0-0 at home to Hungary in one of four matches in Group B.

Benjamin Nygren put Sweden ahead in Solna, where Sebastian Szymanski drew Poland level by half-time before second-half goals from Yasin Ayari and Gyokeres gave the hosts a 3-1 victory.

Georgia and Ukraine shared a 0-0 draw in Tbilisi and there were six goals in Bucharest, where Armin Gigovic and TarikMuharemovic put Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 ahead inside the first 20 minutes against Romania.

Daniel Birligea replied but Haris Tabakovic and Ermin Mahmic gave the visitors a 4-1 lead, although Alexandru Cicaldau pulled one back.

In Group C, Montenegro prevailed in a five-goal thriller against Armenia in Yerevan, where Erik Piloyan’s own goal gave the visitors the lead.

Artur Serobyan equalised and Nikola Krstovic restored Montenegro’s advantage at half-time. Eduard Spertsyan then equalised during the second half and Aleksa Latkovic scored the 89th-minute winner.

Cyprus visited Latvia and had all five attempts on target between the teams but were held to a 0-0 draw.

articles.title: NFL: De’Von Achane suffers season-ending knee injury in major blow to Miami Dolphins
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane has torn his ACL.
articles.content:
NFL: De’Von Achane suffers season-ending knee injury in major blow to Miami Dolphins

Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane has torn his ACL.

Last Update:

De’Von Achane will miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a torn ACL during the Miami Dolphins‘ 24-10 defeat by the Kansas City Chiefs.

The running back sustained the injury on his third rushing attempt of Sunday’s game when he was tackled awkwardly by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman.

Achane was slow to get back to his feet and was eventually helped towards the blue medical tent under his own power. He spent several minutes being assessed before leaving the tent and heading to the locker room for further testing.

He was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley admitted after the match that the initial signs were concerning, although the full extent of the problem had not yet been established.

“To be very honest with you, it does not sound very optimistic at this moment,” Hafley said. “But I can’t give you any other details until I have them.”

Achane’s injury comes as Miami sit 0-3 following their loss to the Chiefs and leaves the Dolphins without the leading figure in their backfield.

The 25-year-old had rushed for 127 yards from 34 carries across Miami’s first three games of the season.

Achane’s injury comes after new contract

Achane’s season-ending injury is particularly significant given how much the Dolphins have relied on him since he entered the NFL.

Although the 5-foot-9, 195-pound back missed five games with a knee problem during his rookie season, he had remained relatively healthy since then.

He missed only two games combined during the past two seasons despite receiving 586 total touches across 2024 and 2025.

Miami made their long-term commitment to Achane clear in May by handing him a four-year, $64 million contract extension that runs through the 2030 season.

Now, the Dolphins must find a way to replace a player who has accounted for far more touches than any other current member of their roster over the past three years.
